facts.claim: Shifted-character keycodes are SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN: lvdesk folds Shift (and Caps) into the character before sending, so Shift+1 arrives as keycode 0x21 '!'; '!' '@' '#' '%' '^' '&' '*' '(' ')' '_' '+' '{' '}' ':' '"' '~' '|' '?' are not in LinuxKeycodeKeysyms and fall to UNKNOWN. Exceptions: '<' (0x3C) -> Linux 86 -> SDL_SCANCODE_NONUSBACKSLASH (wrong key), '$' (0x24) -> extended 0x1b2 -> UNKNOWN. Consequence: a key pressed unshifted and released while Shift is held (press '.', press Shift for run, release '.') arrives as '>' -> release dropped -> SDL_SCANCODE_PERIOD stays pressed in SDL2's keystate (stuck key). The same stuck-key mechanism exists in SDL 1.2 because its keystate is indexed by sym (SDLK_PERIOD vs SDLK_GREATER).

suspects.issue: Wire keycodes 1..7 (Return, BackSpace, Tab, Escape, Delete, Left, Up) sit below the min_keycode=8 xshim advertises, so SDL2's per-keycode table is never filled for them and their events are discarded as SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: SDL2 builds key_layout once over [min_keycode..max_keycode] (8..255) and indexes it per event; SDL_SendKeyboardKeyInternal drops UNKNOWN. SDL 1.2 translates per event by keysym and never looks at min_keycode, which is why prboom is fine and Chocolate Doom is not.
suspects.affected: Every SDL2 client (Chocolate Doom, OpenTyrian, sdl2keys): Escape/Enter/Backspace/Tab/Delete/Left/Up dead, Right/Down alive. Not SDL 1.2, not Xt.
suspects.evidence: /Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h:17-23; /Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/lvdesk/xshim.c:2564-2565; SDL_x11keyboard.c:302-325; SDL_x11video.h:126 + SDL_x11video.c:180; SDL_x11events.c:1150,1160; SDL_keyboard.c:824-826. Minimal server-side fix (our code only): move the seven codes out of 1..7 into the free C1 block (e.g. XLW_RETURN=133 .. XLW_UP=139) in xlite_wirekeys.h, leaving xlw_lo[1..7]=0 and extending xlw_hi; lvdesk.c:430-439 uses the XLW_ macros and xshim passes bytes, so both ends follow the header, and xlw_narrow/XKeysymToKeycode follow automatically. Alternative (protocol-illegal but works for SDL2's loop): advertise min keycode 1 at xshim.c:2564.

suspects.issue: Shift/Caps are folded into the wire keycode at the source, so XKeycodeToKeysym(kc,0) returns the SHIFTED keysym for shifted-character keycodes; SDL2 maps those to SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN and a release that crosses a Shift transition never matches its press (stuck key).
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: SDL2's LinuxKeycodeKeysyms only lists level-0 keysyms; '!'..'~' shifted forms fall to UNKNOWN. Pressing '.' (strafe) then holding Shift (run) and releasing '.' sends '>' whose release is dropped, so SDL2 (and SDL 1.2, keystate by sym) keeps '.' held. Also Shift+digit/punct produce no KEYDOWN at all (only TEXTINPUT), and '<' lands on NONUSBACKSLASH.
suspects.affected: SDL2 clients (key events for shifted punctuation, stuck keys), SDL 1.2 clients (SDLK_EXCLAIM instead of SDLK_1+KMOD_SHIFT; same stuck-key case). Xt/xcalc unaffected (uses xlw_widen directly).

SDL2 then gets key_layout['>']=SCANCODE_PERIOD and keymap[SCANCODE_PERIOD]='.' (X11_KeyCodeToUcs4 uses the same function), SDL 1.2 gets the standard SDLK_period+KMOD_SHIFT, and text input is unchanged.

Do lvdesk's 'input starved for N ms' lines during fullscreen games reflect kbd_poll being skipped while the game holds the evdev grab, and does the 'evdev overflow on mouse fd' lose key or button events that SDL2 would then count as stuck? Not answerable from the SDL2 side.

facts.claim: Device classification: kbd_scan opens every /dev/input/event0..31 and keeps any node whose EV_KEY bitmap has KEY_A (no other test); is_mouse requires REL_X AND BTN_LEFT AND NOT KEY_A; is_touch requires ABS_X + BTN_TOUCH and no REL_X. A composite node with both KEY_A and REL_X is therefore opened only as a keyboard and its motion is never read. Both scans EVIOCGRAB the fd (unless LVDESK_NO_GRAB=1) and dedupe by st_rdev.
facts.evidence: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:702-760 (kbd_scan, KEY_A test at 737-739), 8917-8935 (is_mouse), 8944-8960 (is_touch), 8962-9036 (mouse_scan), 681-699 (input_grab)

facts.claim: Synthetic devices: a mouse whose EVIOCGNAME starts with "uinject" is flagged mouse_raw and its REL deltas are applied verbatim (no acceleration); uinject creates "uinject-mouse" (EV_REL REL_X/Y/WHEEL, BTN_LEFT/RIGHT) and "uinject-kbd", so the injector is classified exactly like a real mouse/keyboard.
facts.evidence: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:9010-9028, 9205-9212; rootfs/uinject.c:51-77, 252-253

facts.claim: Rescans are inotify-driven: with the /dev/input watch open, input_rescan_due() is true only when scan_at==0 (set at start, on an inotify event, or on ENODEV/EBADF from a read); the 2 s timer is used only if inotify is unavailable. So the old 'UINJECT_SETTLE must beat the 2 s rescan' note no longer describes the code.

kbd_poll and mouse_poll are only called when poll() flags one of their fds (POLLIN|POLLERR|POLLHUP|POLLNVAL) or a rescan is due. Consequently the "input starved for N ms" line (gap since the previous kbd_poll, printed when >500 ms) measures time since the last KEYBOARD EVENT, not a loop stall: an idle keyboard through a whole mouse-only game session produces N ~= the session length. It is not evidence of starvation.
facts.evidence: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:929-955 (gap logic), 10372-10387 (rd_kbd/rd_mouse gating), comment at 9226-9236 acknowledging the same for the pointer

facts.claim: Evdev overflow path: SYN_DROPPED on a mouse fd increments mouse_dropped, prints "INPUT LOST - evdev overflow on mouse fd", discards the deltas/wheel/extra-button accumulated in that batch and clears ptr_pressed; the fd is kept open and reading continues. There is no EVIOCGKEY re-sync, so a button that was physically held across the drop is reported released and a later real release is a no-op. On keyboards the same event clears shift/ctrl/alt. The fd is only closed on ENODEV/EBADF.
facts.evidence: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:9190-9204 (mouse), 1060-1073 (keyboard), 9134-9143 and 977-982 (close on ENODEV)

facts.claim: Pointer accumulation: real-mouse REL deltas are summed per poll (rdx/rdy), scaled by a velocity curve computed from device timestamps (PTR_ACCEL_THRESHOLD/SLOPE/MAX, off with LVDESK_PTR_ACCEL=0), with sub-pixel carry; synthetic deltas are added verbatim; touch ABS_X/Y assign ptr_x/ptr_y directly. The position is then clamped to the LVGL display size, or to fs_w x fs_h when fs_active - so in fullscreen the pointer lives in MODE coordinates (0..fs_w-1, 0..fs_h-1).
facts.evidence: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:9083-9112 (w/h choice), 9205-9263 (accumulate), 9286-9333 (accel + clamp)

facts.claim: Hand-off to xshim: (1) GRAB PATH - if xshim_grab_top() (pointer grab's top-level, else the keyboard grab's) is non-zero, the pointer is confined to that top-level's rectangle (the whole mode when fs_active && g == fs_win, else the window's LVGL img area) and xshim_pointer(g, rx, ry, button, act) is called with top-level-relative coordinates: act 0 motion on every position change (button-independent), act 1/2 for Button1 edges, Button2/3 from btn_extra, wheel as Button4/5 press+release pairs. (2) NO-GRAB PATH - Button1 and motion go through LVGL's indev (mouse_read_cb -> xwin_ptr_cb, which is registered only for PRESSED/RELEASED/PRESS_LOST/PRESSING), so without a grab a windowed client receives MotionNotify only while Button1 is held; Button2/3/wheel go through xwin_send_button by hit-testing frames.
facts.evidence: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:9337-9410 (grab path), 9573-9593 (mouse_read_cb), 3977-3998 and 5221-5231 (xwin_ptr_cb + registration), 3847-3897 (xwin_send_button); lvdesk/xshim.c:8895-9001 (xshim_pointer)

facts.claim: Fullscreen differences, all keyed on fs_active: xwin_send_button returns 0 (no Button2/3/wheel to anything), mouse_read_cb forces LV_INDEV_STATE_RELEASED (no Button1/motion via LVGL), the desktop's META-key ungrab is disabled, the cursor is always hidden, win_set_focus refuses focus to any window other than fs_win or the grab holder, and the LVGL refresh timer's callback is swapped to a no-op. NET EFFECT: in fullscreen the ONLY pointer path into a client is the grab path; a fullscreen client that holds neither a pointer nor a keyboard grab receives no motion and no buttons, while keys still reach it via focus.

fs_win is resolved lazily on the first draw after the mode switch via xshim_mode_window(fs_w, fs_h), which scans res[] linearly and returns the LAST mapped top-level of the mode-switching client (vm_cli) that is >= the mode size, else a covering window, else the client's largest. Focus is then moved to the pointer-grab holder's top-level (or fs_win), latched by fs_focused. xwin_on_draw only calls fs_present when the drawn top-level id == fs_win.
facts.evidence: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:5875-5930; lvdesk/xshim.c:9218-9260

facts.claim: xshim_mode_window's 'last one created wins' ordering assumption is not guaranteed: res_new() takes the FIRST free slot, and res_free() returns slots, so after any earlier client has exited a later client's windows land in whatever slots are free, not in creation order.
facts.evidence: lvdesk/xshim.c:761-777 (res_new), 9231-9235 (comment 'res[] fills in creation order')

facts.claim: Warp handling: xshim's WarpPointer resolves dst; dst None or a non-window (including the root, since ROOT_ID 0x100 is a bare constant with no res entry) is treated as a RELATIVE move by (dx,dy); otherwise warp_cb(dst->buf->id, dst->ax+dx, dst->ay+dy) and, by default (XSHIM_WARPMOTION!=0), a synthesised MotionNotify at the destination. lvdesk's xwin_on_warp sets ptr_x/y = x,y when fs_active && top == fs_win, else looks the top up in xwins[] and requires an img; a top with no img is silently ignored. SDL 1.2's move_cursor_to() warps to SDL_Root, so it lands in the relative branch here.

facts.claim: XReparentWindow is a no-op stub in xlite (xlite_missing), and xshim has no core ReparentWindow (opcode 7) handler. Because create_aux_windows creates FSwindow BEFORE WMwindow and X11_CreateWindow resizes WMwindow to the mode size, xshim_mode_window's 'last fitting wins' picks WMwindow, which is also top_of(SDL_Window) - so drawing, the grab top and fs_win all agree on WMwindow and the SDL 1.2 fullscreen path works by coincidence of slot order.

suspects.issue: lvdesk's grab path sends MotionNotify only when the CLAMPED pointer position changes, and clamps to the grabbed area; motion at the edge is silently swallowed.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: Any grabbed client NOT in SDL's warp-recentre relative mode (SDL 1.2 with the cursor still visible, SDL2 with a plain SDL_SetWindowGrab and no relative mode, an Xt client with XtGrabPointer) sees the pointer stick at the window edge and receives no further deltas; combined with root_x==event_x it cannot compute relative motion either. Not what kills TyrQuake (the app ignores motion) but it is a real limitation of the confine implementation: a confined X server still reports motion with clamped coordinates and real X apps derive deltas from XI raw events, which do not exist here.

suspects.issue: WarpPointer with dst == root (or any window without a buffer) is silently ignored, and dst == None (relative) synthesises no MotionNotify.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: SDL 1.2's move_cursor_to() root warps during mode switch are dropped (harmless), but SDL2's X11_WarpMouseGlobal and any client that warps relative to root and then waits for the motion (XMaskEvent on PointerMotionMask, the same stall documented for SDL 1.2 at xshim.c:7245-7250) blocks until the next physical motion. SDL2's relative_mode_warp uses SDL_WarpMouseInWindow (window dst) so it is not hit today. Fix: treat a root/None dst like any other (update ptr through warp_cb, then synthesise motion via xshim_pointer on the top-level under the new position).

suspects.issue: GrabPointer ignores the request's event_mask, and a grab held by another client returns AlreadyGrabbed with no timeout or override; SDL 1.2 spins forever on that reply.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: Second-client difference: launching a second SDL 1.2 game while a stale grab exists (a client whose top-level is still mapped on a leaked fd - memory 'Grab outlives via a leaked fd') hangs the new game inside XGrabPointer with an SDL_Delay(100) loop, and every key goes to the stale holder via lvdesk's grab-first routing (kbd_key). grab_live() only releases when the window is unmapped/gone or the client fd closes. facts.claim: Pointer API answers: XQueryPointer performs NO round trip and always returns True with root=child=0, x=y=0, mask=0. XGetPointerControl returns 2/1/4; XChangePointerControl is accepted and ignored. XGrabPointer/XGrabKeyboard are real requests that wait for the reply status; XUngrabPointer/XUngrabKeyboard/XWarpPointer are fire-and-forget requests (WarpPointer 41). XDefineCursor is ChangeWindowAttributes(CWCursor); XCreatePixmapCursor is a real CreateCursor (93) whose all-zero mask the shim treats as 'hide the pointer'; XCreateFontCursor is just a fresh XID with nothing behind it; XFreeCursor is a no-op.

Event machinery: decode() fills device events fully (time/root/window/subwindow/x_root/y_root/x/y/state/same_screen, keycode kept as the raw wire byte), Enter/Leave, Expose, Map/Unmap, ConfigureNotify, ClientMessage; FocusIn/FocusOut/KeymapNotify/MappingNotify fall to the default arm (only xany.window set; mode/detail stay 0 = NotifyNormal/NotifyAncestor). XEventsQueued(QueuedAlready) never reads the transport; XPending = QueuedAfterFlush (non-blocking drain). XMaskEvent/XCheckMaskEvent/XCheckTypedEvent/XIfEvent/XCheckIfEvent/XWindowEvent take the first matching event from the middle of the queue and keep the rest. XPeekEvent blocks until something is queued. XSync is a GetInputFocus round trip (XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT skips the wait). XSelectInput = ChangeWindowAttributes(CWEventMask).

In XLITE-RING mode both XConnectionNumber() and the Xlib ConnectionNumber() macro (dpy->fd) return the server->client eventfd, because ring attach rewrites pub.fd. SDL 1.2's X11_Pending select()s on the macro value and SDL2's X11_WaitEventTimeout uses SDL_IOReady on it, so event wake-ups are not lost by the transport.

facts.claim: SDL 1.2 relative-mouse (recentering warp) mode requires ALL of: cursor hidden, this->input_grab != SDL_GRAB_OFF, and APPACTIVE|APPINPUTFOCUS|APPMOUSEFOCUS. The fullscreen grab issued by X11_EnterFullScreen is X11_GrabInputNoLock(input_grab|SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN) and does NOT set input_grab; only an application call to SDL_WM_GrabInput does. In non-relative mode MotionNotify is posted as absolute (x,y) and SDL clamps to the surface, so the view moves only until the pointer reaches an edge. The grab is XGrabPointer(SDL_Window, owner_events=True, event_mask=0, confine=SDL_Window) plus XGrabKeyboard(WMwindow).

facts.claim: SDL2 key-repeat handling: with detectable autorepeat refused, SDL2 pairs a KeyRelease with a following KeyPress of the same keycode within 2 ms via XPending + XCheckIfEvent; xlite implements both. lvdesk forwards evdev value 2 (autorepeat) to kbd_key as a press without a release, so SDL2 sees repeated KeyPress and flags repeat itself; SDL 1.2 uses XPending + XPeekEvent the same way. xshim stamps events with real ms times by default.

suspects.issue: SDL2 loses Escape, Return, BackSpace, Tab, Delete, Left and Up because their wire keycodes (1..7) sit below the advertised min_keycode (8) and SDL2 only builds key_layout[] for min..max.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: X11_InitKeyboard's fallback loop assigns key_layout[i] only for i in [8,255]; a KeyPress with detail 4 (Escape) indexes key_layout[4] = SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN and SDL_SendKeyboardKey returns without posting. Chocolate Doom's TranslateKey/GetTypedChar are scancode-based, so menus (Esc/Enter/Backspace) and Left/Up are dead while Right/Down/Home/End/PgUp/PgDn/F-keys/letters/modifiers still work - which reads as 'keyboard does not work properly at all'. SDL 1.2 is unaffected because X11_TranslateKeycode never consults min_keycode. Fix candidates (no app changes): (a) xshim send_setup min keycode 1 (lvdesk/xshim.c:2564); (b) xlite XDisplayKeycodes clamp *min to 1 (xlite_req.c:2023-2029) - sufficient for SDL2 on its own; (c) move XLW 1..7 into the unused C1 range 133-139 in the shared xlite_wirekeys.h (needs lvdesk+xlite rebuilt together). (a)+(b) is the smallest, protocol-tolerant change; xlite is the only client library talking to this server.
suspects.affected: Chocolate Doom, OpenTyrian, sdl2keys, tyr-quake (SDL2) - every SDL2 client. Not prboom/tiopex-quake/xcalc.

suspects.issue: Shift is folded into the wire keycode (uppercase/shifted-punctuation keycodes) instead of being carried only in state, so SDL 1.2 maps Shift+letter to a nonexistent SDLKey and any key released with a different Shift state than it was pressed with gets a different keycode.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: SDL 1.2: X11_TranslateKeycode -> XKeycodeToKeysym('W')=0x57 -> SDLKey 87, which is not in the SDLKey enum (gap between SDLK_AT=64 and SDLK_LEFTBRACKET=91), so run+forward (Shift held while pressing W) is a dead key in prboom and sdlquake; and 'w' pressed, Shift pressed, 'w' released delivers release 0x57 while SDL still holds SDLK_w pressed (stuck movement key). SDL2 normalises A-Z so letters survive, but digits/punctuation do not ('!' -> SCANCODE_UNKNOWN), so Shift+1 is dead and '1' can stick. Real X sends the unshifted keycode plus ShiftMask and lets XLookupString/XKeycodeToKeysym(kc,1) apply shift. Fix lives in lvdesk (send keymap[code][0], keep shift in xkey_mods) plus xlite (XLookupString applies Shift/Caps via a US-ASCII shift table; XKeycodeToKeysym honours index 1; XGetKeyboardMapping per_code=2). xshim only forwards sym and needs no change.
suspects.affected: prboom, tiopex-quake, sdlquake, any SDL 1.2 client (dead Shift+letter, stuck keys); SDL2 clients for shifted digits/punctuation; xcalc/xtlite unaffected in practice (Xt matches keysyms from XLookupString).

suspects.issue: XReparentWindow is a stub, so SDL 1.2's fullscreen structure is never what SDL believes: SDL_Window stays a child of WMwindow while FSwindow (override-redirect, panel-sized, XMapRaised+XRaiseWindow, StructureNotifyMask only) is a separate top-level.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: xshim honours the pointer grab only when the grab window's top-level is the top-level under the pointer (top_of(g)==top). If lvdesk ever puts FSwindow under the pointer, motion hit-tests FSwindow, nothing there selects PointerMotionMask, send_device_event drops the event and the grabbed SDL_Window sees no motion or buttons. It evidently works for prboom today, so lvdesk must keep WMwindow on top or ignore FSwindow, but that is undocumented and fragile; the same stub also makes X11_LeaveFullScreen a partial no-op. A real ReparentWindow (opcode 7) in xlite + xshim would make the layout match SDL's model.

facts.claim: xshim delivers a key to the window the pointer was last in inside the focused top-level (or the keyboard-grab window), propagating up to the first ancestor that selected KeyPress; SDL 1.2's XGrabKeyboard is on WMwindow, so keys landing on the WM window ('KeyPress reached the WM window') is the normal SDL 1.2 routing. Events carry a real monotonic ms timestamp by default, which the 2 ms autorepeat filters in both SDLs need.
facts.evidence: lvdesk/xshim.c:9012-9046 (xshim_key routing), :8823-8878 (send_device_event propagation and evtime stamp), :7198-7213 (GrabKeyboard); sdl-1.2.15 SDL_x11wm.c:364-365 (XGrabKeyboard(WMwindow)); SDL_x11events.c:308-324 (SDL 1.2 X11_KeyRepeat <2 ms); sdl2 SDL_x11events.c:159-182 (X11_KeyRepeatCheckIfEvent <2).

facts.claim: lvdesk forwards kernel autorepeat (value 2) as repeated KeyPress events without intervening KeyRelease, and sends a KeyRelease for every real release (to the grab top or the focused window), so SDL's 'release followed by press within 2 ms' repeat heuristic is not exercised and held keys stay held in both SDL 1.2 and SDL2.
facts.evidence: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:1004-1035 (value==2 handling, bounded runaway repeat), :1156-1176 (release -> xshim_key(..., 0, ...)), :1195 (press or repeat -> kbd_key), :841-849 (kbd_key -> xshim_key press when a grab is live).

facts.claim: The 'input starved for N ms' line in lvdesk.log is the gap between successive kbd_poll() calls, and kbd_poll() is only called when a keyboard fd is readable or a rescan is due. During a game with no key presses the first key press after N ms therefore prints N ~= the session length. lvdesk's own comment states this metric 'cannot tell a quiet moment from a late one'. It is not evidence that input was lost.
facts.evidence: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:929-955 (kbd_poll computes gap since kbd_last_poll_ms and prints if >500 ms), :10344-10387 (rd_kbd set only from poll() revents on keyboard fds or input_rescan_due; kbd_poll called only if rd_kbd), :9226-9231 (comment on the metric).

facts.claim: 'INPUT LOST - evdev overflow on mouse fd' is a real evdev ring overflow (EV_SYN/SYN_DROPPED path) reported by lvdesk's mouse_poll; lvdesk then resets modifier state. It is distinct from the starvation line.
facts.evidence: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:9173-9195 (overflow detection and message in mouse_poll), :1063-1075 (same in kbd_poll, resets shift/ctrl/alt).

facts.claim: Nothing in the code path 'declares the presence of a mouse' to clients. The core X protocol has no such notion; SDL 1.2 never asks; SDL2 only enumerates devices through XInput2, which xshim reports absent. lvdesk decides locally that an evdev node is a mouse when it has REL_X and BTN_LEFT and no KEY_A, which is why the 8bitdo if0 (BTN_LEFT) is opened as a mouse. Under a pointer grab lvdesk sends absolute coordinates clamped to the grab window (and confine_to), with motion reported regardless of button state.
facts.evidence: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:8920-8935 (is_mouse), :9346-9405 (grab routing: clamp to window area, xshim_pointer motion/press/release/wheel); lvdesk/xshim.c:8909-8930 (grab_win routing, owner_events honoured); sdl2 SDL_x11xinput2.c:132-135.

facts.claim: xlite's XQueryPointer never goes to the wire and returns root=0, coordinates 0,0 and mask 0, although xshim implements a correct QueryPointer reply (root-relative pointer position and button state). SDL2's X11_ReconcileKeyboardState uses the mask only for Caps/Num/Scroll lock, and xlite's XQueryKeymap returns all-zero, so ReconcileKeyboardState (run at init and on every FocusIn) releases any key SDL believes is held. xshim sends FocusIn/FocusOut only when lvdesk's focused top-level changes.
facts.evidence: xlite/xlite_req.c:3184-3196 (XQueryPointer zeros, no request), :3200-3206 (XQueryKeymap zeros); lvdesk/xshim.c:7064-7082 (QueryPointer reply with ptr_root_x/y and ptr_btn_state); sdl2 SDL_x11events.c:405-450 (X11_ReconcileKeyboardState), :452-458 (DispatchFocusIn -> ReconcileKeyboardState); lvdesk/xshim.c:9171-9209 (send_focus / xshim_focus only on change); lvdesk/lvdesk.c:2794-2804 (xshim_focus called from window focus change).

facts.claim: xcalc's keyboard and buttons go through xtlite's own dispatcher: it widens the wire keycode with xlw_widen directly and matches the parsed translation table by keysym and Shift/Control state; it never consults XDisplayKeycodes, so wire keycodes 1-7 are fine for Xt apps. Keys go to the XtSetKeyboardFocus target or propagate to the parent.
facts.evidence: xtlite/xtlite.c:958-991 (dispatch: detail = xlw_widen(ev->xkey.keycode), mods = state & (ControlMask|ShiftMask)), :1331-1350 (main loop: ButtonPress/Release -> dispatch, KeyPress -> kbd_focus target), :541-542 (event mask selected: ButtonPress/Release, KeyPress, Enter/Leave).

facts.claim: SDL 1.2 and SDL2 are both built with dynamic X11 loading of libX11.so.6 (our xlite), and SDL2 additionally dlopens libXext/libXcursor/libXi/libXfixes/libXrandr, all of which exist on the target as the real X.Org libraries (not our shims).

suspects.issue: xshim advertises min keycode 8 in the connection setup while the wire keyboard contract uses keycodes 1-7 for Return, BackSpace, Tab, Escape, Delete, Left and Up. SDL2 builds its keycode->scancode table only from min_keycode upward, so those seven keys are SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN in every SDL2 client.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: Chocolate Doom translates by scancode and drops key 0: Enter/Escape do nothing in menus, Up/Left (forward/turn-left) are dead in game, Backspace/Tab/Delete dead, while Right/Down/letters/Ctrl/Alt/Shift/F-keys work - which reads as 'keyboard does not work properly at all'. prboom and tiopex (SDL 1.2) are immune because SDL 1.2 calls XKeycodeToKeysym per event and never consults XDisplayKeycodes. Fix in our code only: either change lvdesk/xshim.c:2564 to advertise min keycode 1 (nothing but xlite reads it - xlite/xlite.c:773, xlite_req.c:2023-2028 - and SDL2's fingerprint arithmetic tolerates it), or move XLW_RETURN..XLW_UP to the unused C1 range 133-139 in xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h (both ends include the header; lvdesk and xlite must be rebuilt together and rootfs/sdl2keys + sdlkeys re-run). The first is a one-line change that leaves the wire untouched.
suspects.affected: Chocolate Doom (SDL2), tyr-quake 0.71 (SDL2 build), rootfs/sdl2keys, any future SDL2 client. Not prboom, not tiopex-quake, not OpenTyrian (all SDL 1.2), not xcalc (xtlite uses xlw_widen directly).
suspects.evidence: lvdesk/xshim.c:2564-2565; xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h:17-23; lvdesk/lvdesk.c:430-439; sdl2-2.32.10/src/video/x11/SDL_x11keyboard.c:227,302-325; SDL_x11video.h:126; SDL_x11events.c:1150,1160; chocolate-doom-3.1.1/src/i_input.c:105-131,252-259; sdl2 src/events/SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:63,76,77,90,165-173 (keysyms present, so only the range gate fails).

suspects.issue: tiopex-quake (the SDL 1.2 'TyrQuake' being run) contains no mouse code whatsoever and never calls SDL_WM_GrabInput; the observed absence of recentering warps and of view turning is the application, not xlite/xshim/lvdesk.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: IN_Init sets mouse_avail=0, IN_Move returns at once, and Sys_SendKeyEvents has no SDL_MOUSEMOTION/SDL_MOUSEBUTTON cases, so motion and buttons are generated by SDL 1.2 (absolute mode, since input_grab stays OFF) and discarded unread. No change to our stack can make this binary turn the view. The SDL2 TyrQuake 0.71 build (rootfs/tyr-quake, from tyrquake-0.71/common/in_sdl.c) is the only Quake here with mouse code, and it would in turn hit the min-keycode-8 defect above for Escape/Enter/Up/Left.
suspects.affected: tiopex-quake only (mouse). Keyboard in tiopex works via SDLK keysyms.
suspects.evidence: tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/vid_sdl.c:633-651, :224-630; rootfs/build-tiopex.sh:14-17; artifacts/quake/td-rate48k-221611/run.sh; sdl-1.2.15 SDL_x11mouse.c:246-268; src/video/SDL_video.c:1832-1863.

suspects.issue: lvdesk folds Shift/Caps into the wire keycode ('A' = 0x41 for Shift+a) and xlite's XLookupString/XkbLookupKeySym assume that; real X servers send the unshifted keycode plus ShiftMask and let the client fold. SDL 1.2 maps Latin-1 keysyms verbatim and has no SDLKey for 0x41-0x5A.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: In SDL 1.2 apps, any letter pressed with Shift held arrives as an unknown SDLKey (tiopex: K_UNKNOWN; prboom: rc=65..90 which no default binding uses; OpenTyrian: keysactive[65]) so Shift+WASD-style 'run while moving' loses the movement key, and if Shift is released first the release comes as the lowercase keysym and SDL 1.2's keystate keeps the uppercase entry pressed (stuck key). Same for Shift+digit -> punctuation keysyms. SDL2 is unaffected (lowercase normalisation before the scancode lookup). A fix must change both ends together: lvdesk sends the unshifted character with ShiftMask, xlite's XLookupString applies Shift/Caps itself (xlite_key.c:184-208) and XkbLookupKeySym stops claiming Shift is consumed (xlite_key.c:486-496); xfiles and the terminal path must be re-tested.
suspects.affected: prboom, tiopex-quake, OpenTyrian (all SDL 1.2) for Shift+letter/digit combinations; not SDL2 apps; xtlite matches keysym+ShiftMask exactly as sent so xcalc is unaffected.
suspects.evidence: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:474-481, :486-488; xlite/xlite_key.c:194-201, :483-495; sdl-1.2.15 SDL_x11events.c:1141-1142; tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/vid_sdl.c:373-450; sdl2 src/events/SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:402-404.

suspects.issue: xlite's XQueryPointer answers from constants (root 0, 0,0, mask 0) without asking xshim, although xshim implements a correct reply; XQueryKeymap answers all-zero.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: SDL2's X11_ReconcileKeyboardState (init and every FocusIn) trusts XQueryKeymap and releases every key SDL believes held, so a key held across a lvdesk focus change is dropped; the zero modifier mask also clears Caps/Num lock state. SDL2's SDL_GetGlobalMouseState and any client that positions popups from XQueryPointer get 0,0. Low frequency here because xshim emits FocusIn only on a real focus change, but it is a latent 'held key released' bug for SDL2 apps and a wrong answer for every Xlib client. Fix: make XQueryPointer send opcode 38 and parse xshim's reply (xshim.c:7064-7082), and have XQueryKeymap ask (xshim would need to implement opcode 44 from lvdesk's key state) or at least report the modifier keys lvdesk knows are held.
suspects.affected: Chocolate Doom and other SDL2 clients on focus changes; any client using XQueryPointer for placement.
suspects.evidence: xlite/xlite_req.c:3184-3206; lvdesk/xshim.c:7064-7082, :9171-9209; sdl2 SDL_x11events.c:405-458.

suspects.issue: SDL2 relative mouse in Chocolate Doom depends entirely on xshim's synthesised warp MotionNotify landing exactly at the SDL window's centre in that window's coordinates; xshim computes the synthetic event as dst->ax+dx, dst->ay+dy then hit-tests, and lvdesk's xwin_on_warp resolves the pointer into the top-level's image area.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: If the synthetic motion arrives at any coordinate other than (w/2, h/2) of the SDL window (e.g. a child window under the pointer, a window origin offset, or motion compression folding it), SDL2 treats it as user motion, warps again, and every real delta is measured from a stale last_x - the view drifts or spins. Not confirmed broken (the SDL 1.2 path with the same mechanism works for prboom), but SDL2's warp mode is stricter: it also gates the warp on SDL_WINDOW_INPUT_FOCUS, which requires xshim's FocusIn to have reached SDL2's window (sent only when lvdesk changes its focused top-level). Needs a board test with sdl2keys once the keycode fix lands.
suspects.affected: Chocolate Doom, tyr-quake 0.71 (SDL2). prboom (SDL 1.2) tolerates a fudge zone of 8 px.
suspects.evidence: lvdesk/xshim.c:7221-7275; lvdesk/lvdesk.c:4978-5010; sdl2 src/events/SDL_mouse.c:558-577, :1132-1180; sdl-1.2.15 SDL_x11events.c:333-372 (MOUSE_FUDGE_FACTOR 8); lvdesk/xshim.c:9171-9209.

suspects.issue: SDL2 dlopens the real X.Org libXcursor/libXi/libXfixes/libXrandr from the target, which are linked for X.Org's libX11 internals, not xlite.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: Not an input defect as read: X11_InitXinput2 returns before calling into libXi because xshim says XInputExtension is absent, and relative mode falls back to warping. But libXcursor is used by SDL2's default/system cursor creation (X11_CreateDefaultCursor at SDL_x11mouse.c:478) and any call there that reaches an Xlib internal xlite does not export would fail or crash at startup; the trace showed XDefineCursor requests, so at least the cursor path completes. Flagged so nobody chases a mouse bug into libXi.
suspects.affected: SDL2 clients only.
suspects.evidence: sdl2-2.32.10/include/SDL_config.h:397-412; sdl2 SDL_x11xinput2.c:132-135; SDL_x11mouse.c:464-479; target /usr/lib listing.

Harmless, but it would confirm the trace is chronological.

The first is recommended for the fix pass; the second is the durable one.

Whether Shift folding (lvdesk.c:474-481) should be reversed to X semantics (unshifted keycode + ShiftMask) now that SDL 1.2 apps are the majority; it requires xlite's XLookupString/XkbLookupKeySym to apply Shift themselves and re-validation of xfiles and the terminal keyseq path (lvdesk.c:860, 905).

facts.claim: SDL 1.2 creates three X windows: FSwindow (override-redirect, selects only StructureNotifyMask), WMwindow (selects FocusChange|KeyPress|KeyRelease|PropertyChange|StructureNotify|KeymapState) and SDL_Window, a CHILD of WMwindow that selects EnterWindow|LeaveWindow|ButtonPress|ButtonRelease|PointerMotion|Exposure. Keys therefore arrive on WMwindow and pointer events on SDL_Window.
facts.evidence: /src/build/buildroot/build/sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11video.c:347-359 (FSwindow), :387-405 (WMwindow, app_event_mask), :1051-1061 (SDL_Window child of WMwindow + XSelectInput)

facts.claim: The pointer grab SDL issues is XGrabPointer(SDL_Window, owner_events=True, event_mask=0, Async, Async, confine_to=SDL_Window, cursor=None); the keyboard grab is on WMwindow. The trace's 'XGrabPointer(FSwindow ... confine=FSwindow)' label is therefore a mislabel: SDL never grabs FSwindow, the id in the trace is SDL_Window.
facts.evidence: SDL_x11wm.c:352-354 (XGrabPointer args), :364-365 (XGrabKeyboard WMwindow); xlite trace prints only the raw ids: /Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/xlite/xlite_req.c:2345-2349

facts.claim: Fullscreen entry (X11_EnterFullScreen) does: GrabInput(OFF) [XUngrabPointer+XUngrabKeyboard], XMapRaised(FSwindow), X11_ResizeFullScreen -> XWarpPointer(root, x,y) twice, XMoveResizeWindow(FSwindow), XWarpPointer(root, real_w/2, real_h/2), XReparentWindow(SDL_Window -> FSwindow), then GrabInput(input_grab|SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN) -> XUngrabPointer, XGrabPointer(SDL_Window), XGrabKeyboard(WMwindow). This is exactly the 'XWarpPointer -> root 0,0, XUngrabPointer, XGrabPointer -> 0' prefix seen in BOTH traces.
facts.evidence: SDL_x11modes.c:1002 (GrabInput OFF), :1021 (XMapRaised), :950-970 (move_cursor_to x3 at :952,:954,:963; XReparentWindow :968), :1067 (grab with SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN); SDL_x11wm.c:342-345 (ungrab first when fullscreen), :338-340 (OFF path)

facts.claim: XReparentWindow is a generated no-op stub in xlite (sends nothing, returns 0), so on this desktop SDL_Window is NEVER moved into FSwindow: it stays a child of WMwindow. The fullscreen picture works only because lvdesk's xshim_mode_window() picks the LAST-created mapped top-level of the mode-switching client that fits the mode, which is WMwindow (created after FSwindow) - and hit_test from WMwindow reaches SDL_Window at 0,0.
facts.evidence: /Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/xlite/stubs.c:610-615; /Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/lvdesk/xshim.c:9218-9260 (fits/covering/last-wins rule), :761-777 (res_new takes the first free slot), :8778-8805 (hit_test)

facts.claim: Relative (mouse-look) mode is entered by X11_CheckMouseModeNoLock only when ALL of: cursor hidden (!(SDL_cursorstate & CURSOR_VISIBLE)), this->input_grab != SDL_GRAB_OFF, and SDL_GetAppState() has APPACTIVE|APPINPUTFOCUS|APPMOUSEFOCUS. It first tries DGA mouse (X11_EnableDGAMouse), which needs the XFree86-DGA extension; xshim's QueryExtension only knows RENDER, XFree86-VidModeExtension, RANDR and MIT-SHM, so DGA is absent and the XWarpPointer path is used. The implicit fullscreen grab passes input_grab|SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN to X11_GrabInputNoLock WITHOUT changing this->input_grab; only SDL_WM_GrabInput changes it.
facts.evidence: SDL_x11mouse.c:227-282 (conditions :247-250, DGA :252-253, mouse_relative=1 :267); SDL_x11dga.c:55-60 (XF86DGAQueryExtension gate); xshim.c:6132-6190 (QueryExtension cases :6142,:6174,:6180,:6186); SDL_x11modes.c:1067; SDL_video.c:1871-1900 (SDL_WM_GrabInput)

facts.claim: X11_WarpedMotion posts the delta from mouse_last on every MotionNotify, and only when the pointer is within MOUSE_FUDGE_FACTOR (8 px) of the surface edge does it drain queued MotionNotify, XWarpPointer(SDL_Window, w/2, h/2) and block in XMaskEvent(PointerMotionMask) for up to 10 events until one lands within 8 px of the centre. xlite's XMaskEvent takes the first matching queued event non-destructively (keys typed while waiting are kept), and xshim synthesises the warp's MotionNotify at the exact destination (XSHIM_WARPMOTION default on).
facts.evidence: SDL_x11events.c:331-392; /Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/xlite/xlite.c:1176-1208 (queue_take), :1220-1252 (take_wait), :1326-1330 (XMaskEvent); xshim.c:7221-7278 (WarpPointer: warp_cb + xshim_pointer synth at :7271-7277)

facts.claim: xlite prints an XWarpPointer trace line only for every 50th call (n++ % 50 == 0), so 'NO recentering warps ever' in a trace only proves fewer than 50 warps happened; 'XWarpPointer -> root 0,0' is warp #1 (the first move_cursor_to of fullscreen entry) and the next line can only appear at #51.
facts.evidence: xlite_req.c:2405-2411

facts.claim: tiopex-quake is built from tyrquake/sdlquake-master (sdlquake's MIPS-handheld SDL 1.2 glue, vid_sdl.c), and that glue has NO mouse support at all: IN_Init sets mouse_avail = 0, IN_Move returns immediately, no source file handles SDL_MOUSEMOTION/SDL_MOUSEBUTTONDOWN/SDL_GetRelativeMouseState, and SDL_WM_GrabInput is never called. It does call SDL_ShowCursor(0) after SDL_SetVideoMode(w,h,8,flags). So input_grab stays SDL_GRAB_OFF, mouse_relative is never set (no recentering warps - matches the trace), and even absolute motion would be discarded by the game. This is the whole explanation of 'TyrQuake mouse: nothing'.
facts.evidence: /Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/rootfs/build-tiopex.sh:1-14 (SRC=tyrquake/sdlquake-master, file list includes source/vid_sdl.c, no in_*.c); /Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/vid_sdl.c:104-115 (flags/SDL_SetVideoMode), :145 (SDL_ShowCursor(0)), :633-651 (IN_Init/IN_Move), :36-37 (mouse_avail/mouse_x unused); grep -l of SDL_MOUSEMOTION|SDL_MOUSEBUTTONDOWN|SDL_GetRelativeMouseState|SDL_WM_GrabInput over tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/*.c matches no file

That explicit grab is the 'XUngrabPointer, XGrabPointer' pair AFTER the two XDefineCursor lines in its trace, and it is what makes input_grab != OFF so mouse_relative turns on and the recentering warps appear.

No xlite/xshim answer is needed to produce the tiopex trace; it is produced by the app.

facts.claim: SDL 1.2 drops the implicit fullscreen grab by itself: any FocusIn queues switch_waiting=FULLSCREEN with a 1500 ms timer, and when it fires X11_PumpEvents calls X11_GrabInputNoLock(this, this->input_grab) - which for an app with input_grab == SDL_GRAB_OFF is XUngrabPointer+XUngrabKeyboard, and xshim then clears grab_win. Any FocusOut queues LeaveFullScreen after 200 ms (the historical 'prboom left fullscreen when the weapon was fired').
facts.evidence: SDL_x11events.c:465-479 (FocusIn), :483-497 (FocusOut), :952-982 (switch handling; :976-980 GrabInputNoLock with input_grab or OFF); SDL_x11wm.c:338-340; xshim.c:7190-7196 (UngrabPointer clears grab); lvdesk.c:3852-3862 (history)

facts.claim: lvdesk delivers pointer input to a fullscreen client ONLY through a live pointer grab: mouse_poll routes motion/buttons to xshim_grab_top() (requiring g == fs_win or an xwins entry with an image); without a grab, xwin_send_button returns 0 when fs_active and the LVGL indev is told the button is up unless (!grab && !fs_active). So an SDL 1.2 fullscreen app that relies on SDL's implicit fullscreen grab (never calls SDL_WM_GrabInput) loses all mouse input 1.5 s after the first FocusIn lvdesk sends it.
facts.evidence: lvdesk.c:9346-9408 (grab routing, 'have' gate :9355-9366), :3864-3865 (fullscreen: no button hit-test), :9591 (indev state), :2794-2804 and :5895-5924 and :5132-5133 (xshim_focus callers), xshim.c:9192-9206 (xshim_focus sends FocusOut/FocusIn)

facts.claim: SDL2 keyboard (Chocolate Doom, OpenTyrian): X11_InitKeyboard's fingerprint match fails here (XKeysymToKeycode(XK_Home)-min_keycode = 10-8 = 2 etc.), so it takes the fallback and builds key_layout[i] only for i = min_keycode..max_keycode; xshim's setup reply advertises min_keycode 8, max 255. xlite/lvdesk wire keycodes for Return(1), BackSpace(2), Tab(3), Escape(4), Delete(5), Left(6), Up(7) are BELOW 8, so key_layout[1..7] stays SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN and SDL_SendKeyboardKey is called with SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN for those keys. Chocolate Doom's TranslateKey maps by scancode -> scancode_translate_table[0] -> nothing. Keycodes >= 8 (Right, Down, Home, End, PgUp/Dn, Insert, KP_Enter, F1-F12, Shift, Ctrl at 8-31; Caps/Alt/Super at 128-132; letters/digits/space) go through XKeycodeToKeysym -> xlw_widen -> SDL_GetScancodeFromKeySym and work.
facts.evidence: /src/build/buildroot/build/sdl2-2.32.10/src/video/x11/SDL_x11keyboard.c:224-260 (fingerprint), :302-325 (fallback loop from min_keycode), :75-84; xshim.c:2564-2565 (min 8 / max 255); xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h:17-31,41-44,55-59; xlite/xlite_key.c:100-105 (XKeycodeToKeysym = xlw_widen), :506-511 (XKeysymToKeycode = xlw_narrow); SDL_x11events.c:1106-1162 (SDL_SendKeyboardKey(key_layout[keycode]) :1150,:1160); sdl2 src/events/SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:390-436; chocolate-doom-3.1.1/src/i_input.c:105-134

facts.claim: lvdesk sends the SHIFTED character as the wire keycode (keymap[code][shift]) so Shift+a arrives as keycode 65 'A' and Shift+1 as 33 '!'. SDL 1.2's X11_TranslateKeycode maps Latin-1 keysyms as key = xsym & 0xFF, giving SDLKey 65 (not SDLK_a=97; 65-90 are not valid SDLKeys) - tiopex's keysym switch and prboom's I_TranslateKey then see an unknown key for every shifted letter/symbol. SDL2 normalises 0x41-0x5A to lowercase so shifted LETTERS work, but shifted punctuation keycodes (33..64 range like '!' '@' '#') have no entry in LinuxKeycodeKeysyms and get SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN at key_layout build time.
facts.evidence: lvdesk.c:425-482 (xkey_sym: :474 keymap[code][shift], :477-480 caps); SDL_x11events.c:1119-1143 (Latin-1: key = xsym & 0xFF); SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:402-404 (uppercase normalisation), :411-425 (table match)

facts.claim: SDL2 relative mouse mode cannot use XInput2 here (xshim does not advertise XInputExtension, xlite exports no XIQueryVersion), so SDL_SetRelativeMouseMode falls back to warp mode: every non-centre MotionNotify triggers X11_WarpMouse -> XWarpPointer(window, w/2, h/2); xshim synthesises the MotionNotify at the centre and SDL2 recognises it as its own warp. This path is consistent with Chocolate Doom's mouse not being reported broken.
facts.evidence: SDL_x11mouse.c:381-384 (needs Xinput2), :361-373 (X11_WarpMouse); SDL_x11xinput2.c:132-143; sdl2 src/events/SDL_mouse.c:1132-1170 (fallback :1146-1152), :558-577 (centre recognition); xlite/libX11-exports.txt has XQueryExtension (line 320) but no XIQueryVersion; xshim.c:6132-6190

facts.claim: 'lvdesk: input starved for N ms' is NOT starvation when N spans the whole game: kbd_last_poll_ms is only updated inside kbd_poll, and kbd_poll runs only when a keyboard fd is readable or a device rescan is due; rescans are now inotify-driven rather than on a 2 s timer, so an untouched keyboard for N ms prints 'starved for N ms' at the next key. The code comment itself says the gap 'cannot tell a quiet moment from a late one'.
facts.evidence: lvdesk.c:929-957 (gap measured in kbd_poll), :10361-10362 and :10382 and :10387 (when kbd_poll runs), :10366-10380 (inotify rescans), :9225-9235 (comment)

facts.claim: 'INPUT LOST - evdev overflow on mouse fd' is real kernel-side loss (SYN_DROPPED): lvdesk then discards the whole batch, zeroes deltas and clears ptr_pressed/press_edge, so a click can be lost and the button state reset; mouse_poll only runs when the fd is readable, so the drop means the main loop did not get back to poll() before the evdev client ring (default 64 events) filled - i.e. a loop stall while the mouse was moving.

'How the presence of a mouse is declared' does not exist as a mechanism: xshim implements no XInput/XI2 and answers QueryPointer with a synthetic root position; SDL 1.2 and SDL2 never ask whether a pointer exists. lvdesk classifies an evdev node as a mouse iff it has REL_X and BTN_LEFT and NOT KEY_A (so the 8bitdo if0 qualifies), as a keyboard iff it has KEY_A, and EVIOCGRABs both; a node with KEY_A and BTN_LEFT would be a keyboard, never a mouse.
facts.evidence: lvdesk.c:8919-8936 (is_mouse), :735-740 (keyboard = KEY_A + input_grab), :8982-8987; xshim.c:7064-7082 (QueryPointer)

facts.claim: xlite's XQueryPointer always returns root/child 0, coordinates 0,0, mask 0, and XQueryKeymap returns 32 zero bytes. SDL 1.2 only uses them for modifier/state initialisation (harmless). SDL2's X11_ReconcileKeyboardState (run on every FocusIn) compares the zero keymap with SDL's keyboard state and sends SDL_RELEASED for every key SDL believes is held - so a FocusIn delivered mid-keypress releases the key in SDL2 apps.
facts.evidence: xlite_req.c:3184-3207; SDL_x11video.c:1275-1295 (X11_UpdateMouse); SDL_x11events.c:1310-1408 (X11_SetKeyboardState); sdl2 SDL_x11events.c:410-450 (:446-447 release)

facts.claim: lvdesk swallows KEY_LEFTMETA/KEY_RIGHTMETA presses (they are the desktop's ungrab key; in fullscreen they are ignored entirely) but forwards their RELEASES through the generic release path, so clients see Super_L/Super_R releases with no press.
facts.evidence: lvdesk.c:1184-1193 (press path 'continue'), :1156-1177 (release path forwards xkey_sym for any code, incl. KEY_LEFTMETA -> XLW_SUPER_L via :469-470)

facts.claim: SDL 1.2 discards a KeyRelease immediately followed (< 2 ms, same keycode) by a KeyPress as autorepeat, so xshim's real timestamps matter (they are on by default). lvdesk forwards evdev value 2 (kernel autorepeat) as another press without a release, which SDL 1.2 sees as a repeated KeyPress - the 'kc=4/7/8/9 storms' are those repeats; SDL 1.2 drops duplicate presses of an already-pressed sym.
facts.evidence: SDL_x11events.c:305-324 (X11_KeyRepeat), :402-408; xshim.c:8850-8870 (evtime default on); lvdesk.c:986-1000 (value 2 comment), :1156 (only value 0 is a release), :1194 (kbd_key for 1 and 2)

facts.claim: SDL 1.2 (Buildroot sdl-1.2.15) dlopen()s libX11.so.6 / libXext.so.6 and resolves every SDL_X11_SYM by name; a missing name only zeroes that module's HAVE flag. XKeycodeToKeysym, XLookupString, XQueryKeymap, XGetModifierMapping, XGetPointerControl, XChangePointerControl, XGrabPointer, XWarpPointer, XDefineCursor, XCreatePixmapCursor and XResetScreenSaver are all in BASEXLIB and all exist in xlite; X_HAVE_UTF8_STRING XIM paths are neutralised by XOpenIM being a stub (returns 0) so the plain XLookupString branch runs.

suspects.issue: tiopex-quake has no mouse implementation (sdlquake handheld glue): IN_Init sets mouse_avail=0, IN_Move is empty, no SDL_MOUSEMOTION/BUTTON handling, SDL_WM_GrabInput never called.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: With input_grab left at SDL_GRAB_OFF, X11_CheckMouseModeNoLock never sets mouse_relative, so no recentering warps are ever issued, and whatever motion SDL does post is never read by the game - the view cannot turn no matter what xlite/xshim/lvdesk do.
suspects.affected: tiopex-quake (SDL 1.2 TyrQuake) only. Not fixable in xlite/xshim/lvdesk; the SDL2 tyr-quake build (rootfs/build-tyrquake.sh, tyrquake-0.71/common/in_sdl.c) does implement SDL_MOUSEMOTION and SDL_SetRelativeMouseMode.
suspects.evidence: tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/vid_sdl.c:633-651, :36-37; rootfs/build-tiopex.sh:11-14; grep over tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/*.c finds no SDL_MOUSEMOTION/SDL_WM_GrabInput; tyrquake/tyrquake-0.71/common/in_sdl.c:65,583; SDL_x11mouse.c:247-250

suspects.issue: SDL2 key_layout gap: wire keycodes 1..7 (Return, BackSpace, Tab, Escape, Delete, Left, Up) are below xshim's advertised min_keycode of 8, so SDL2 never assigns them a scancode.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: X11_InitKeyboard's fallback builds key_layout only from min_keycode; the KeyPress handler sends SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN for those keycodes; Chocolate Doom maps by scancode (scancode_translate_table) and OpenTyrian by keysym.sym derived from the same keymap, so Esc/Enter/Backspace/Tab/Delete/Left/Up are dead in every SDL2 app while Right/Down/F-keys/letters work - which reads as 'keyboard does not work properly at all'.
suspects.affected: Chocolate Doom, OpenTyrian, tyr-quake (SDL2) and any SDL2 client. SDL 1.2 is unaffected (translates per event via XKeycodeToKeysym). Fix belongs in xlite_wirekeys.h (both ends include it): move XLW_RETURN..XLW_UP out of 1..7 into unused codes >= 8 (e.g. the C1 block 133..139 next to XLW_SUPER_R) and rebuild lvdesk + xlite; alternatively have xshim advertise min_keycode 1 (xshim.c:2564), which SDL2 would honour but violates the core protocol's min >= 8 and may upset other clients.
suspects.evidence: sdl2 SDL_x11keyboard.c:227, :308-324; sdl2 SDL_x11events.c:1150,:1160; xshim.c:2564-2565; xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h:17-23; chocolate-doom-3.1.1/src/i_input.c:105-134; opentyrian src/keyboard.c:151-208

suspects.issue: Shifted keys are sent as the shifted character code (keycode 'A' = 65, '!' = 33) instead of the base key plus ShiftMask.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: SDL 1.2's X11_TranslateKeycode yields SDLKey 65..90 / 33.. for shifted keys, which are not SDLK_* values, so any SDL 1.2 binding on a letter stops firing while Shift is held (Quake +speed/run combos, Doom key+shift) and prboom/tiopex translate them to unknown; SDL2 recovers letters by normalising 0x41-0x5A but shifted punctuation keycodes have no scancode.
suspects.affected: All SDL 1.2 clients (prboom, tiopex-quake, sdlkeys) for Shift+letter/symbol; SDL2 clients for Shift+punctuation. Fix in lvdesk xkey_sym (send keymap[code][0] as keycode, keep Shift in state - xkey_mods already sets bit 0 and xshim_key packs it into the event state) plus xlite XLookupString applying ShiftMask/LockMask to produce the shifted character for text-oriented clients (xcalc/xterm-likes read XLookupString).
suspects.evidence: lvdesk.c:474-481, :484-488; xshim.c:9018; SDL_x11events.c:1141-1143; SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:402-425; xlite/xlite_key.c:184-208

suspects.issue: lvdesk gives a fullscreen client pointer input only via a live pointer grab, while SDL 1.2 itself drops the implicit fullscreen grab 1.5 s after any FocusIn when the app has not called SDL_WM_GrabInput(ON), and leaves fullscreen 200 ms after any FocusOut.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: lvdesk sends FocusIn/FocusOut through xshim_focus on window creation and focus changes; for an SDL 1.2 fullscreen app relying on SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN (no explicit grab: most SDL 1.2 games at menus/title screens, prboom outside a level, sdlkeys without grab) the resulting XUngrabPointer clears xshim's grab_win, after which mouse_poll routes nothing to the client and xwin_send_button drops buttons in fullscreen - mouse dead until the app explicitly grabs.
suspects.affected: Any SDL 1.2 fullscreen client without an explicit SDL_WM_GrabInput(ON); prboom recovers only because I_StartTic re-issues its own grab. Fix in lvdesk: when fs_active, route pointer events to fs_win even with no grab (treat fs_win as the grab top in mouse_poll and xwin_send_button), and avoid sending FocusOut/FocusIn to a fullscreen client's own top-levels after the first FocusIn (xshim_focus already dedups by id).

suspects.issue: XReparentWindow is a stub, so SDL_Window never moves into FSwindow; fullscreen presentation depends on xshim_mode_window's 'last-created fits' rule picking WMwindow.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: If FSwindow ever sorts after WMwindow in res[] (slot reuse after a resource freed between them, or a client that recreates windows), fs_win becomes FSwindow: SDL draws into SDL_Window under WMwindow (black screen) and the grab top (WMwindow) != fs_win, so mouse_poll's 'have' gate fails unless an xwins frame exists for WMwindow and pointer input silently stops. Also under real X the pointer over FSwindow would reach SDL_Window; here it works only by the accident that hit_test(WMwindow) finds SDL_Window at 0,0.
suspects.affected: All SDL 1.2 fullscreen clients (prboom, tiopex-quake, sdlkeys). Fix: implement ReparentWindow (core opcode 7) in xlite (send it) and xshim (re-parent the res, update ax/ay and buf), or make xshim_mode_window prefer the top-level that holds the pointer grab / has been drawn into.

suspects.issue: XLITE_TRACE_INPUT prints only every 50th XWarpPointer.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: Does not break input, but it produced the false reading 'NO recentering warps ever' for tiopex and hides the first 49 warps of any client; diagnosing mouse-look from this trace is unreliable.
suspects.affected: Every trace-based diagnosis of SDL 1.2 / SDL2 warp-mode mouse. Fix: print every warp when tracing (drop the n % 50 sampling), or print the count on ungrab.
suspects.evidence: xlite_req.c:2405-2411

suspects.issue: xlite's XQueryKeymap returns all zeros; SDL2 reconciles keyboard state against it on every FocusIn.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: X11_ReconcileKeyboardState sends SDL_RELEASED for every key SDL thinks is held, so a FocusIn arriving while a key is held (e.g. lvdesk re-focusing on window creation or the fullscreen latch) drops that key in SDL2 apps - Doom stops moving until the key is re-pressed.
suspects.affected: Chocolate Doom, OpenTyrian, tyr-quake (SDL2). Fix in xlite: track pressed keycodes from the KeyPress/KeyRelease events decode() already sees and answer XQueryKeymap with that bitmap.
suspects.evidence: xlite_req.c:3200-3207; sdl2 SDL_x11events.c:410-450; xlite/xlite.c:154-196 (decode sees every key event)

suspects.issue: lvdesk swallows Super/Meta key presses but forwards their releases.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: Clients never see Super_L/Super_R pressed (bindings on the Windows key are dead) and receive unbalanced releases; harmless for SDL but wrong for any client binding LGUI/RGUI.
suspects.affected: All X clients; minor. Fix: forward the press when fs_active (it is already ignored as a desktop key there) or when a grab is held.

suspects.issue: Mouse evdev ring overflow (SYN_DROPPED) during fullscreen games.
suspects.why_it_breaks_input: lvdesk discards the whole batch and clears ptr_pressed, so a click in progress is lost and motion jumps; the cause is the main loop not returning to poll() fast enough while the mouse moves (fs_present / draw time), not the client.
suspects.affected: Every fullscreen SDL client's mouse (prboom mouse-look hiccups, lost clicks). Mitigation: measure fsg_present_us (lvdesk.c:5935-5943) when the drop prints; keep the mouse read ahead of present, or read evdev from a helper thread into a larger user ring.

Either the stderr capture missed process start, or the XDefineCursor lines were attributed elsewhere; it does not change the mouse conclusion, but it should be re-checked because it was the trace detail that made the two apps look different.

Confirm the observed 'TyrQuake' binary was rootfs/tiopex-quake (SDL 1.2, no mouse code) and not rootfs/tyr-quake (SDL2, in_sdl.c with SDL_SetRelativeMouseMode). The trace's 'XWarpPointer -> root 0,0' is SDL 1.2-only (SDL_x11modes.c:338/952), which fits tiopex; check `images/tiopex-quake.nm` for IN_Move/mouse_avail and the launcher entry.

Prediction to verify with rootfs/sdl2keys.c on Chocolate Doom: Escape, Enter, Backspace, Tab, Delete, Left and Up produce SDL_KEYDOWN with scancode 0 (UNKNOWN), Right/Down/Home/End/PgUp/PgDn/F1-F12/Shift/Ctrl and letters/digits produce correct scancodes, Shift+digit/punctuation produces UNKNOWN. If Right/Down also fail, the cause is not the key_layout gap.

Does lvdesk actually send a FocusIn/FocusOut to the fullscreen client during play (xshim_focus callers at lvdesk.c:2804, 5133, 5895-5924)? If yes, every SDL 1.2 fullscreen app without an explicit grab loses its pointer 1.5 s later (events.c:976-980) and leaves fullscreen on FocusOut; the xlite trace would show a bare 'XUngrabPointer()' ~1.5 s after start with no XGrabPointer following.

SDL_WM_GrabInputRaw's body was not read; it is assumed (from SDL_WM_GrabInput at SDL_video.c:1871-1900 and the CheckMouseMode hook at SDL_x11video.c:172) to store video->input_grab and call CheckMouseMode. If it does not call CheckMouseMode, prboom's relative mode would depend on the later SDL_ShowCursor/MapNotify paths instead.

Is res[] ordering of FSwindow before WMwindow guaranteed for every SDL 1.2 client? create_aux_windows creates FSwindow then WMwindow (SDL_x11video.c:352,387) and res_new reuses the lowest free slot, so a resource freed below FSwindow's slot between two SDL_SetVideoMode calls (vis_change path) could reorder them and make xshim_mode_window pick FSwindow.

The 8bitdo if0: is_mouse requires REL_X && BTN_LEFT && !KEY_A. If that interface also reports KEY_A it is opened as a keyboard (and grabbed) instead; if it reports neither REL_X nor KEY_A it is ignored. Its actual EVIOCGBIT capabilities were not available from code.

causes.title: SDL2 keyboard: wire keycodes 1..7 (Return, BackSpace, Tab, Escape, Delete, Left, Up) sit below the min_keycode=8 xshim advertises, so SDL2 never gives them a scancode
causes.mechanism: xshim's connection-setup reply hard-codes min keycode 8 / max 255 (lvdesk/xshim.c:2564-2565); xlite copies those bytes into pub.min_keycode/max_keycode (xlite/xlite.c:773-774) and XDisplayKeycodes returns them (xlite/xlite_req.c:2023-2029). lvdesk emits XLW_RETURN=1 .. XLW_UP=7 for those keys (xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h:17-23, lvdesk/lvdesk.c:430-439) and xshim forwards the byte as KeyPress detail (lvdesk/xshim.c:9014-9043). SDL2's X11_InitKeyboard cannot fingerprint a scancode table (XKeysymToKeycode is xlw_narrow: Home=10, Prior=12, Up=7, Left=6, Delete=5 minus 8 gives 2,4,-1,-2,-3, distance > 2; container sdl2-2.32.10/src/video/x11/SDL_x11keyboard.c:224-260) so it takes the fallback and fills key_layout[i] only for i = min_keycode..max_keycode (SDL_x11keyboard.c:302-325). key_layout is calloc'd, so [1..7] stay SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN. Every KeyPress/KeyRelease is delivered as SDL_SendKeyboardKey(key_layout[keycode]) (SDL_x11events.c:1150, 1160 - the only keycode<min check is inside #ifdef DEBUG_SCANCODES at 1119 and just logs), and SDL_SendKeyboardKeyInternal returns 0 for SCANCODE_UNKNOWN (src/events/SDL_keyboard.c:824-826). Chocolate Doom's TranslateKey is scancode-indexed (chocolate-doom-3.1.1/src/i_input.c:105-131) and drops key 0, so Esc/Enter/Backspace/Tab/Delete/Left/Up are dead while Right(8)/Down(9)/Home..F12(10-27)/Shift/Ctrl(28-31)/letters/digits and Caps/Alt/Super(128-132) work. SDL 1.2 is immune: X11_TranslateKeycode calls XKeycodeToKeysym per event and never consults min_keycode (sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:1119-1142), which is why prboom's keyboard works.
causes.evidence: Our side: lvdesk/xshim.c:2564-2565; xlite/xlite.c:773-774; xlite/xlite_req.c:2023-2029; xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h:17-23 and xlw_lo table :62-68; xlite/xlite_key.c:100-105 (XKeycodeToKeysym = xlw_widen), :506-511 (XKeysymToKeycode = xlw_narrow); lvdesk/lvdesk.c:430-439. Client side (container /src/build/buildroot/build): sdl2-2.32.10/src/video/x11/SDL_x11keyboard.c:74-84, 224-260, 302-325; SDL_x11video.h:126 (key_layout[256]); SDL_x11events.c:1109, 1119 (DEBUG only), 1150, 1160; src/events/SDL_keyboard.c:824-826; chocolate-doom-3.1.1/src/i_input.c:105-131; sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:1119-1142 (SDL 1.2 unaffected). grep for XDisplayKeycodes/min_keycode in xtlite/*.c, xlite/*.c (other than the two sites), rootfs/sdlkeys.c, rootfs/sdl2keys.c: no other reader.
causes.affected_apps: Every SDL2 client: Chocolate Doom, rootfs/sdl2keys, rootfs/tyr-quake (the SDL2 tyrquake-0.71 build). NOT SDL 1.2 (prboom, tiopex-quake, OpenTyrian - the Buildroot opentyrian.mk depends on 'sdl' and uses sdl-config, so it is SDL 1.2 here, not SDL2 as the task text says), NOT xcalc (xtlite widens the keycode itself, xtlite/xtlite.c:966-967).
causes.explains_observations: (b) 'Chocolate Doom keyboard does not work properly at all' while prboom's keyboard works: menus cannot be opened (Esc) or confirmed (Enter), forward (Up) and turn-left (Left) are dead, Right/Down/fire (Ctrl)/letters still respond, which reads as broken-but-not-dead. Also explains why the earlier 2026-09-20 modifier remap fixed Doom's Ctrl/Alt/Shift (they are >= 8) without fixing its menus.
causes.code_test: Run rootfs/sdl2keys with `uinject keytest` (board test, later phase): predicted DOWN/UP for Escape, Return, BackSpace, Tab, Delete, Left, Up print scancode 0/UNKNOWN (or nothing) while Right, Down, Home, End, F1-F12, letters print correct scancodes. Code-only check: assert min_keycode (8) > XLW_UP (7) in lvdesk/xshim.c:2564 vs xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h:23, and trace SDL_x11keyboard.c:308-323 with min_keycode=8 to see key_layout[1..7] untouched.
causes.fix_sketch: Primary (one binary, no wire change): in lvdesk/xshim.c send_setup change `*p++ = 8; /* min keycode */` to `*p++ = 1;` (XLW_RETURN). Only xlite reads this byte and it only feeds XDisplayKeycodes; SDL2's fingerprint arithmetic then yields Home=9, Prior=11, Up=6, Left=5, Delete=4, KP_Enter=14 which still matches no XFree86/evdev table (distance 6 > 2), so it takes the same fallback loop, now over 1..255, and key_layout[1..7] get SDL_SCANCODE_RETURN/BACKSPACE/TAB/ESCAPE/DELETE/LEFT/UP via xlw_widen -> SDL_GetScancodeFromKeySym (keysyms 0xFF0D/08/09/1B/FFFF/FF51/FF52 are all in KeySymToSDLScancode). Durable follow-up (protocol-clean, both ends rebuilt together): move XLW_RETURN..XLW_UP to 133..139 in xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h by extending xlw_hi and zeroing xlw_lo[1..7]; lvdesk.c:430-439 uses the macros and xlw_narrow/xlw_widen follow the tables, but a lvdesk/libX11 version skew on the card would silently kill those seven keys, so ship the xshim byte first.
causes.fix_location: lvdesk/xshim.c:2564 (send_setup, min keycode byte). Optional durable variant: xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h:17-23 and :62-70 (xlw_lo/xlw_hi), rebuild lvdesk + xlite/build.sh together.

causes.title: TyrQuake (tiopex-quake) has no mouse code at all: the dead mouse is the application, not the stack
causes.mechanism: The binary run today is rootfs/tiopex-quake, built by rootfs/build-tiopex.sh from tyrquake/sdlquake-master (the MIPS-handheld SDL 1.2 glue, 'generic vid_sdl.c'). In that file IN_Init sets mouse_avail = 0, IN_Move returns immediately when !mouse_avail, IN_Commands is empty, and Sys_SendKeyEvents' switch handles only SDL_KEYDOWN/SDL_KEYUP (and SDL_QUIT). No file under tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source references SDL_MOUSEMOTION, SDL_MOUSEBUTTON* or SDL_WM_GrabInput. So MotionNotify/ButtonPress delivered by lvdesk/xshim through the SDL 1.2 grab (which IS made: X11_EnterFullScreen -> X11_GrabInputNoLock(input_grab|SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN) -> XUngrabPointer, XGrabPointer(SDL_Window, owner_events=True, confine SDL_Window, cursor None) - exactly the traced sequence) are read by SDL and discarded unread by the game. The missing recentering warps follow from SDL 1.2's relative mode needing this->input_grab != SDL_GRAB_OFF (SDL_x11mouse.c:246-250), which only SDL_WM_GrabInput sets (SDL_video.c:1832-1854); the implicit fullscreen grab never touches input_grab. prboom calls SDL_WM_GrabInput(SDL_GRAB_ON) from I_StartTic whenever it is in a level (prboom-2.5.0/src/SDL/i_video.c:226-236) and consumes motion.xrel, which is why it warps and works. Injected uinject motion fails for the same reason.

Note also that XLITE_TRACE_INPUT prints only every 50th XWarpPointer (xlite/xlite_req.c:2405-2411), so 'no recentering warps' in a short session is weak evidence on its own.
