causes.title: In fullscreen, lvdesk delivers pointer input ONLY through a live pointer grab, and SDL 1.2 drops its implicit fullscreen grab 1.5 s after any FocusIn when the app never called SDL_WM_GrabInput
causes.mechanism: lvdesk's fullscreen pointer path: mouse_poll routes motion/buttons only when xshim_grab_top() is non-zero and equals fs_win or an xwins entry with an image (lvdesk/lvdesk.c:9346-9400); with fs_active, xwin_send_button returns 0 (lvdesk.c:3864-3865) and mouse_read_cb tells LVGL the button is up (lvdesk.c:9591-9592). So a fullscreen client without a grab gets no motion and no buttons while keys still arrive via focus (kbd_key -> win_focus_xid). SDL 1.2 makes the grab during X11_EnterFullScreen, but lvdesk then sends FocusIn to the client's WMwindow (fs_win resolution calls win_set_focus -> xshim_focus at lvdesk.c:5875-5924 and :2804; new-window focus at :5133; send_focus at lvdesk/xshim.c:9171-9205 to any window selecting FocusChangeMask, which SDL 1.2's WMwindow does). SDL 1.2's FocusIn handler queues switch_waiting = 0x01|SDL_FULLSCREEN with a 1500 ms timer (SDL_x11events.c:465-479); when it fires, X11_EnterFullScreen returns early (currently_fullscreen, SDL_x11modes.c:997-999) and X11_PumpEvents then calls X11_GrabInputNoLock(this, this->input_grab) (SDL_x11events.c:975-980), which for input_grab == SDL_GRAB_OFF executes XUngrabPointer + XUngrabKeyboard (SDL_x11wm.c:338-341). xshim clears grab_win (xshim.c:7190-7196) and lvdesk's fullscreen pointer path goes silent. prboom survives because its I_StartTic sets input_grab ON via SDL_WM_GrabInput when in a level, and GrabInputNoLock(ON) re-grabs. Any FocusOut similarly queues X11_LeaveFullScreen after 200 ms (SDL_x11events.c:483-497).
causes.evidence: Our side: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:9346-9400 (grab-only delivery), :3864-3865, :9591-9592, :2794-2804 (win_set_focus -> xshim_focus), :5133, :5875-5924 (fs_win latch focuses the grab holder); lvdesk/xshim.c:9171-9205 (send_focus/xshim_focus), :7190-7196 (UngrabPointer clears grab). Client side (container sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11): SDL_x11events.c:465-479, 483-497, 950-983; SDL_x11modes.c:997-999, 1065-1067; SDL_x11wm.c:328-380; src/video/SDL_video.c:1832-1854 (input_grab only set by SDL_WM_GrabInputRaw); SDL_x11video.c:403-405 (WMwindow selects FocusChangeMask per the maps; not re-read here).
causes.affected_apps: Any SDL 1.2 fullscreen client that relies on the implicit SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN and never calls SDL_WM_GrabInput(ON): tiopex-quake (moot, see C2), OpenTyrian when input_grab is off, prboom at the title/menu/paused states (it regrabs on level entry), rootfs/sdlkeys without its grab flag. Not SDL2 (grabs from SDL_UpdateWindowGrab while relative mode is on).
causes.explains_observations: Would produce exactly the 'keys but no mouse motion/buttons in fullscreen' signature for any SDL 1.2 app that does not grab explicitly, and is the generic stack-side gap the TyrQuake symptom pointed at; for tiopex it is masked by C2. It is also the mechanism behind the historical 'prboom left fullscreen when the weapon was fired' note at lvdesk.c:3852-3862.
causes.code_test: With XLITE_TRACE_INPUT=1 on an SDL 1.2 fullscreen app that does not grab (e.g. rootfs/sdlkeys started without grab, or tiopex), look for a bare 'xlite: XUngrabPointer()' ~1.5 s after 'xshim: pointer grabbed by' with no following XGrabPointer, and lvdesk.log 'xshim: pointer released by'. Code-only: trace SDL_x11events.c:975-980 with input_grab=OFF and SDL_x11wm.c:338-341.
causes.fix_sketch: In lvdesk mouse_poll, when fs_active and no grab is held, treat fs_win as the grab top for delivery: `uint32_t g = xshim_grab_top(); if (!g && fs_active && fs_win) g = fs_win;` so motion/buttons keep flowing to the fullscreen client's top-level through xshim_pointer (hit_test then finds SDL_Window at 0,0 under WMwindow exactly as in the grabbed case). Keep xwin_send_button's fs_active early return. Additionally stop re-sending FocusIn/FocusOut to the fullscreen client's own top-levels after the first FocusIn (the fs_focused latch at lvdesk.c:5918 already prevents per-frame repeats; extend the same guard to win_set_focus while fs_active so a focus flip between the client's two top-levels does not emit FocusOut on the grabbed one).
causes.fix_location: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:9347 (mouse_poll grab block, fallback g = fs_win when fs_active) and lvdesk/lvdesk.c:2794-2804 (win_set_focus fullscreen guard).

causes.title: Shift/Caps are folded into the wire keycode by lvdesk, so SDL 1.2 sees uppercase/punctuation keysyms that are not SDLKeys, and press/release keycodes disagree when Shift changes between them (stuck keys) in both SDLs
causes.mechanism: xkey_sym returns keymap[code][shift ? 1 : 0] with Caps inverting letters (lvdesk/lvdesk.c:471-482), and the release path recomputes xkey_sym with the modifier state current at release time (lvdesk.c:1156-1174). So Shift+w arrives as keycode 0x57 'W' with ShiftMask in state, and 'press w, press Shift, release w' arrives as press 0x77 / release 0x57. xlite's XKeycodeToKeysym(kc, index) ignores index and returns xlw_widen(kc), i.e. the shifted keysym (xlite/xlite_key.c:100-105), and XkbLookupKeySym documents that 'the server folded Shift into the character before sending' (xlite_key.c:481-496). SDL 1.2's X11_TranslateKeycode maps Latin-1 keysyms as key = xsym & 0xFF (SDL_x11events.c:1141-1142) and the SDLKey enum has no members 65..90 ('Skip uppercase letters', include/SDL_keysym.h:75-85), so Shift+letter is an unknown key to every SDL 1.2 app, and SDL_KeyState is indexed by sym (src/events/SDL_keyboard.c:535-546) so a release under a different keysym leaves the pressed entry set. SDL2 normalises 0x41-0x5A to lowercase (src/events/SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:402-404) so letters survive, but shifted punctuation ('!' '@' '#' ...) has no entry in LinuxKeycodeKeysyms and maps to SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN, and the same press/release keycode mismatch sticks keys in SDL2's per-scancode state.
causes.evidence: Our side: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:471-482, :486-488 (xkey_mods sets ShiftMask bit 0), :1156-1174; xlite/xlite_key.c:100-105, :184-208 (XLookupString), :481-496; lvdesk/xshim.c:9018 (state = mods | buttons). Client side (container): sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:1119-1142; sdl-1.2.15/include/SDL_keysym.h:74-92; sdl-1.2.15/src/events/SDL_keyboard.c:535-546; sdl2-2.32.10/src/events/SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:402-425; tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/vid_sdl.c:373-450 (maps only SDLK_a..z, default K_UNKNOWN at :616-618 per the maps).
causes.affected_apps: SDL 1.2: prboom, tiopex-quake, OpenTyrian, sdlkeys (Shift+letter/digit unbound; stuck movement key after a Shift transition - Doom/Quake 'run' is Shift). SDL2: Chocolate Doom, tyr-quake for Shift+punctuation and the stuck-key case. xcalc/xtlite unaffected (it matches the folded keysym plus ShiftMask exactly as sent).
causes.explains_observations: Not the primary cause of (a) or (b), but it is the remaining keyboard defect once C1 lands: 'hold Shift to run then press W' and 'release a movement key after tapping Shift' misbehave in every SDL 1.2 game, and shifted digits/punctuation produce no SDL2 KEYDOWN. Consistent with prboom's keyboard being reported as 'works' in a quick test that did not combine Shift with movement.
causes.code_test: Board (later): rootfs/sdlkeys + `uinject type` with Shift held: predicted sym 65..90 for shifted letters (not SDLK_a..z) and a stuck SDLK_w after 'w down, Shift down, w up'. Code-only: xkey_sym(KEY_W) with shift=1 returns 'W' (0x57); SDLKey enum has no 87.
causes.fix_sketch: Keep the wire contract for text clients but make the keysym APIs X-correct: lvdesk sends the UNSHIFTED character as the keycode (keymap[code][0], caps not applied) and carries Shift/Lock only in state (xkey_mods already does); xlite's XLookupString/Xutf8LookupString/XkbLookupKeySym apply ShiftMask/LockMask through a small US-ASCII shift table to produce the character (so xfiles, the terminal and xcalc still get 'A' and '!'), XKeycodeToKeysym honours index (0 = base keysym, 1 = shifted) and XGetKeyboardMapping returns per_code=2. Alternative with no lvdesk change: give XKeycodeToKeysym an unfold table for shifted ASCII keycodes (index 0: 'A'->'a', '!'->'1', '>'->'.') - this fixes SDL2's key_layout and SDL 1.2's SDLKey but not the press/release mismatch, so the lvdesk change is the real fix. Must be done as one commit across lvdesk + xlite and re-tested with sdlkeys, sdl2keys, xfiles and the terminal keyseq path (lvdesk.c:860, 905).
causes.fix_location: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:471-482 (xkey_sym), :1156-1174 (release path); xlite/xlite_key.c:100-105 (XKeycodeToKeysym), :184-208 (XLookupString), :481-496 (XkbLookupKeySym); xlite/xlite_req.c:2031-2049 (XGetKeyboardMapping per_code).

causes.title: ReparentWindow is unimplemented (xlite stub, no xshim opcode 7), so SDL 1.2 fullscreen routing works only by the accident that WMwindow is created last and sized to the mode
causes.mechanism: SDL 1.2's X11_EnterFullScreen does XReparentWindow(SDL_Window -> FSwindow) (SDL_x11modes.c:968) and LeaveFullScreen reparents back (:1086). xlite's XReparentWindow is a generated no-op stub that sends nothing (xlite/stubs.c:610-615) and xshim's core switch has no case 7, so SDL_Window stays a child of WMwindow; top_of(SDL_Window) == WMwindow. lvdesk resolves fs_win lazily via xshim_mode_window, which scans res[] linearly and lets the LAST mapped top-level of the mode-switching client that fits the mode win (lvdesk/xshim.c:9218-9260, comment 'res[] fills in creation order'); SDL creates FSwindow before WMwindow and sizes WMwindow to the mode, so fs_win == WMwindow == grab top and the pointer grab block in mouse_poll (lvdesk.c:9355-9358) uses the full mode area. But res_new takes the FIRST free slot (xshim.c:761-777), so after any resource has been freed (a previous client exiting, an SDL_SetVideoMode that destroys/recreates windows) a later client's FSwindow can land in a slot after its WMwindow, fs_win becomes FSwindow, and then xwin_on_draw never matches fs_win (nothing presented), the grab top (WMwindow) != fs_win so the 'have' gate at lvdesk.c:9353-9366 fails (no xwins img exists in fullscreen) and no motion/buttons are delivered while keys still arrive. Also xshim's grab is only honoured when top_of(grab_win) == the top lvdesk names (xshim.c:8915-8927), so an FSwindow target would hit-test FSwindow, whose mask is StructureNotify only, and the event would be dropped in send_device_event.
causes.evidence: Our side: xlite/stubs.c:610-615; lvdesk/xshim.c:761-777 (res_new first-free), 9218-9260 (xshim_mode_window), 8915-8927 (grab honoured only for top_of(g)==top), 6132-7935 (no `case 7:` in the core switch; default at 7935-7956 per the maps); lvdesk/lvdesk.c:5875-5877 (lazy fs_win), 9353-9366 (have gate). Client side (container sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11): SDL_x11modes.c:968, 1086; SDL_x11video.c:352 (FSwindow created) vs :387 (WMwindow created), :359 (FSwindow mask StructureNotify only), :1051-1061 (SDL_Window child of WMwindow selecting Button/Motion).
causes.affected_apps: All SDL 1.2 fullscreen clients (prboom, tiopex-quake, OpenTyrian fullscreen, sdlkeys) on the second or later launch in one lvdesk session, or after any window destroy/recreate; latent for anything else that reparents.
causes.explains_observations: Not needed for today's two observations (a single-launch session), but it is the 'works once, not the next time' shape and the reason lvdesk needs the 'prboom has two top-levels, focus the grab holder' special case (lvdesk.c:2793-2796, 5878-5905). It must be understood before the C3 fix, which routes to fs_win.
causes.code_test: Code-only: instantiate res[] with a freed low slot, create FSwindow then WMwindow, call xshim_mode_window(320,240): it returns FSwindow (800x480 fits). Board (later): launch prboom -fullscreen, quit, launch again; lvdesk.log's 'fullscreen' fs_win id differs from the grab holder and the screen stays on the title frame.
causes.fix_sketch: Make xshim_mode_window prefer, in order: the top-level holding the pointer grab (top_of(grab_win)) when its owner is vm_cli; else the vm_cli top-level that has been drawn into most recently (track a per-res 'last_present' or use the existing draw callback); else the current fits/covering/fallback rules. That removes the slot-order dependency without changing which window is presented for SDL 1.2. Implementing core opcode 7 (re-parent, geom_update subtree, damage) plus sending it from xlite is the protocol-correct alternative but changes the presented top-level to FSwindow (800x480 buffer into a 320x240 mode) and must be A/B'd on prboom before shipping.
causes.fix_location: lvdesk/xshim.c:9218-9260 (xshim_mode_window ordering rule); optionally lvdesk/xshim.c core switch (new case 7) and xlite/stubs.c:610-615 -> a real XReparentWindow in xlite/xlite_req.c.

causes.title: Windowed clients without a grab receive MotionNotify only while Button1 is held (LVGL indev path), so hover/absolute-motion clients see a frozen pointer
causes.mechanism: Without a grab, lvdesk feeds pointer position to LVGL's indev (mouse_read_cb, lvdesk.c:9573-9593) and the client image's xwin_ptr_cb is registered only for LV_EVENT_PRESSED/RELEASED/PRESS_LOST/PRESSING (lvdesk.c:5221-5231); LVGL emits no button-up motion to the object, so xshim_pointer motion is only generated while Button1 is down. Button2/3/wheel go through xwin_send_button by frame hit-test (lvdesk.c:3847-3897). A windowed X client that selected PointerMotionMask expecting hover motion therefore gets none until it clicks. SDL2 in relative mode and SDL 1.2 with SDL_WM_GrabInput both hold an X grab, which switches lvdesk to the grab path (lvdesk.c:9346-9400, motion regardless of buttons), so games survive; menus driven by absolute mouse position (OpenTyrian's SDL_MOUSEMOTION handling, SDL2 apps not in relative mode, Xt hover) do not.
causes.evidence: Our side: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:5221-5231 (event registration), :3977-3998 (xwin_ptr_cb per the maps), :9573-9593 (mouse_read_cb), :9346-9400 (grab path is the only button-independent motion source). Client side: opentyrian src/keyboard.c:134-240 (absolute SDL_MOUSEMOTION per the maps, container opentyrian-cf5dbeb.../src/keyboard.c); SDL 1.2 SDL_x11events.c:517-541 (non-relative MotionNotify -> absolute SDL_PrivateMouseMotion); sdl2 SDL_x11window.c:681-686 (window selects PointerMotionMask per the maps).
causes.affected_apps: Windowed clients not holding a grab: OpenTyrian windowed menus (SDL 1.2 absolute motion), Chocolate Doom's menu when relative mode is off (windowed, cursor shown), prboom windowed while un-grabbed (menus/paused), xcalc hover (cosmetic), any Xt/Xaw client using motion.
causes.explains_observations: Not today's two observations; predicted breakage class (c) for windowed SDL2/Xt clients: 'mouse buttons work but the pointer does not move in-app until I click'.
causes.code_test: Board (later): run rootfs/sdlkeys windowed WITHOUT grab and move the mouse over it: predicted no motion lines until Button1 is held. Code-only: no LV_EVENT_HOVER/… registration in lvdesk.c:5221-5231 and xwin_ptr_cb only sends xshim_pointer under PRESSED/PRESSING.
causes.fix_sketch: In mouse_poll's no-grab branch, when the pointer position changes and the top-level under the pointer is an xwins entry with an img (hit-test the frames like xwin_send_button does), call xshim_pointer(top, rx, ry, 0, 0) for hover motion, rate-limited to once per loop pass (xshim already folds motion, xshim.c:3074-3120). Keep LVGL's own press routing unchanged so desktop chrome behaves as before.
causes.fix_location: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:9346-9410 (mouse_poll, add a no-grab hover branch beside the grab block) reusing the frame hit-test from xwin_send_button (lvdesk.c:3847-3897).

causes.title: xlite's XQueryPointer and XQueryKeymap answer constants without asking xshim, so SDL2 force-releases every held key on each FocusIn and any client positioning from XQueryPointer gets 0,0
causes.mechanism: xlite's XQueryPointer returns root=child=0, coordinates 0,0, mask 0 with no request (xlite/xlite_req.c:3184-3197) although xshim implements a correct QueryPointer reply from ptr_root_x/y and ptr_btn_state (lvdesk/xshim.c:7064-7082); XQueryKeymap returns 32 zero bytes (xlite_req.c:3200-3207). SDL2's X11_ReconcileKeyboardState runs at init and on every FocusIn (SDL_x11events.c:403-450, 452-458): for every keycode whose SDL state is PRESSED but whose XQueryKeymap bit is clear it sends SDL_RELEASED. lvdesk sends FocusIn from win_set_focus (lvdesk.c:2804), from new-window id assignment (:5133), and SDL2 itself triggers one via XSetInputFocus on show (sdl2 SDL_x11window.c:1173-1177 -> xlite_req.c:1662-1670 -> xshim.c:7679-7681 -> xshim_focus). A movement key held across any of those is silently dropped.
causes.evidence: Our side: xlite/xlite_req.c:3184-3207, :1662-1670; lvdesk/xshim.c:7064-7082 (correct reply exists), :7679-7681, :9171-9205; lvdesk/lvdesk.c:2804, :5133. Client side (container sdl2-2.32.10/src/video/x11): SDL_x11events.c:403-458; SDL_x11window.c:1173-1177; SDL_x11mouse.c:434-447 (X11_GetGlobalMouseState per the maps). SDL 1.2 uses XQueryPointer only in X11_UpdateMouse to post a bogus motion to 0,0 (SDL_x11video.c:1275-1295 per the maps).
causes.affected_apps: SDL2 clients (Chocolate Doom, tyr-quake) on any focus change while a key is held; any client that places popups from XQueryPointer. Low frequency, latent.
causes.explains_observations: A plausible secondary contributor to 'keys drop' reports in SDL2 games; does not explain (a) or (b) on its own.
causes.code_test: Code-only: XQueryPointer body has no REQ(); XQueryKeymap memsets zero. Board (later): sdl2keys, hold 'w', click another window then back: predicted spurious UP for 'w' at the FocusIn.
causes.fix_sketch: xlite: implement XQueryPointer as a real opcode 38 round trip parsing xshim's reply (root x/y at bytes 8-15 of the reply data, mask at 16); implement XQueryKeymap by tracking KeyPress/KeyRelease in decode() (xlite/xlite.c:154-196) into a 32-byte bitmap keyed by wire keycode, or add opcode 44 (QueryKeymap) to xshim answered from lvdesk's key state via a new xshim_keystate callback. The decode-side bitmap is simplest and needs no xshim change.
causes.fix_location: xlite/xlite_req.c:3184-3207 (XQueryPointer, XQueryKeymap); xlite/xlite.c:154-196 (decode() key bookkeeping).

causes.title: 'How the presence of a mouse is declared' is not a mechanism in this stack; the lvdesk log lines cited as evidence are measurement artefacts, and device classification only decides which evdev nodes lvdesk reads
causes.mechanism: No X client here ever asks whether a pointer exists: the core protocol has no such query, SDL 1.2 never asks, and SDL2 only enumerates devices via XInput2, which xshim reports absent (QueryExtension answers only RENDER, XLITE-SHM, XLITE-RING, XFree86-VidModeExtension, RANDR, MIT-SHM at lvdesk/xshim.c:6132-6191; sdl2 SDL_x11xinput2.c:132-135 returns before touching libXi), so SDL2 uses warp-emulated relative mode (src/events/SDL_mouse.c:1143-1152) which xshim's synthesised warp MotionNotify satisfies (xshim.c:7221-7278, arrives at exactly dst->ax+dx so SDL_mouse.c:558-577 recognises it). On the lvdesk side, is_mouse = REL_X && BTN_LEFT && !KEY_A (lvdesk.c:8920-8935) and keyboard = KEY_A (lvdesk.c:735-740); the 8bitdo if0 qualifies as a mouse only because it reports REL_X and BTN_LEFT, and its REL deltas are simply summed into the same ptr_x/ptr_y as the Logitech's - a wrong classification could only add motion, not remove it. The 'input starved for N ms' line is the gap between successive kbd_poll calls (lvdesk.c:929-955), and kbd_poll runs only when a keyboard fd is readable or a rescan is due (lvdesk.c:10382-10387), so N ~= the length of a mouse-only game session is expected and is not starvation. 'INPUT LOST - evdev overflow on mouse fd' is a real SYN_DROPPED (lvdesk.c:9190-9204): the batch is discarded and ptr_pressed is cleared without an EVIOCGKEY re-sync, so a held button is reported released once; that is a transient loss during a long present, not a persistent mouse death.
causes.evidence: lvdesk/xshim.c:6132-6191, 7221-7278; lvdesk/lvdesk.c:735-740, 8920-8935, 929-955, 10368-10388, 9190-9204; container sdl2-2.32.10/src/video/x11/SDL_x11xinput2.c:132-135, SDL_x11mouse.c:381-384, src/events/SDL_mouse.c:558-577, 1132-1156. The 8bitdo if0's actual EVIOCGBIT capability bits: not found in code (needs the device).
causes.affected_apps: None as a cause. The SYN_DROPPED path affects all clients transiently (lost click / released fire button during a long fullscreen present).
causes.explains_observations: Explains why the two lvdesk.log lines should not be read as the mouse being lost, and closes the user's 'is it how the mouse is declared?' hypothesis: nothing declares it, and the declaration lvdesk does make (is_mouse) cannot produce 'motion never arrives' for a device it opened.
causes.code_test: Code-only: grep xshim.c for 'XInputExtension' (0 hits) and xlite/libX11-exports.txt for XIQueryVersion (absent); kbd_poll's gap is computed only inside kbd_poll. causes.title: SDL2 keyboard: wire keycodes 1..7 (Return, BackSpace, Tab, Escape, Delete, Left, Up) sit below the min-keycode 8 that xshim advertises, so SDL2 never builds a scancode for them
causes.mechanism: xshim's connection-setup reply hard-codes min keycode 8 / max 255 (lvdesk/xshim.c:2564-2565); xlite copies the bytes (xlite/xlite.c:773-774) and XDisplayKeycodes returns them (xlite/xlite_req.c:2023-2029). The shared wire contract puts the seven specials at 1..7 (xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h:17-23) and lvdesk emits exactly those (lvdesk/lvdesk.c:430-439), xshim forwards the byte as the KeyPress detail (lvdesk/xshim.c:9014-9046). SDL2's X11_InitKeyboard: fingerprint values are XKeysymToKeycode(sym)-min_keycode = Home 2, Prior 4, Up -1, Left -2, Delete -3, KP_Enter 7 (xlw_narrow, xlite/xlite_key.c:506-511), three negatives alone give distance >2 and the XF86Documents check yields 0-8 != 235, so it takes the 'layout unknown' branch and fills key_layout[i] ONLY for i in [min_keycode..max_keycode] = 8..255 (container sdl2-2.32.10/src/video/x11/SDL_x11keyboard.c:227-229, 302-325; key_layout is calloc'd, SDL_x11video.h:126). Every KeyPress/KeyRelease is delivered as SDL_SendKeyboardKey(key_layout[keycode]) (SDL_x11events.c:1150, 1160) and SDL_SendKeyboardKeyInternal returns 0 for SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN (src/events/SDL_keyboard.c:824). Keycodes >= 8 (Right, Down, Home..F12, Shift/Ctrl 28-31, Caps/Alt/Super 128-132, letters, digits, space) resolve correctly through XKeycodeToKeysym = xlw_widen (xlite/xlite_key.c:100-105) and SDL_GetScancodeFromKeySym (src/events/SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:390-435). SDL 1.2 never consults min_keycode: X11_TranslateKeycode calls XKeycodeToKeysym per event and maps 0xFF-page keysyms through MISC_keymap (container sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:1119-1165), which is why prboom's keyboard works.
causes.evidence: Client side: sdl2-2.32.10/src/video/x11/SDL_x11keyboard.c:227 (X11_XDisplayKeycodes), 228-260 (fingerprint), 302-325 (fallback loop from min_keycode), SDL_x11events.c:1150/1160, src/events/SDL_keyboard.c:824; chocolate-doom-3.1.1/src/i_input.c:105-131 (TranslateKey by scancode, returns 0), 252-259 (event dropped when data1 == 0). Our side: lvdesk/xshim.c:2564-2565; xlite/xlite.c:773-774; xlite/xlite_req.c:2023-2029; xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h:17-23; lvdesk/lvdesk.c:430-439. Contrast SDL 1.2: sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:1119-1165 (no min_keycode use).
causes.affected_apps: Every SDL2 client: Chocolate Doom, rootfs/tyr-quake (tyrquake-0.71, SDL2), rootfs/sdl2keys. NOT prboom / tiopex-quake / OpenTyrian (all SDL 1.2 - note buildroot/package/opentyrian/opentyrian.mk depends on 'sdl' and uses sdl-config, so OpenTyrian here is SDL 1.2, not SDL2 as the task text says), NOT xcalc (xtlite widens the wire keycode itself, xtlite/xtlite.c:966-967).
causes.explains_observations: (b) 'Chocolate Doom keyboard does not work properly at all' while prboom works: Escape/Enter (menus), Backspace, Tab, Delete, Left and Up are dead; Right, Down, letters, Ctrl/Alt/Shift, F-keys work - a menu you cannot open or confirm and a player who can turn right but not left reads as 'not working at all'. Text input (SDL_TEXTINPUT via XLookupString, xlite/xlite_key.c:184-208) still works, so typed characters appear where Chocolate Doom reads chars, which is a second confusing symptom.
causes.code_test: Static: `./docker/build.sh 'grep -n "for (i = min_keycode" /src/build/buildroot/build/sdl2-2.32.10/src/video/x11/SDL_x11keyboard.c'` shows both loops start at min_keycode; `grep -n 'min keycode' lvdesk/xshim.c` shows 8; `sed -n 17,23p xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h` shows 1..7. Prediction for the board later: rootfs/sdl2keys with `uinject keytest` prints DOWN/UP with scancode=0 (Unknown) for Escape, Return, BackSpace, Tab, Delete, Left, Up and correct scancodes for Right/Down/letters; after the fix all seven print their real scancode. If Right/Down also fail the cause is not this one.
causes.fix_sketch: Fix pass (one byte, our code only, no wire change): advertise min keycode 1 in send_setup - `*p++ = 1; /* min keycode */` at lvdesk/xshim.c:2564. xlite is the only libX11 here and merely copies the byte; SDL2's fingerprint values become 9,11,6,5,4,14 which still match no XFree86/evdev table (needs >=4 of 6 exact) and XF86Documents gives -1 != 235, so the fallback loop now covers 1..255 and SDL_GetScancodeFromKeySym finds 0xFF0D/0xFF08/0xFF09/0xFF1B/0xFFFF/0xFF51/0xFF52 by table scan (SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:411-424). SDL 1.2 and xtlite never read min_keycode, so they are unaffected. Optionally mirror it in XDisplayKeycodes (clamp *min to 1) for belt and braces. Durable follow-up (protocol-clean): move XLW_RETURN..XLW_UP to the free C1 block 133..139 in xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h (update xlw_lo/xlw_hi tables at :61-70 and xlw_widen/narrow :72-97), rebuild lvdesk AND xlite together (both include the header; lvdesk.c:430-439 uses the macros, xshim passes bytes), and re-run sdlkeys + sdl2keys.
causes.fix_location: lvdesk/xshim.c:2564 (send_setup min keycode) [+ optional xlite/xlite_req.c:2023-2029]; durable variant: xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h:17-23 and :61-97, rebuild lvdesk + xlite

causes.title: TyrQuake as run (rootfs/tiopex-quake, SDL 1.2) contains no mouse code at all: the dead mouse is the application, not lvdesk/xshim/xlite
causes.mechanism: rootfs/build-tiopex.sh:11-19 compiles tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/vid_sdl.c (the generic handheld glue) with sdl-config 1.2. In that file IN_Init sets mouse_avail = 0, IN_Shutdown likewise, IN_Commands is empty and IN_Move returns immediately when !mouse_avail (vid_sdl.c:633-651); Sys_SendKeyEvents handles only SDL_KEYDOWN/SDL_KEYUP/SDL_QUIT (vid_sdl.c:224-630). A grep over tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/*.c for SDL_MOUSEMOTION|SDL_MOUSEBUTTON|SDL_GetRelativeMouseState|SDL_WM_GrabInput matches nothing (only mouse_avail and SDL_ShowCursor(0) at :145). Because SDL_WM_GrabInput is never called, this->input_grab stays SDL_GRAB_OFF; X11_EnterFullScreen's grab passes input_grab|SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN to X11_GrabInputNoLock WITHOUT changing input_grab (sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11modes.c:1067; SDL_x11wm.c:328-379 never touches it; only SDL_WM_GrabInputRaw does, src/video/SDL_video.c:1832-1863). X11_CheckMouseModeNoLock enters relative mode only when the cursor is hidden AND input_grab != OFF AND full app focus (SDL_x11mouse.c:246-250), so mouse_relative is never 1, X11_WarpedMotion never runs and no recentering XWarpPointer is ever issued (SDL_x11events.c:519-541). Motion that SDL does post (absolute) is discarded unread by the game. There is also no 'presence of a mouse' declaration anywhere in the path: the core protocol has none, SDL 1.2 never asks, SDL2 only asks via XInput2 which xshim reports absent (lvdesk/xshim.c:6132-6191); lvdesk's only notion is is_mouse() = REL_X && BTN_LEFT && !KEY_A (lvdesk/lvdesk.c:8917-8935).
causes.evidence: App: tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/vid_sdl.c:36-37, 145, 224-630, 633-651; rootfs/build-tiopex.sh:11-19; artifacts/quake/td-rate48k-221611/run.sh (exec ./tiopex-quake ... -fullscreen). SDL 1.2: SDL_x11modes.c:1002, 1067; SDL_x11wm.c:328-379; SDL_video.c:1832-1863; SDL_x11mouse.c:246-268; SDL_x11events.c:519-541. Contrast prboom: prboom-2.5.0/src/SDL/i_video.c:226-236 (SDL_WM_GrabInput per tic in a level), 693 (SDL_ShowCursor(0)). The SDL2 build rootfs/tyr-quake (rootfs/build-tyrquake.sh, tyrquake-0.71/common/in_sdl.c) is a different binary with mouse code - and it is hit by C1.
causes.affected_apps: tiopex-quake only (mouse). Its keyboard works because SDL 1.2 translates by keysym.
causes.explains_observations: (a) entirely: TyrQuake shows the fullscreen-entry prefix (XWarpPointer -> root 0,0 is move_cursor_to in X11_ResizeFullScreen, SDL_x11modes.c:336-339/952-963; XUngrabPointer + XGrabPointer(owner=1 confine=same window) is X11_GrabInputNoLock), then no recentering warps (mouse_relative never set) and the view never turns for real or injected motion (no consumer). Keys work (SDL_KEYDOWN handled). The trace's 'FSwindow' label is a mislabel: SDL grabs SDL_Window, confine SDL_Window (SDL_x11wm.c:352-354). The missing XDefineCursor is a separate anomaly (SDL_SetVideoMode always calls SDL_SetCursor(NULL) -> XDefineCursor, SDL_video.c:760, SDL_x11mouse.c:146-168) and most likely means XLITE_TRACE_INPUT was not in that process's environment (the harness run.sh does not export it); note also the warp trace prints only every 50th call (xlite/xlite_req.c:2404-2411).
causes.code_test: `grep -rn -E 'SDL_MOUSEMOTION|SDL_MOUSEBUTTON|SDL_WM_GrabInput|GetRelativeMouseState' tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/` returns nothing; `sed -n 633,651p tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/vid_sdl.c` shows the empty IN_* functions; `strings rootfs/tiopex-quake | grep libSDL` -> libSDL-1.2.so.0. Board later: sdlkeys (SDL 1.2 logger, grab+hide) under the same fullscreen shows motion arriving, proving the stack delivers what the app ignores.
causes.fix_sketch: None possible within xlite/xshim/lvdesk - the binary has no consumer. Under the no-app-patching rule, close the observation as 'application feature absent'. The mouse-capable Quake on the card is rootfs/tyr-quake (SDL2), which needs C1 (Escape/Enter/Up/Left) and benefits from C3/C5 before it can be judged.
causes.fix_location: n/a (application); document in docs/current-state.md next to the tiopex build note

causes.title: In fullscreen, lvdesk delivers pointer input ONLY through a live pointer grab, and lvdesk's own FocusIn makes SDL 1.2 drop its implicit fullscreen grab 1.5 s later for any app that never called SDL_WM_GrabInput - the generic 'keys but no mouse in fullscreen' mechanism
causes.mechanism: lvdesk side: mouse_poll routes motion/buttons/wheel to xshim_grab_top() only, gated on g == fs_win or an xwins img (lvdesk/lvdesk.c:9346-9408); with fs_active, xwin_send_button returns 0 (lvdesk.c:3864-3865) and the LVGL indev is told the button is up unless (!grab && !fs_active) (lvdesk.c:9591-9592). So a fullscreen client without a grab gets no pointer events at all, while keys still reach it via focus (kbd_key -> win_focus_xid, lvdesk.c:840-848, 1163-1177). SDL 1.2 side: any FocusIn on WMwindow sets switch_waiting = FULLSCREEN with a 1500 ms timer; when it fires X11_PumpEvents calls X11_GrabInputNoLock(this, this->input_grab) (sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:465-479, 952-982), and for input_grab == SDL_GRAB_OFF that is XUngrabPointer + XUngrabKeyboard (SDL_x11wm.c:338-340), which xshim honours by clearing grab_win (lvdesk/xshim.c:7190-7196). lvdesk DOES send that FocusIn: xshim_focus/send_focus emit FocusIn/FocusOut to every window of a top-level that selected FocusChangeMask (xshim.c:9171-9205; WMwindow selects it, SDL_x11video.c:403-405), and lvdesk calls xshim_focus from make_window/map (lvdesk.c:5131-5133) and from the first fullscreen draw, which re-focuses the grab holder's top-level (lvdesk.c:5875-5924, win_set_focus -> xshim_focus at 2794-2804). xlite decodes FocusIn with mode/detail 0 (memset in decode, xlite/xlite.c:145-149, default arm :239-241), so SDL always acts on it. Any FocusOut (e.g. when FSwindow maps after WMwindow and make_window focuses it, before fs_active is set) queues X11_LeaveFullScreen after 200 ms (SDL_x11events.c:483-497) - a race the current ordering usually wins. prboom survives only because I_StartTic re-issues SDL_WM_GrabInput(ON) every tic while in a level (prboom i_video.c:226-236), so input_grab is ON and the 1.5 s re-grab re-grabs; in menus/paused (input_grab OFF) prboom's pointer is dead too.
causes.affected_apps: Any SDL 1.2 fullscreen client that relies on SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN alone (tiopex-quake would be, if it had mouse code; sdlkeys without grab; prboom outside a level; OpenTyrian fullscreen unless its input_grab option is on); any non-SDL fullscreen client (an Xt app switching modes) that does not grab; any client whose XGrabPointer is answered AlreadyGrabbed by a stale grab (xshim.c:7177-7179; SDL 1.2 then spins forever with SDL_Delay(100), SDL_x11wm.c:349-358).
causes.explains_observations: The generic shape of (a): fullscreen keys arrive, motion and buttons do not. Also the historical 'prboom left fullscreen when the weapon was fired' (lvdesk.c:3852-3862). Not what kills tiopex (C2), but it is what will kill the next fullscreen app that does not grab explicitly.
causes.code_test: Static: confirm the three fs_active gates (lvdesk.c:3864, 9591, 9355-9366) and that xshim_focus is reached from the fullscreen draw path (lvdesk.c:5922 -> 2804). Log test (existing logs, no board access needed): an SDL 1.2 fullscreen app run with XLITE_TRACE_INPUT=1 that never calls SDL_WM_GrabInput shows 'xlite: XUngrabPointer()' ~1.5 s after 'XGrabPointer(... ) -> 0' with no XGrabPointer following, and lvdesk.log shows 'xshim: pointer released by 0x...' at the same time. For prboom the same ungrab is followed by a fresh XGrabPointer.
causes.fix_sketch: lvdesk: when fs_active and xshim_grab_top() == 0, treat fs_win as the grab top in mouse_poll (a = mode rect, deliver motion/buttons/wheel via xshim_pointer(fs_win, ...)) - xshim_pointer then hit-tests to SDL_Window whose mask selects Button/Motion (xshim.c:8929-8930, send_device_event propagation), so the client gets X-correct events without a grab; keep xwin_send_button's early return. Also stop the focus churn: in xshim_focus, do not emit FocusOut/FocusIn when the old and new top-levels belong to the same client while a vidmode client is fullscreen (xshim.c:9192-9206), and in lvdesk's map path (lvdesk.c:5131-5133) do not steal focus for a second top-level of the client that already holds focus. Optional robustness: on GrabPointer from a different client, let a grab whose holder's fd is alive but whose top-level is no longer the mode window be released (xshim.c:7177-7179) so a stale grab cannot hang a new SDL 1.2 app.
causes.fix_location: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:9346-9366 (mouse_poll grab block), 5131-5133 (map-time focus), 2794-2804 (win_set_focus); lvdesk/xshim.c:9192-9206 (xshim_focus), 7177-7179 (GrabPointer)

causes.title: Shift and Caps are folded into the wire keycode ('A' for Shift+a, '!' for Shift+1), so XKeycodeToKeysym(kc,0) returns the SHIFTED keysym: SDL 1.2 maps Shift+letter to a non-existent SDLKey and both SDLs get stuck keys when Shift changes between press and release
causes.mechanism: lvdesk chooses the character with the CURRENT shift/caps state on both press and release: xkey_sym uses keymap[code][shift ? 1 : 0] and inverts letters for caps (lvdesk/lvdesk.c:474-482); releases call the same xkey_sym at release time (lvdesk.c:1156-1174). xlite treats keycode == keysym: XKeycodeToKeysym/XkbKeycodeToKeysym return xlw_widen(kc) ignoring the index (xlite/xlite_key.c:100-105, 158-163), and XkbLookupKeySym declares Shift consumed 'because the server folded Shift into the character' (xlite_key.c:481-496). SDL 1.2's X11_TranslateKeycode maps Latin-1 keysyms as key = xsym & 0xFF (sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:1141-1142); SDLKey has no members 65..90, so Shift+W is SDLKey 87 which nothing binds, and SDL_KeyState is indexed by sym (src/events/SDL_keyboard.c:535-546) so press 'w'(0x77)/release 'W'(0x57) leaves SDLK_w held. SDL2 normalises 0x41-0x5A to lowercase (src/events/SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:402-404) so letters survive, but '!' '@' '#' etc. are absent from LinuxKeycodeKeysyms and map to SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN, so Shift+digit sends no KEYDOWN and press '.'/Shift/release '>' leaves SCANCODE_PERIOD held.
causes.evidence: Ours: lvdesk/lvdesk.c:379-411 (keymap[][2]), 474-482, 486-488 (xkey_mods carries Shift as state bit 0 already), 1156-1174; xlite/xlite_key.c:100-105, 158-163, 184-208, 481-496; xlite/xlite_req.c:2031-2049 (XGetKeyboardMapping per_code=1 identity). Client: sdl-1.2.15 SDL_x11events.c:1119-1143, include/SDL_keysym.h:75-85 (SDLK_AT=64 .. SDLK_LEFTBRACKET=91, SDLK_a=97), src/events/SDL_keyboard.c:535-546; sdl2 src/events/SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:61-310 (level-0 syms only), 402-404, 411-424; tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/vid_sdl.c:373-450 (only SDLK_a..z cases). xtlite is unaffected: it widens the wire code itself and matches keysym + ShiftMask (xtlite/xtlite.c:963-968).
causes.affected_apps: prboom, tiopex-quake, OpenTyrian, sdlkeys (all SDL 1.2): Shift+letter dead (run-while-moving combos), stuck movement keys; Chocolate Doom, tyr-quake, sdl2keys (SDL2): Shift+punctuation dead, stuck keys across a Shift transition. xcalc: unaffected.
causes.explains_observations: Contributes to (b) beyond C1 (keys that 'stick' or fail while Shift/run is held) and to the general 'keyboard not handled properly' report for SDL 1.2 games; not the primary symptom in either trace.
causes.code_test: Static: `sed -n 474,482p lvdesk/lvdesk.c` (shift applied in xkey_sym) and `sed -n 100,105p xlite/xlite_key.c` (index ignored); `grep -c 'XK_exclam\|0x21,' /src/build/buildroot/build/sdl2-2.32.10/src/events/SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c` = 0 in the container. Board later: sdlkeys with `uinject type` of a shifted letter shows key=87 ('W') instead of key=119 + mod SHIFT; sdl2keys shows scancode=0 for Shift+1.
causes.fix_sketch: xlite-only, minimal and safe: give XKeycodeToKeysym/XkbKeycodeToKeysym a US level table for ASCII keycodes - index 0 returns the level-0 keysym ('A'->'a', '!'->'1', '>'->'.'), index 1 returns the shifted one - while XLookupString/Xutf8LookupString/XkbLookupKeySym keep returning the folded character for text. SDL2 then builds key_layout['!'] = SCANCODE_1 and keymap[SCANCODE_1] = '1' (X11_KeyCodeToUcs4 uses the same function with group 0; the lowercase entry is visited later and wins), SDL 1.2 gets SDLK_w + KMOD_SHIFT (its modstate comes from the XLW_SHIFT_L/R key events, not xkey.state) and press/release match by sym; XGetKeyboardMapping should report per_code=2 with both levels for consistency (xlite_req.c:2031-2049). The fuller fix (lvdesk sends keymap[code][0] with Shift/Lock only in state and xlite applies the shift table in XLookupString) is X-correct but touches xtlite's exact-match translations and the terminal keyseq path (lvdesk.c:860, 905) and needs xfiles re-tested - do it second.
causes.fix_location: xlite/xlite_key.c:100-105 (XKeycodeToKeysym), 158-163 (XkbKeycodeToKeysym), xlite/xlite_req.c:2031-2049 (XGetKeyboardMapping); later lvdesk/lvdesk.c:474-482 + xlite/xlite_key.c:184-208, 481-496

causes.title: xlite's XQueryKeymap and XQueryPointer answer from constants (nothing held, 0,0) without asking the server, so SDL2 force-releases every held key on each FocusIn and global pointer queries are wrong
causes.mechanism: XQueryPointer returns True with root/child 0, x=y=0, mask 0 and sends no request (xlite/xlite_req.c:3184-3198); XQueryKeymap memsets 32 zero bytes (xlite_req.c:3200-3207) - although xshim implements a correct QueryPointer reply from ptr_root_x/y and ptr_btn_state (lvdesk/xshim.c:7064-7082, set at 8901-8906). SDL2's X11_ReconcileKeyboardState runs at init and on every FocusIn and sends SDL_RELEASED for every scancode SDL believes pressed that the (all-zero) keymap denies (sdl2-2.32.10/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:403-450, 452-458). xshim emits FocusIn whenever lvdesk's focused top-level changes (xshim.c:9192-9206; callers lvdesk.c:2804, 5133, 5922) and on SDL2's own XSetInputFocus (xshim.c:7679-7681, issued by X11_ShowWindow because no _NET_SUPPORTING_WM_CHECK exists so net_wm is false, SDL_x11window.c:1173-1178). XGetModifierMapping is all zeros too (xlite_key.c:210-221), so Caps/Num lock masks are never known.
causes.evidence: Ours: xlite/xlite_req.c:3184-3207; xlite/xlite_key.c:210-221; lvdesk/xshim.c:7064-7082, 8901-8906, 7679-7681, 9192-9206. Client: sdl2 SDL_x11events.c:403-458; SDL_x11window.c:1173-1178; SDL_x11mouse.c:434-447 (X11_GetGlobalMouseState); sdl-1.2.15 SDL_x11video.c:1275-1295 (X11_UpdateMouse posts a bogus 0,0 motion - harmless).
causes.affected_apps: SDL2 clients (Chocolate Doom, tyr-quake, sdl2keys): a movement key held across any focus event is silently released; any client positioning from XQueryPointer (SDL_GetGlobalMouseState, Xt popups) gets 0,0.
causes.explains_observations: A secondary contributor to (b)/(c): 'keys drop' in SDL2 games whenever lvdesk re-sends focus. Not the primary symptom.
causes.code_test: Static: `sed -n 3184,3207p xlite/xlite_req.c` shows no REQ()/xlite_reply(); `grep -n 'case 44' lvdesk/xshim.c` shows QueryKeymap (opcode 44) is unhandled. Board later: sdl2keys with a key held while another window is focused/unfocused prints an UP with no physical release.
causes.fix_sketch: xlite: implement XQueryPointer as a real opcode-38 round trip parsing xshim's reply (root x/y, mask); implement XQueryKeymap from a 32-byte bitmap that decode() maintains from every KeyPress/KeyRelease it sees (xlite/xlite.c:154-196 already sees them; keycodes are 1..255 so the bitmap indexes directly). Optionally xshim answers opcode 44 from lvdesk's key state, but the client-side bitmap is sufficient and cheaper.
causes.fix_location: xlite/xlite_req.c:3184-3207 (XQueryPointer, XQueryKeymap); xlite/xlite.c:154-196 (decode key bookkeeping); optional lvdesk/xshim.c core switch (opcode 44)

causes.title: Windowed clients without a pointer grab receive MotionNotify only while Button1 is held: hover-driven UIs (OpenTyrian menus, SDL2 non-relative mode, Xt) see a frozen pointer until a click
causes.mechanism: Without a grab, lvdesk feeds the pointer through LVGL's indev; xwin_ptr_cb is registered on the client image only for PRESSED, RELEASED, PRESS_LOST and PRESSING (lvdesk/lvdesk.c:5221-5231) and it calls xshim_pointer(x->id, ..., 1, act) with act 0 (motion) only from PRESSING (lvdesk.c:3977-3998), so motion reaches the client only with Button1 down. Button2/3/wheel go through xwin_send_button hit-testing (lvdesk.c:3847-3897). The grab path (lvdesk.c:9346-9408) reports motion regardless of buttons but only for the grab holder. Real X delivers PointerMotion to whatever selected it under the pointer. OpenTyrian (SDL 1.2) uses absolute SDL_MOUSEMOTION for its menus and grabs only when its input_grab option is on (opentyrian src/keyboard.c:100-112, 134-240); SDL2 windowed non-relative mode and Xt hover/Enter-Leave behave the same way.

causes.title: ReparentWindow is unimplemented (xlite stub, no xshim opcode 7), so SDL 1.2 fullscreen routing works only because WMwindow happens to sort after FSwindow in res[]; slot reuse can flip fs_win to FSwindow and silently kill both picture and pointer
causes.mechanism: SDL 1.2 reparents SDL_Window into FSwindow on fullscreen entry and back on leave (sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11modes.c:968, 1086). xlite's XReparentWindow is a no-op stub (xlite/stubs.c:610-615) and xshim's core switch has no case 7 (only RENDER/SHM/RANDR minor-op 7s at xshim.c:4840, 5642, 8142), so SDL_Window stays a child of WMwindow and top_of(SDL_Window) == WMwindow. lvdesk resolves fs_win via xshim_mode_window, which scans res[] linearly and lets the LAST mapped top-level of the vidmode client that fits the mode win, on the assumption 'res[] fills in creation order' (xshim.c:9218-9260); but res_new takes the first FREE slot (xshim.c:761-777), so after any earlier client freed resources a later-created WMwindow can land in a lower slot than FSwindow. Then fs_win = FSwindow: xwin_on_draw(WMwindow) never presents (lvdesk.c:5926), and in mouse_poll g == WMwindow != fs_win so 'have' falls back to an xwins img that fullscreen never creates (lvdesk.c:9355-9366) - no motion, no buttons - while keys still flow through focus. FSwindow selects StructureNotify only (SDL_x11video.c:359), so even xshim_pointer(FSwindow) would drop everything at propagation (xshim.c:8828-8845).

causes.title: SDL2 keyboard: wire keycodes 1..7 (Return, BackSpace, Tab, Escape, Delete, Left, Up) sit below the min_keycode=8 xshim advertises, so SDL2 never builds a scancode for them and drops the events
causes.mechanism: xshim's connection setup says min-keycode 8 / max 255. xlite copies those bytes verbatim and XDisplayKeycodes returns them. SDL2's X11_InitKeyboard cannot fingerprint the layout (XKeysymToKeycode is xlw_narrow: Home=10, Prior=12, Up=7, Left=6, Delete=5, KP_Enter=15, minus 8 gives 2,4,-1,-2,-3,7 -> no table within distance 2; XF86Documents narrows to 0, 0-8 != 235) and takes the fallback loop `for (i = min_keycode; i <= max_keycode; ++i) key_layout[i] = X11_KeyCodeToSDLScancode(i)`. SDL_VideoData is calloc'd, so key_layout[1..7] stays SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN. Every KeyPress/KeyRelease does SDL_SendKeyboardKey(..., key_layout[keycode]) and SDL_SendKeyboardKeyInternal returns 0 for SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN. lvdesk emits exactly those codes (xkey_sym returns XLW_ESCAPE=4 etc.) and xshim_key forwards the byte as the event detail. Right(8), Down(9), Home..F12 (10-27), Shift/Ctrl (28-31), Caps/Alt/Super (128-132) and printable ASCII are >= 8 and map correctly via xlw_widen -> SDL_GetScancodeFromKeySym. SDL 1.2 never consults min_keycode: X11_TranslateKeycode calls XKeycodeToKeysym per event and maps 0xFF-page keysyms through MISC_keymap, so prboom/tiopex keyboards work. Chocolate Doom keys everything off sym->scancode (TranslateKey -> scancode_translate_table, event dropped when 0), so Escape/Enter (menus), Up/Left (forward/turn), Backspace/Tab/Delete are dead while Right/Down/letters/Ctrl/Alt/Shift/F-keys work - 'does not work properly at all'.

causes.title: lvdesk folds Shift and Caps into the wire keycode ('A'=65 for Shift+a, '!'=33 for Shift+1) and computes the KeyRelease code with the modifier state current at release, so SDL 1.2 gets non-SDLK keys for Shift+letter and both SDLs get stuck keys across a Shift transition
causes.mechanism: xkey_sym() returns keymap[code][shift ? 1 : 0] with caps inversion, and both the press (kbd_key) and the release path call it with the state at that instant. Real X sends the level-0 keycode plus ShiftMask and lets the client apply Shift. SDL 1.2's X11_TranslateKeycode maps Latin-1 keysyms as `key = xsym & 0xFF`; SDLKey has no members between SDLK_AT (64) and SDLK_LEFTBRACKET (91), so Shift+w arrives as SDLKey 87 which prboom's I_TranslateKey and tiopex's SDLK_a..z switch treat as unknown (run+forward dead), and 'w' pressed / Shift pressed / 'w' released delivers press 0x77 and release 0x57: SDL's keystate (indexed by sym) keeps SDLK_w pressed. SDL2 normalises 0x41-0x5A to lowercase before its table lookup so shifted LETTERS survive, but shifted punctuation keysyms ('!' '@' '#' '>' ...) are absent from LinuxKeycodeKeysyms and map to SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN: Shift+digit produces no KEYDOWN, and '.' pressed then released while Shift (run) is held arrives as '>' whose release is dropped - SCANCODE_PERIOD stays pressed. xlite's XLookupString/XkbLookupKeySym are written for the folded contract (Shift reported as consumed).

causes.title: Fullscreen pointer delivery exists ONLY through the grab path, and its correctness rests on the grab top-level coinciding with fs_win - which holds for SDL 1.2 only because XReparentWindow is a no-op stub and res_new() happens to hand out slots in creation order
causes.mechanism: When fs_active, xwin_send_button returns 0 (no Button2/3/wheel hit-testing), mouse_read_cb reports RELEASED to LVGL (no Button1/motion via the indev), and the only pointer route into a client is the block in mouse_poll keyed on g = xshim_grab_top(): it uses the whole mode rectangle when g == fs_win, else looks for an xwins[] img for g, else delivers nothing (have == 0) silently. fs_win is resolved lazily on the first draw by xshim_mode_window(), which returns the LAST mapped top-level of the mode-switching client that is >= the mode ('The last one created wins: res[] fills in creation order'). SDL 1.2 creates FSwindow before WMwindow and sizes WMwindow to the mode, so fs_win = WMwindow; because XReparentWindow is an xlite stub (and xshim has no core opcode 7 handler) SDL_Window stays a child of WMwindow, so top_of(SDL_Window) = WMwindow = fs_win and everything lines up - by coincidence. res_new() takes the FIRST free slot, so after any earlier client has exited, a later SDL 1.2 client's FSwindow and WMwindow can land in reversed slot order and fs_win becomes FSwindow: xwin_on_draw(WMwindow) never presents (black or frozen picture) and the grab block has g = WMwindow != fs_win with no img -> no motion, no buttons, keys still arrive via the keyboard grab. That is the generic 'keys but no pointer' signature for a fullscreen SDL 1.2 client on a second launch. Any fullscreen client whose XGrabPointer is refused (AlreadyGrabbed from a stale grab held by another connection - SDL 1.2 then spins forever with SDL_Delay(100)) is in the same state.

causes.title: Windowed clients without a pointer grab receive MotionNotify only while Button1 is held: lvdesk routes hover motion through LVGL's indev, which only fires PRESSING, so plain PointerMotion selection is never honoured
causes.mechanism: Outside the grab block, the only two pointer routes are xwin_send_button (Button2/3/wheel by frame hit-test, no motion) and xwin_ptr_cb, which is registered on the client img for LV_EVENT_PRESSED/RELEASED/PRESS_LOST/PRESSING only and calls xshim_pointer(x->id, ..., 1, act) with act=0 for PRESSING. LVGL generates no button-up motion events to the object, and no hover path calls xshim_pointer at all (the seven callers are lines 3890, 3997 and the grab block). A windowed client that selected PointerMotionMask therefore sees a frozen pointer until a click, and Enter/Leave crossing only on clicks. SDL 1.2 OpenTyrian uses absolute SDL_MOUSEMOTION for its menus and only grabs on input_grab(); SDL2 apps in non-relative mode (Chocolate Doom menus before the game grabs, or after SDL_WINDOW_INPUT_FOCUS is lost so warp-relative is off) and Xt hover (Xaw Command highlights on EnterWindow) are all affected. SDL2 relative mode survives because SDL_UpdateWindowGrab issues XGrabPointer (owner_events False, confine=window) after FocusIn, which puts the client on the grab path.

causes.title: xlite's XQueryPointer and XQueryKeymap answer from constants (0,0 / nothing held) without asking xshim, so SDL2's X11_ReconcileKeyboardState force-releases every held key on each FocusIn and SDL 1.2's X11_UpdateMouse posts a bogus motion to 0,0
causes.mechanism: XQueryPointer returns True with root=child=0, x=y=0, mask=0 and never sends opcode 38, although xshim implements a correct QueryPointer reply from ptr_root_x/y and ptr_btn_state. XQueryKeymap memsets 32 zero bytes. SDL2 runs X11_ReconcileKeyboardState at init and from X11_DispatchFocusIn: for every keycode where SDL believes the key is pressed and the (zero) X keymap says released, it sends SDL_RELEASED. xshim sends FocusIn whenever lvdesk's focused top-level changes (win_set_focus -> xshim_focus, make_window's late xshim_focus, and SDL2's own XSetInputFocus via opcode 42) and xlite decodes FocusIn with mode/detail 0 so SDL2 always dispatches it. A movement key held across any such focus event is silently dropped in SDL2 apps. SDL 1.2's X11_UpdateMouse (every SDL_SetVideoMode) treats 0,0 as in-window and posts a motion to 0,0 (harmless).

causes.title: WarpPointer to the root (or None) is a RELATIVE move with no synthesised MotionNotify, and warps to a top-level without an lvdesk img are ignored - SDL 1.2's root warps land at the wrong place and any client waiting for the warp's motion stalls
causes.mechanism: ROOT_ID (0x100) is a bare constant with no res[] entry (res_find fails), so xshim's WarpPointer takes the `!dst` branch and calls warp_cb(0, dx, dy): lvdesk's xwin_on_warp then ADDS (dx,dy) to ptr_x/ptr_y and clamps. SDL 1.2's move_cursor_to(SDL_Root, x, y) during fullscreen entry therefore moves the pointer BY (0,0) then BY (real_w/2, real_h/2) instead of TO those points, and no MotionNotify is synthesised on that branch (the synth at xshim.c:7266-7276 is only reached for a real window dst). A warp to a real window whose top-level has no img and is not fs_win is silently dropped in xwin_on_warp. Today this is benign: SDL 1.2 immediately recentres via XWarpPointer(SDL_Window) (window dst, synthesised motion works, which is what fixed the 'stall then lurch'), and SDL2's warp-relative uses SDL_WarpMouseInWindow. SDL2's X11_WarpMouseGlobal (root dst) and any client that warps to root then blocks in XMaskEvent(PointerMotionMask) would hang until real motion arrives.

causes.title: The diagnostics misled the investigation: 'input starved for N ms' measures time since the last KEY, not a loop stall; XWarpPointer is traced 1-in-50; SYN_DROPPED discards the batch and forges a Button1 release without re-syncing from EVIOCGKEY
causes.mechanism: kbd_poll is only entered when poll() flags a keyboard fd or a rescan is due (rescans are inotify-driven now, not the 2 s timer), so kbd_last_poll_ms advances only on keyboard events; a mouse-only game session prints 'starved for <session length>' on the first key afterwards - lvdesk's own comment concedes the gap 'cannot tell a quiet moment from a late one'. The XWarpPointer trace prints only when n++ % 50 == 0, so 'no recentering warps' proves fewer than 50, not zero (C2 shows tiopex IS in relative mode). On SYN_DROPPED lvdesk zeroes the accumulated deltas/wheel/extra button and clears ptr_pressed without asking the kernel for the real button state, so a held fire button is reported released and the later physical release is a no-op; the fd stays open. None of these lose the game's keys, but two of them produced false evidence today.

CLIENT SIDE: sdl-1.2.15 SDL_x11events.c:352-355 (one XWarpPointer per edge visit; 320x240 mode needs ~150 px of travel per warp, so 50 warps is thousands of pixels).

result.reasoning: Every link in the chain checks out against the actual source. (1) xshim advertises min keycode 8 / max 255 in the setup reply (lvdesk/xshim.c:2564-2565); xlite copies bytes 26/27 into pub.min_keycode/max_keycode (xlite/xlite.c:773-774) and XDisplayKeycodes returns them unmodified (xlite/xlite_req.c:2023-2029). (2) The wire contract puts Return/BackSpace/Tab/Escape/Delete/Left/Up at 1..7 (xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h:17-23); lvdesk's xkey_sym emits exactly those macros (lvdesk/lvdesk.c:430-439); xshim_key forwards the byte as the event detail with no remapping (lvdesk/xshim.c:9014-9046, send_device_event(..., (uint8_t)sym, ...)); xlite's event decoder deliberately keeps the WIRE keycode in xkey.keycode (xlite/xlite.c:185-195 comment: 'The keycode keeps the WIRE value, including the XLW_ low codes'). (3) SDL2 2.32.10 X11_InitKeyboard: XkbQueryExtension returns False in xlite (xlite/xlite_key.c:129-140) so data->xkb stays NULL (SDL_VideoData is SDL_calloc'd, SDL_x11video.c:180) and X11_KeyCodeToSym falls to X11_XKeycodeToKeysym = xlw_widen (SDL_x11keyboard.c:96-131; xlite/xlite_key.c:100-105). Fingerprint values are XKeysymToKeycode(sym) - min_keycode with XKeysymToKeycode = xlw_narrow (xlite/xlite_key.c:506-511): Home 10-8=2, Prior 12-8=4, Up 7-8=-1, Left 6-8=-2, Delete 5-8=-3, KP_Enter 15-8=7; three negatives each add 1 to distance (SDL_x11keyboard.c:236-241), so best_distance >= 3 > 2; the XF86Documents re-check gives xlw_narrow(0x1008FF5B)=0, 0-8=-8 != 235 (SDL_x11keyboard.c:250-260). The 'layout unknown' branch then fills key_layout[i] only for i in [min_keycode..max_keycode] = 8..255 (SDL_x11keyboard.c:302-325); key_layout is a 256-entry array inside the calloc'd SDL_VideoData (SDL_x11video.h:126), so entries 1..7 stay SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN (0). (4) At event time SDL_x11events.c:1150/1160 send SDL_SendKeyboardKey(state, key_layout[keycode]) with no range check, and the 'unknown keycode' block at SDL_x11events.c:1118-1127 is inside #ifdef DEBUG_SCANCODES - it is a log, not a runtime fallback, and is compiled out. SDL_SendKeyboardKeyInternal returns 0 immediately for SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN (src/events/SDL_keyboard.c:824-826), so no SDL_KEYDOWN/KEYUP is ever posted for those seven keys. (5) Keycodes >= 8 do resolve: all nine special keysyms are present in LinuxKeycodeKeysyms (SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:63 Escape, 76 BackSpace, 77 Tab, 90 Return, 165 Up, 167 Left, 168 Right, 170 Down, 173 Delete) and the table scan at :411-424 finds them by keysym, so Right (wire 8) and Down (wire 9) get SDL_SCANCODE_RIGHT/DOWN while Left/Up, sitting below 8, never get looked up. (6) Chocolate Doom's TranslateKey indexes scancode_translate_table[scancode], whose entry 0 is 0 (i_input.c:105-131; doomkeys.h:94-95 '0, 0, 0, 0, a'), and I_HandleKeyboardEvent only posts when data1 != 0 (i_input.c:252-259) - but this is moot since no SDL key event reaches it at all. (7) SDL 1.2 contrast holds: X11_TranslateKeycode calls XKeycodeToKeysym per event and maps 0xFF-page keysyms through MISC_keymap with no min_keycode involvement (sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:1119-1165), so prboom/TyrQuake keyboards work with the same wire bytes; xtlite widens the wire keycode itself (xtlite/xtlite.c:966-967), so xcalc is unaffected. The fix sketch also checks out: with min keycode 1 the fingerprint values become 9,11,6,5,4,14 and none of the four scancode tables (darwin: H,G,Z,V,NONUSBACKSLASH,Q; xfree86 1 and 2: 3,4,5,8,0,BACKSPACE; xvnc: UNKNOWN,UNKNOWN,LALT,0,2,5 at indices 4,5,6,9,11,14) matches a single fingerprint scancode, so the layout-unknown loop runs 1..255 and SDL_GetScancodeFromKeySym resolves 1..7 by keysym scan. Symptom match: Escape and Enter dead means menus cannot be opened or confirmed, Up dead means no forward movement, Left dead means no left turn, while letters, Ctrl/Alt/Shift (28-31, 128-132) and Right/Down work - a Doom that 'does not work properly at all' on the keyboard, while prboom (SDL 1.2) works. result.corrected_mechanism: SDL2's X11 backend builds its keycode->scancode table (SDL_VideoData.key_layout[256], calloc'd) once at init and only for X keycodes in [min_keycode, max_keycode] as reported by XDisplayKeycodes (sdl2-2.32.10/src/video/x11/SDL_x11keyboard.c:227, 302-325). xshim's setup reply advertises min keycode 8 (lvdesk/xshim.c:2564), which xlite passes through verbatim (xlite/xlite.c:773, xlite/xlite_req.c:2023-2029). But the shared wire contract encodes Return, BackSpace, Tab, Escape, Delete, Left and Up as keycodes 1..7 (xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h:17-23), lvdesk emits exactly those (lvdesk/lvdesk.c:430-439), xshim forwards the byte unchanged as the KeyPress detail (lvdesk/xshim.c:9042), and xlite keeps the wire value in xkey.keycode by design (xlite/xlite.c:185-195). Because xlite's XkbQueryExtension returns False, SDL2 uses XKeycodeToKeysym (= xlw_widen) and XKeysymToKeycode (= xlw_narrow); the six-key fingerprint comes out as 2,4,-1,-2,-3,7, matches no scancode set (three negatives alone push distance past 2) and the XF86Documents check gives -8, so SDL2 takes the 'layout unknown' branch and fills key_layout[8..255] via SDL_GetScancodeFromKeySym, leaving key_layout[1..7] = SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN. Each KeyPress/KeyRelease is delivered as SDL_SendKeyboardKey(state, key_layout[keycode]) with no range check (SDL_x11events.c:1150, 1160; the only 'unknown keycode' handling at :1118-1127 is compiled out under DEBUG_SCANCODES), and SDL_SendKeyboardKeyInternal returns 0 for SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN before posting anything (src/events/SDL_keyboard.c:824). Net effect in every SDL2 client on this desktop: Escape, Return, BackSpace, Tab, Delete, Left and Up generate no SDL key events at all (only SDL_TEXTINPUT for the four that XLookupString maps to a control character), while Right, Down, Home/End/PgUp/PgDn/Insert/KP_Enter/F1-F12 (10-27), Shift/Ctrl (28-31), Caps/Alt/Super (128-132), letters, digits and space all resolve correctly. Chocolate Doom therefore cannot open or confirm menus (Escape/Enter), move forward (Up) or turn left (Left) but can turn right, move back, fire and strafe - which presents as 'keyboard does not work properly at all'. SDL 1.2 (prboom, TyrQuake, OpenTyrian) is unaffected because X11_TranslateKeycode calls XKeycodeToKeysym per event and never consults min_keycode (sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:1119-1165); xcalc is unaffected because xtlite widens the wire keycode itself (xtlite/xtlite.c:966-967). Fix (our code only): advertise min keycode 1 at lvdesk/xshim.c:2564 - with min_keycode=1 the fingerprint becomes 9,11,6,5,4,14, which matches none of the darwin/xfree86_1/xfree86_2/xvnc tables (verified at those indices) and XF86Documents gives -1, so SDL2 still takes the layout-unknown branch but now fills key_layout[1..255], and SDL_GetScancodeFromKeySym finds 0xFF0D/0xFF08/0xFF09/0xFF1B/0xFFFF/0xFF51/0xFF52 by keysym scan in LinuxKeycodeKeysyms (SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:63,76,77,90,165,167,173). Optionally clamp *min to 1 in XDisplayKeycodes (xlite/xlite_req.c:2025) as belt and braces; the durable variant is to move the seven low XLW_ codes into the free C1 range 133..139 in xlite_wirekeys.h and rebuild lvdesk and xlite together. Test prediction correction: rootfs/sdl2keys with `uinject keytest` will print NO line at all for those seven keys (no event is posted), and correct scancodes for Right/Down/letters; after the fix all seven print their real scancode.

SDL 1.2 (prboom, tiopex-quake, OpenTyrian) never consults min_keycode - it maps each event's keysym through MISC_keymap (sdl-1.2.15 SDL_x11events.c:1119-1165) - and xtlite widens the byte itself (xtlite/xtlite.c:966-967), so only SDL2 apps show it. SDL SIDE (does not hold): C3 claims the 1.5 s FocusIn timer runs X11_GrabInputNoLock(this, this->input_grab) with input_grab == SDL_GRAB_OFF for any app that never called SDL_WM_GrabInput, producing a bare XUngrabPointer. In SDL 1.2.15 input_grab is never OFF for a fullscreen surface after SDL_SetVideoMode returns:

SDL_WM_GrabInput (:1893-1899) adds SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN (= 2, include/SDL_video.h:927) because SDL_VideoSurface->flags has SDL_FULLSCREEN, and SDL_WM_GrabInputRaw (:1846-1857) sees mode 2 != OFF with input_grab == OFF, calls video->GrabInput(this, 2) and stores input_grab = 2.

An app's own SDL_WM_GrabInput(SDL_GRAB_OFF) in fullscreen is converted to mode 2 (:1893-1897) and, since input_grab != OFF, calls nothing (:1846-1849) and leaves input_grab = 2.
 - Therefore the FocusIn timer (SDL_x11events.c:465-479, :952-982) calls X11_GrabInputNoLock(this, 2), which takes the ELSE branch of SDL_x11wm.c:338-361: XUngrabPointer, then XGrabPointer(SDL_Window, True, confine SDL_Window) in a loop until GrabSuccess, then XGrabKeyboard. It is a re-grab, not a release. xshim answers the client's own UngrabPointer by clearing grab_cli (xshim.c:7191-7196), so the immediately following GrabPointer from the same client cannot hit AlreadyGrabbed (:7177-7179). No bare ungrab exists on this path.
 - The observed trace 'XWarpPointer -> root 0,0, XUngrabPointer, XGrabPointer(FSwindow owner=1 confine=FSwindow) -> 0' is exactly that re-grab shape (warp = X11_ResizeFullScreen, SDL_x11modes.c:338). Its symptom is the game LEAVING fullscreen (mode restore, XReparentWindow to WMwindow, SDL_x11modes.c:1086-1130), which was not observed for tiopex (320x240 mode stayed up, keys arrived). lvdesk's win_set_focus refuses focus moves away from fs_win/grab top while fs_active (lvdesk.c:2794-2796), xshim_focus dedups same-id calls (xshim.c:9192-9193), and xwin_on_draw focuses the grab holder's top-level (lvdesk.c:5896-5924), so no FocusOut is generated on the steady-state fullscreen path.

In fullscreen, SDL_WM_GrabInput(SDL_GRAB_ON) becomes mode 3 and SDL_WM_GrabInputRaw does NOT call GrabInput because input_grab (2) != OFF (SDL_video.c:1850-1853); it only stores input_grab = 3. That function normalises 0x41-0x5A to lowercase (:402-404) so 'W' and 'w' both become SCANCODE_W, but KeySymToSDLScancode (:27-53) has no ASCII punctuation, LinuxKeycodeKeysyms holds only level-0 syms (0x31 for KEY_1 at :64, no 0x21 anywhere - grep confirms), ExtendedLinuxKeycodeKeysyms (:325-386) has only XK_dollar at linux keycode 0x1b2 (a nonsense key). So key_layout['!'] = SCANCODE_UNKNOWN and SDL_SendKeyboardKey (SDL_keyboard.c:824-825) returns 0 for UNKNOWN. Event dispatch uses key_layout[keycode] for both press and release (SDL_x11events.c:1150, 1160). Hence Shift+1 in Chocolate Doom produces text "!" (via XLookupStringAsUTF8) but no KEYDOWN, and press '.'/Shift/release '>' leaves SCANCODE_PERIOD held. Chocolate Doom's TranslateKey (i_input.c:105-128) is scancode-driven, so it inherits exactly this.

Would it produce observed symptoms? Nothing in the claim is wrong or overstated, so refuted=false.

result.corrected_mechanism:
lvdesk composes the wire keycode from the LIVE modifier state on both press and release (lvdesk.c:474-482 via keymap[code][shift], with Caps Lock inverting letter case), and xlite tells every client that keycode == keysym regardless of the requested shift level (XKeycodeToKeysym/XkbKeycodeToKeysym ignore index/level, xlite_key.c:100-105, 158-163; XGetKeyboardMapping per_code=1, xlite_req.c:2031-2049). Consequences, each verified in the client source:

SDL 1.2 (prboom, TyrQuake, OpenTyrian-1.2 builds, sdlkeys): X11_TranslateKeycode(kc,0) takes the keysym's low byte as the SDLKey (SDL_x11events.c:1141-1142). SDLKey has no members 65-90 (SDL_keysym.h:81-83 "Skip uppercase letters"), so (a) Shift+letter arrives as SDLKey 65-90 which no game binds (TyrQuake vid_sdl.c default -> K_UNKNOWN; prboom passes 87 through unbound); (b) with Caps Lock on, EVERY unshifted letter arrives as its uppercase code, so WASD is entirely dead in SDL 1.2 games until Caps is cleared; (c) SDL_KeyState[] is indexed by sym and drops events that do not change state (SDL_keyboard.c:537-546), so a key pressed as 'w'(0x77) and released as 'W'(0x57) because Shift (run) went down in between never gets its SDL_KEYUP - the player keeps moving forward; the same for any punctuation across a Shift transition. Shift itself is fine (XLW_SHIFT_L -> 0xFFE1 -> SDLK_LSHIFT feeds SDL_ModState), so only the co-pressed key is mangled.

SDL2 (Chocolate Doom, sdl2keys): key_layout is built per keycode from the same identity keysym (fingerprint fails, SDL_x11keyboard.c:301-323), then SDL_GetScancodeFromKeySym lowercases 0x41-0x5A (SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:402-404) so letters survive Shift and Caps, but shifted punctuation ('!' '@' '#' '>' '?' '_' '+' '{' '}' '|' ':' '"' '~' '<' etc.) has no entry in any of the three tables and maps to SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN, which SDL_SendKeyboardKey ignores (SDL_keyboard.c:824-825). So Shift+digit/punctuation produces SDL_TEXTINPUT but no SDL_KEYDOWN/KEYUP, and a punctuation key released after Shift changed state stays held (press '.' -> SCANCODE_PERIOD down, release as '>' -> UNKNOWN -> ignored).

xcalc/xtlite is unaffected (xtlite.c:963-968 matches widened keysym plus ShiftMask itself). This is a real, contributory defect - stuck movement keys, dead run+move combos, dead letters under Caps Lock in SDL 1.2, dead shifted punctuation in SDL2 - but it does not explain the TyrQuake mouse-look failure or the Chocolate Doom "keyboard does not work at all" report, which need another cause. The minimal fix stands as sketched: make XKeycodeToKeysym/XkbKeycodeToKeysym (and XGetKeyboardMapping with per_code=2) return the US level-0 keysym for index/level 0 ('A'->'a', '!'->'1', '>'->'.') and the shifted one for index 1, leaving XLookupString/Xutf8LookupString/XkbLookupKeySym returning the folded character for text; SDL 1.2 then sees SDLK_w with KMOD_SHIFT from the Shift key events and press/release match by sym, and SDL2 builds key_layout['!'] = SCANCODE_1 with keymap[SCANCODE_1] = '1' (the unshifted entry is visited later in X11_UpdateKeymap and wins).

result.reasoning:
Every line citation in C5 checks out: xlite/xlite_req.c:3184-3198 (XQueryPointer returns True with root/child 0, all coords 0, mask 0, no REQ/round trip), 3200-3207 (XQueryKeymap memsets 32 zero bytes), xlite/xlite_key.c:210-221 (XGetModifierMapping is calloc'd zeros, max_keypermod 2), lvdesk/xshim.c:7064-7082 (opcode 38 answered from ptr_root_x/y and ptr_btn_state, set at 8905-8906), no `case 44` in xshim's core switch (opcode 44 appears only in the opstr name table at xshim.c:2073), SDL2 X11_ReconcileKeyboardState at sdl2-2.32.10/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:403-450 called from X11_DispatchFocusIn (452-458), from X11_InitKeyboard (SDL_x11keyboard.c:335) and on KeymapNotify (917), and X11_ShowWindow forcing XSetInputFocus when !net_wm (SDL_x11window.c:1173-1178). xlite's decode() does deliver FocusIn/FocusOut usably: the default arm sets xany.window = g32(e+4) with mode/detail left 0 (NotifyNormal/NotifyAncestor), which SDL2's filters at SDL_x11events.c:1038-1050 pass, so X11_DispatchFocusIn really runs on every xshim FocusIn.

The mechanism fails on its consequence, not its citations. The claimed harm - "SDL2 force-releases every held key on each FocusIn" because the keymap is all zeros - is pre-empted in every focus sequence xshim can produce:
1. xshim_focus() (lvdesk/xshim.c:9192-9204) is the only emitter of FocusIn. It returns early when the id is already focused (9196-9197), and otherwise sends FocusOut to the previously focused top-level (9198-9199) BEFORE FocusIn to the new one (9201-9202). send_focus (9170-9189) emits mode 0 / detail 3 (NotifyNonlinear), which SDL2 processes.
2. SDL2 already releases every held key on FocusOut, independently of XQueryKeymap: X11_DispatchFocusOut (SDL_x11events.c:472-483) calls SDL_SetKeyboardFocus(NULL), which at src/events/SDL_keyboard.c:771-773 calls SDL_ResetKeyboard(). So when the following FocusIn's reconcile runs, SDL believes nothing is pressed and the loop at 403-450 has nothing to release; the zero keymap releases nothing extra. SDL 1.2 behaves the same way: FocusOut -> SDL_PrivateAppActive(0, SDL_APPINPUTFOCUS) (sdl-1.2.15 SDL_x11events.c:483-487) -> SDL_ResetKeyboard (src/events/SDL_active.c:87-88), before X11_SetKeyboardState's XQueryKeymap (SDL_x11events.c:1322) could matter.
3. The only FocusIn that is not preceded by a FocusOut on the same window is the first one: lvdesk.c:5125-5133 (make_window focused the frame before it had an X id) or SDL2's own XSetInputFocus at ShowWindow, which xshim routes to xshim_focus and dedups (xshim.c:7679-7681, 9196). Both happen at window creation, before any key can be held. The lvdesk.c:5915-5922 fullscreen path is guarded by fs_focused precisely so it does not re-send FocusIn per frame.
4. The QueryPointer modifier-mask half is inert too: xshim's "correct" reply carries only ptr_btn_state (xshim.c:355 "Button1Mask.. of held buttons", 7080), never LockMask/Num/Scroll, so a real opcode-38 round trip would return the same mask=0 for the bits X11_ReconcileKeyboardState tests (SDL_x11events.c:417-421) and SDL_ToggleModState would set the same values. Modifier bits reach clients only in key-event state (xshim.c:9018, mods & 0x0F).
5. Symptom fit: Chocolate Doom windowed "keyboard does not work at all" involves no focus change during play, so a FocusIn-only mechanism cannot produce a whole-session failure; Chocolate Doom's mouse uses SDL_GetRelativeMouseState (chocolate-doom-3.1.1/src/i_input.c:443, i_video.c:268-269), not SDL_GetGlobalMouseState, so XQueryPointer's 0,0 is never consulted; TyrQuake's dead mouse motion is an SDL 1.2 MotionNotify path, and the only SDL 1.2 use of XQueryPointer (X11_UpdateMouse, SDL_x11video.c:1275-1295) posts a 0,0 motion the proposal itself calls harmless.

Residual (not the observed symptom): SDL2 defers focus events only while last_mode_change_deadline is set (SDL_x11events.c:1055, 1088), which happens solely after a display-mode change (SDL_x11modes.c:740) for ~400 ms; there a FocusOut+FocusIn pair collapses into one pending FocusIn (1620-1633), and the reconcile with a zero keymap would then release keys SDL still thinks are held. That is a fullscreen-mode-change corner, not "keys drop whenever lvdesk re-sends focus", and not any of the three observations. XQueryPointer/XQueryKeymap/XGetModifierMapping are genuine fidelity gaps worth closing cheaply, but they do not contribute to (b) or (c).

result.corrected_mechanism: Not a cause of the observed symptoms. xlite's constant XQueryPointer (0,0, mask 0), XQueryKeymap (all zero) and XGetModifierMapping (all zero) are real fidelity gaps, but they are inert for keyboard state here: xshim only ever emits FocusIn after a FocusOut to the previously focused top-level (xshim.c:9196-9202), and both SDL2 (SDL_x11events.c:472-483 -> SDL_keyboard.c:771-773) and SDL 1.2 (SDL_x11events.c:483-487 -> SDL_active.c:87-88) already release every held key on that FocusOut, so the zero keymap in the subsequent FocusIn reconcile has nothing left to release. The first FocusIn (window creation / ShowWindow's XSetInputFocus) precedes any key press. A real QueryPointer reply from xshim would carry the same mask=0 for Lock/Num/Scroll because xshim's reply holds only ptr_btn_state (xshim.c:7080). Chocolate Doom never calls SDL_GetGlobalMouseState. The only path where the zero keymap could actually drop a held key is SDL2's ~400 ms deferred-focus window after a display-mode change (SDL_x11modes.c:740; SDL_x11events.c:1055/1088/1620-1633) collapsing FocusOut+FocusIn into one FocusIn - a fullscreen-mode-change corner, not the windowed Chocolate Doom keyboard failure nor the TyrQuake mouse failure. Implementing XQueryKeymap from a decode()-maintained bitmap and XQueryPointer as an opcode-38 round trip is a cheap correctness improvement, not a fix for (b) or (c).

result.corrected_mechanism: lvdesk folds the CURRENT Shift and Caps Lock state into the one-byte wire keycode on both press and release (lvdesk.c:476-481, 1170-1174), and xlite reports keycode == keysym for every level (XKeycodeToKeysym/XkbKeycodeToKeysym ignore index/level, xlite_key.c:100-105, 158-163). Consequences, verified per client library: SDL 1.2 (prboom, tiopex-quake, OpenTyrian-1.2 builds, sdlkeys) translates each press and release with XKeycodeToKeysym(kc,0) and maps Latin-1 as key = xsym & 0xFF (SDL_x11events.c:1124, 1141-1142); a shifted or Caps-inverted letter arrives as keysym 0x41-0x5A, for which no SDLKey exists (SDL_keysym.h:75-79), so Shift+letter and EVERY letter while Caps Lock is on produce an unbound key, and a letter whose Shift/Caps state differs between press and release stays pressed in SDL_KeyState[sym] (SDL_keyboard.c:537-546) with no SDL_KEYUP for the lowercase sym. Shifted punctuation is merely a different valid SDLKey ('!'=SDLK_EXCLAIM) - dead only if the app binds the unshifted key. SDL2 (Chocolate Doom, sdl2keys) is spared for letters (uppercase normalised to lowercase, SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:402-404) but its keycode->scancode table, built once at init from XKeycodeToKeysym(kc,0) because Xkb is absent (SDL_x11keyboard.c:125, 160-166, 305-324), has SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN for every shifted-punctuation keycode ('!' '@' '#' '<' '>' ...) since only level-0 syms are in LinuxKeycodeKeysyms; those presses are dropped (SDL_keyboard.c:824) and a '.' released as '>' leaves SCANCODE_PERIOD held. This is a real latent defect but it explains none of the 2026-09-23 observations: prboom/TyrQuake keyboards worked (arrows and modifiers travel as XLW_ codes), and Chocolate Doom's failure involves no shifted key. result.reasoning: The mechanism survives a line-by-line read of both sides. (1) The client image registers exactly four LVGL events: PRESSED (lvdesk/lvdesk.c:5221), RELEASED (5229), PRESS_LOST (5230), PRESSING (5231); no HOVER_OVER/HOVER_LEAVE, and LVGL would only emit those on widget crossings anyway, never per-position (lvgl/src/indev/lv_indev.c:1465-1489). (2) xwin_ptr_cb (lvdesk.c:3977-3998) maps PRESSED->act 1, RELEASED/PRESS_LOST->act 2, default (PRESSING)->act 0, always with button=1 (3997). (3) There are exactly three xshim_pointer call sites in lvdesk.c: 3890 (xwin_send_button: buttons 2/3/4/5, act 1/2 only, no act 0), 3997 (the LVGL callback), and 9380-9400 (the grab branch, which does send act 0 on every position change but only to xshim_grab_top()).
