result.corrected_mechanism: lvdesk delivers pointer motion to an X client through exactly two paths. (A) Grab path, lvdesk.c:9346-9408: when xshim_grab_top() is non-zero, mouse_poll clamps the pointer to the grab holder's rectangle and calls xshim_pointer(g, rx, ry, 0, 0) on every position change (9380), independent of button state - the only path that yields button-free MotionNotify, and only to the grab holder. (B) No-grab path: the pointer is fed to LVGL's indev (mouse_read_cb 9565-9593, PRESSED iff ptr_pressed, which tracks BTN_LEFT/BTN_TOUCH only, 9266-9272); the client's lv_image is subscribed only to PRESSED/RELEASED/PRESS_LOST/PRESSING (5221-5231), and xwin_ptr_cb (3977-3998) emits act 1 / act 2 / act 0 respectively, always as button 1. Since LVGL raises PRESSING only while the indev is pressed, and LVGL's own HOVER_OVER/LEAVE are crossing-only events that lvdesk does not subscribe to (lv_indev.c:1465-1489), an ungrabbed client gets MotionNotify - and, because Enter/Leave are generated inside xshim_pointer (xshim.c ~8935-8970), EnterNotify/LeaveNotify too - only while Button1 is down. Right/middle/wheel go through xwin_send_button (3847-3897) as press/release only, never motion, and that path is disabled while fs_active (3872). Real X delivers PointerMotion and crossings to whatever selected them under the pointer with no button requirement. Affected: any windowed client relying on ungrabbed motion or Enter/Leave: OpenTyrian (SDL 1.2, starts ungrabbed and reads mouse_x/mouse_y from absolute SDL_MOUSEMOTION for its menus), xcalc/Xt-Xaw hover highlight (EnterWindow translations), sdlkeys without grab, SDL2 clients with relative mode off (menus with cursor shown). Explicitly NOT affected and NOT explained by this: fullscreen prboom/TyrQuake (grab path A carries motion) and Chocolate Doom's keyboard - those need a different root cause. Fix belongs in lvdesk mouse_poll: when no grab is held and not fs_active, hit-test xwins[] like xwin_send_button does and call xshim_pointer(id, rx, ry, 0, 0) on each position change (dedupe as g_x/g_y does), leaving Button1 press/release on the LVGL path so chrome and click-to-focus keep working; xshim's Enter/Leave and motion-fold (xshim.c:3074-3120) then work unchanged.

result.reasoning:
Every code fact in C5 checks out line by line, but the mechanism cannot produce any observed symptom, including the "secondary" one it claims, so as a root cause it is refuted.

Facts confirmed: xlite/xlite_req.c:3184-3198 XQueryPointer returns True with everything 0 and no request; :3200-3207 XQueryKeymap memsets 32 zero bytes; xlite/xlite_key.c:210-221 XGetModifierMapping is all zeros; lvdesk/xshim.c:7064-7082 answers QueryPointer correctly from ptr_root_x/y (set at 8905-8906) and ptr_btn_state; `grep -n 'case 44' lvdesk/xshim.c` is empty (QueryKeymap unhandled). SDL2 2.32.10 X11_ReconcileKeyboardState (SDL_x11events.c:403-450) does release every SDL-pressed scancode the zero keymap denies, and it runs from X11_InitKeyboard (SDL_x11keyboard.c:335), X11_DispatchFocusIn (SDL_x11events.c:458) and KeymapNotify (:917). xshim sends FocusIn/FocusOut from xshim_focus (xshim.c:9194-9206), and SDL2 does XSetInputFocus when net_wm is false (SDL_x11window.c:1173-1178) which xshim maps to xshim_focus (xshim.c:7679-7681).

Why it does not bite:
1. Timing. The reconcile can only release a key SDL believes pressed at the moment it runs. Init (SDL_x11keyboard.c:335) precedes any key event. FocusIn is dispatched only 200 ms after it arrives (SDL_x11window.h:30, SDL_x11events.c:1060-1061, 1624-1632), so the initial FocusIn of a game window is reconciled before the player presses anything. KeymapNotify is never sent by xshim (`grep -n KeymapNotify lvdesk/xshim.c` empty), so :917 never runs.
2. No mid-game re-send. xshim_focus dedups by id (`if (id == focused) return;` xshim.c:9197), so lvdesk calling win_set_focus on the already-focused game window (lvdesk.c:2804, 3773 make_window, 5133) emits nothing. Every other xshim_focus/win_set_focus caller (lvdesk.c:2820, 2823, 3016, 3184, 3255, 3411, 3482, 3678, 3887, 6534, 6776, 9560, 10132) is a user action on the desktop (title click, taskbar, switcher, ctl menu) or boot-time. The claim "lvdesk re-sends focus" during a game has no code path.
3. Even a real focus change is parity with a real X server. A focus change slower than 200 ms dispatches FocusOut first, and SDL_SetKeyboardFocus(NULL) calls SDL_ResetKeyboard (SDL_keyboard.c:771-773) on any server, so the held key is lost identically on real X. Only a FocusOut->FocusIn bounce within 200 ms (pending state overwritten, :1056-1061, :1089-1094) would reach the reconcile with keys still pressed; nothing in lvdesk does that automatically.
4. Self-healing. xlite reports DetectableAutoRepeat unsupported (xlite_key.c:141-147) and the observed KeyPress storms show the server repeats presses; SDL2's SDL_SendKeyboardKey turns a press on a released scancode into a fresh KEYDOWN (SDL_keyboard.c:846-855), so even a reconcile release would be undone at the next autorepeat. Worst case is one KEYUP/KEYDOWN blip per focus change, not a keyboard that "does not work properly at all".
5. Pointer side. SDL2 reaches XQueryPointer only via X11_GetGlobalMouseState (SDL_x11mouse.c:412-457), called only from SDL_GetGlobalMouseState (SDL_mouse.c:1038-1055); Chocolate Doom's i_video.c/i_input.c and OpenTyrian's src do not call it (grep empty), and no other SDL2 core path calls it. SDL 1.2's two uses are X11_UpdateMouse (SDL_x11video.c:1279-1296, run once from SDL_SetVideoMode via SDL_video.c:761-762; the 0,0 motion is one absolute event) and X11_SetKeyboardState (SDL_x11events.c:1310-1395), which runs once from X11_SetVideoMode (SDL_x11video.c:1190) and otherwise only on KeymapNotify (SDL_x11events.c:510-514), never sent. So TyrQuake's dead mouse and Chocolate Doom's keyboard are untouched by these two functions. Our own tree has no XQueryPointer/XQueryKeymap caller either (grep of xlite/, lvdesk/, xtlite/ shows only the implementations).

Net: real, cheap-to-fix latent defects (XQueryPointer should be the opcode-38 round trip xshim already answers; XQueryKeymap should track decode()'s KeyPress/KeyRelease), but not a cause of today's observations, primary or secondary.

result.reasoning:
Every code fact in C5 checks out, but the mechanism cannot fire in steady-state play, so it does not produce any of the observed symptoms.

1. The cited xlite behaviour is real: XQueryPointer fills root/child/x/y/mask with 0 and returns True without any request (xlite/xlite_req.c:3184-3198); XQueryKeymap memsets 32 zero bytes (xlite_req.c:3200-3207); XGetModifierMapping returns an all-zero map (xlite/xlite_key.c:210-221). xshim does answer opcode 38 for real from ptr_root_x/y and ptr_btn_state (lvdesk/xshim.c:7064-7082, set at 8901-8906), and opcode 44 (QueryKeymap) appears only in the opcode-name table (xshim.c:2073) with no handler.

2. SDL2's reconcile is exactly as described (sdl2-2.32.10/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:403-450) and with an all-zero keymap the else-branch at 447-449 sends SDL_RELEASED for every scancode SDL believes down. But it is only reached from three places: X11_InitKeyboard (SDL_x11keyboard.c:335, before any key can be down), X11_DispatchFocusIn (SDL_x11events.c:452-458), and KeymapNotify (SDL_x11events.c:912-918) - and xshim never emits event type 11 (grep KeymapNotify / send_event_d(...,11 in lvdesk/xshim.c: no hits). So the only live trigger is FocusIn.

3. FocusIn is deduplicated at the source. xshim_focus() keeps a static `focused` and returns immediately when id == focused (xshim.c:9192-9197). For a freshly created game window lvdesk calls xshim_focus(id) once the xid is known (lvdesk.c:5126-5134) and SDL2's X11_ShowWindow XSetInputFocus (SDL_x11window.c:1173-1178, taken because net_wm is only set TRUE when _NET_SUPPORTING_WM_CHECK yields a wm_window, SDL_x11video.c:391-398, and xshim exports no such atom) hits opcode 42 -> xshim_focus(same id) -> dedup (xshim.c:7679-7681). Net result: exactly one FocusIn, delivered while SDL's keystate is empty, so the reconcile loop releases nothing. SDL2's other XSetInputFocus sites (SDL_x11window.c:1047 X11_SetWindowInputFocus, 1076 X11_SetWindowBordered) target the same window and are also deduped. A second FocusIn needs a genuine change of lvdesk's focused top-level (clicks on another window at lvdesk.c:3184/3883/9560, minimise/close via win_focus_next 2814-2824, terminal launch 10132, or the now-latched fullscreen path 5918-5924). None of those occur during ordinary Chocolate Doom play, so "keyboard does not work properly at all" cannot come from this path. xlite does deliver FocusIn/FocusOut correctly (default decode sets xany.window, xlite/xlite.c:239-241; mode/detail zero = NotifyNormal/NotifyAncestor, which SDL2 accepts at SDL_x11events.c:1037-1058), so the mechanism is not blocked - it simply has nothing to release.

4. Control from the working app: SDL 1.2 does the identical thing. X11_SetKeyboardState(display, NULL) calls XQueryKeymap and XQueryPointer and zeroes the whole SDL key state (sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:1310-1345), run from SDL_SetVideoMode (SDL_x11video.c:1190) and otherwise only on KeymapNotify (SDL_x11events.c:514, never sent). prboom's keyboard works, confirming a zero keymap at a moment when nothing is held is a no-op.

5. XQueryPointer 0,0 is inert for these clients: SDL2 uses it only in the reconcile (modifier lock bits, and X11_GetNumLockModifierMask is 0 anyway because XGetModifierMapping is zeros) and in X11_GetGlobalMouseState (SDL_x11mouse.c:434-447), which SDL2 core reaches only via the public SDL_GetGlobalMouseState (src/events/SDL_mouse.c:1038-1055); no call to SDL_GetGlobalMouseState exists in chocolate-doom-3.1.1/src or the opentyrian source (grep: no hits). SDL 1.2's X11_UpdateMouse (SDL_x11video.c:1284) posts a harmless 0,0 motion inside the surface, as the candidate itself notes. It cannot explain TyrQuake's dead mouse motion, which never goes through XQueryPointer.

So C5 is accurate about the code but is not a cause of (a), (b) or (c). What survives is a latent defect: a key held across a real focus change (user clicks another lvdesk window, minimises, or a window closes) is spuriously released in SDL2 clients, and SDL_GetGlobalMouseState would return 0,0 if any client called it.

In that last case any key SDL believes held is spuriously released. SDL_GetGlobalMouseState would return 0,0 but no shipped SDL2 app calls it, and SDL 1.2 uses the same zero keymap once at SetVideoMode (prboom works). This is a correctness gap worth fixing (client-side 32-byte bitmap maintained from KeyPress/KeyRelease in xlite/xlite.c decode; real opcode-38 round trip for XQueryPointer), but it is not a cause of the Chocolate Doom keyboard failure, the TyrQuake dead mouse, or anything else observed on 2026-09-23.

result.reasoning:
C3's trigger does not exist in SDL 1.2. The claim is that for an app that never called SDL_WM_GrabInput, `this->input_grab == SDL_GRAB_OFF`, so the FocusIn 1.5 s timer's `X11_GrabInputNoLock(this, this->input_grab)` (sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:976) becomes XUngrabPointer+XUngrabKeyboard (SDL_x11wm.c:338-340) and the grab is dropped for good. That premise is false line by line:

1. SDL_SetVideoMode itself forces input_grab to SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN. It saves the grab (SDL_video.c:677 `saved_grab = SDL_WM_GrabInputOff()`, which returns OFF for a fresh app), sets the mode, then calls `SDL_WM_GrabInput(saved_grab)` (SDL_video.c:764). SDL_WM_GrabInput adds SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN whenever `SDL_VideoSurface->flags & SDL_FULLSCREEN` (SDL_video.c:1893-1899; SDL_VideoSurface was assigned the new fullscreen mode at :707). SDL_WM_GrabInputRaw then, because input_grab is still OFF, calls the driver `video->GrabInput(this, mode=2)` and stores `video->input_grab = mode` (SDL_video.c:1847-1857). `input_grab` is written nowhere else (`grep "input_grab *="` over src/video: only SDL_video.c:1856). SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN == 2 (include/SDL_video.h:923-928), which is not SDL_GRAB_OFF.

2. So when the FocusIn timer fires, X11_GrabInputNoLock receives 2, takes the ELSE branch (SDL_x11wm.c:342-358): XUngrabPointer then XGrabPointer(SDL_Window, owner=True, confine SDL_Window) retried until GrabSuccess, then XGrabKeyboard. That is a RE-GRAB, not a release. The proposal's own log test ("XUngrabPointer ~1.5 s after the grab with no XGrabPointer following") cannot occur for any fullscreen SDL 1.2 client, with or without an SDL_WM_GrabInput call. xshim handles the pair correctly: UngrabPointer clears grab_win/grab_cli (xshim.c:7190-7196) and the immediate GrabPointer by the same client succeeds (xshim.c:7177-7186, grab_cli is -1).

3. Corroboration that this line-764 grab IS the one observed: the X11_EnterFullScreen grabs cited by C3 (SDL_x11modes.c:1002 and :1067) are no-ops during SDL_SetVideoMode, because `SDL_VideoSurface` is a macro for `current_video->screen` (src/video/SDL_sysvideo.h:420), which SDL_SetVideoMode sets to NULL at SDL_video.c:680 before calling video->SetVideoMode (:681), and X11_GrabInputNoLock returns SDL_GRAB_OFF immediately when `this->screen == NULL` (SDL_x11wm.c:332-334). Hence exactly ONE XUngrabPointer+XGrabPointer pair appears in the trace for both prboom and TyrQuake, and the existing xshim logs show one "pointer grabbed by" per fullscreen run and one "released" only at exit (artifacts/sdlbench/extended/sdl1-fullscreen-r1.log:224-225, artifacts/sdlbench/20260919-172317/sdl1-doom_frame-r1.log:195-196).

4. The prboom "survives because I_StartTic re-issues SDL_WM_GrabInput(ON)" argument is also wrong: with input_grab already 2 (or 3), SDL_WM_GrabInputRaw's non-OFF branch only calls the driver when `video->input_grab == SDL_GRAB_OFF` (SDL_video.c:1851-1853), so prboom's per-tic call does nothing at the X level; prboom and TyrQuake are in the identical SDL grab state. The symptom difference between them therefore cannot come from this mechanism. (`sdlkeys without grab` in affected_apps is also wrong: rootfs/sdlkeys.c:18-19 calls SDL_WM_GrabInput(SDL_GRAB_ON).)

5. The lvdesk half is accurately quoted (pointer in fullscreen only via a live grab: lvdesk.c:9351-9366, 3864-3865, 9591-9592) but is inert without the trigger. Note also xshim never implements core ReparentWindow (`->parent` assigned only at creation, xshim.c:6413; no opcode-7 arm in the core request switch), so top_of(SDL_Window) stays WMwindow, and xshim_mode_window's "fits" rule returns the client's last-created qualifying top-level (xshim.c:9234-9250) - WMwindow at 320x200 - so `g == fs_win` at lvdesk.c:9355 is satisfied and pointer events are delivered while the grab lives, which is what prboom shows.

6. The FocusOut-at-FSwindow-map race that C3 mentions in passing is real code (make_window -> win_set_focus(rec) with rec->xid still 0 -> xshim_focus(0) sends FocusOut to WMwindow, lvdesk.c:3773, 2804, xshim.c:9199-9200; SDL then queues X11_LeaveFullScreen after 200 ms, SDL_x11events.c:483-497, 968-975, which ungrabs via SDL_x11modes.c:1130 with mode 2&~2 = OFF), but its symptom is a VISIBLE exit from fullscreen (FSwindow unmapped, "xshim: video mode 800x480"), not silent "keys but no mouse", and the TyrQuake session stayed fullscreen. It is a different bug and does not rescue C3.

result.corrected_mechanism: There is no "SDL drops its implicit fullscreen grab 1.5 s after lvdesk's FocusIn" mechanism. What actually happens: SDL_SetVideoMode(...|SDL_FULLSCREEN) ends with SDL_WM_GrabInput(saved_grab) (SDL_video.c:764), which stores input_grab = SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN (2) for every fullscreen SDL 1.2 client and issues the single XUngrabPointer+XGrabPointer(SDL_Window, owner=1, confine=SDL_Window) seen in the traces (the X11_EnterFullScreen grabs are skipped because this->screen is NULL during the mode set). Every later FocusIn on WMwindow re-arms the 1.5 s timer, and when it fires X11_GrabInputNoLock(this, 2) performs XUngrabPointer immediately followed by XGrabPointer on the same window (SDL_x11wm.c:342-358); xshim releases and re-grants the grab within one request batch (xshim.c:7177-7196), so xshim_grab_top() stays non-zero across the desktop's polls except for a sub-millisecond window, and lvdesk's fs_active-gated pointer path (lvdesk.c:9351-9366) keeps delivering. Whether an app called SDL_WM_GrabInput is irrelevant (SDL_video.c:1851-1853 makes prboom's per-tic call a no-op once input_grab is non-OFF). The only genuine focus-related hazard in this code is different and visible: lvdesk's make_window for FSwindow calls win_set_focus before rec->xid is set (lvdesk.c:3773 -> 2804 -> xshim_focus(0)), sending FocusOut to WMwindow, which queues X11_LeaveFullScreen 200 ms later (ungrab, unmap FSwindow, mode restore) unless the first-fullscreen-draw refocus (lvdesk.c:5875-5924) delivers FocusIn to WMwindow first; that produces an exit from fullscreen, not keys-without-mouse, and did not occur in the TyrQuake session. TyrQuake's dead mouse must be explained elsewhere (C2).

result.reasoning:
The two factual premises C7 rests on are both wrong, and its failure mode does not match what was observed.

1. The slot-order argument fails. res_new (lvdesk/xshim.c:762-777) is first-free for EVERY allocation, not just WMwindow's. SDL creates FSwindow first (sdl-1.2.15 SDL_x11video.c:352) and WMwindow second (:387) on the same connection, so any hole an earlier client left is visible to the FSwindow allocation too: FSwindow takes the lowest hole and WMwindow necessarily lands in a higher one. Between the two CreateWindow requests only XInternAtom/XSendEvent/XGetWMHints and, on a re-call, XDestroyWindow(old WMwindow) (:382) run. The re-call path (only when vis_change, SDL_x11video.c:1019-1020) destroys the old FSwindow first (:339), so new-FS slot <= old-FS slot < old-WM slot, and SDL_Window was already destroyed by X11_DestroyWindow (:738-740) before that, so res_free_tree(old WMwindow) (xshim.c:6544-6572, :805-813) frees only a slot above the new FSwindow's. By induction WMwindow's slot is always above FSwindow's for a single client. The only residual path is another X client freeing a resource into a lower slot during the client's XInternAtom/XGetWMHints round-trips (a few ms); games are launched by appmenu_spawn with no terminal X client in between (lvdesk/lvdesk.c:6540-6560) and lvdesk hosts xshim in-process rather than being a client, so 'after any earlier client freed resources' is not a trigger.

2. The grab premise is wrong. SDL 1.2 grabs on SDL_Window with confine_to SDL_Window (SDL_x11wm.c:352-354), not on FSwindow; xlite prints raw ids (xlite_req.c:2346-2348), so 'FSwindow' in the trace is the observer's label. xshim_grab_top returns top_of(grab window) if mapped (xshim.c:9275-9287, 9289-9309), and top_of(SDL_Window) == WMwindow because the reparent is a no-op on both sides (xlite/stubs.c:610-615 sends nothing; xshim only names opcode 7 in its opstr table at xshim.c:2059 and has no core case). xshim_mode_window's 'fits' rule (xshim.c:9218-9260) resolves to WMwindow by the same ordering, so fs_win and the grab top agree and mouse_poll's `g == fs_win` branch (lvdesk.c:9355-9358) holds. This is exactly why prboom's mouse works.

3. Symptom mismatch. If fs_win were FSwindow, xwin_on_draw would never present (lvdesk.c:5927) and the picture would freeze along with the pointer. Today's TyrQuake had a live picture, working keys and a dead mouse in the same lvdesk session where prboom worked, and C7 itself says it does not explain today's traces. It also cannot account for the absence of XDefineCursor and of recentering warps in TyrQuake - those are client-side calls (SDL_ShowCursor -> XDefineCursor; recentering in SDL_x11events on MotionNotify with mouse_relative), not routing.

Real but harmless: ReparentWindow is unimplemented. Because it is a no-op consistently, SDL_Window stays under WMwindow and both the presented top-level and the grab top-level are WMwindow. Implementing reparenting without also changing fs_win selection would make the 800x480 FSwindow (SDL_x11modes.c:1013-1019 sizes it to MAX(window, real, screen)) the presented and grabbed top-level, which is riskier than the status quo; not a fix candidate for the observed bugs.

result.reasoning: The lvdesk half of C6 holds line by line. lvdesk/lvdesk.c:5221-5231 registers xwin_ptr_cb on the client image for LV_EVENT_PRESSED, RELEASED, PRESS_LOST and PRESSING only; xwin_ptr_cb (lvdesk.c:3977-3998) maps PRESSED->act 1, RELEASED/PRESS_LOST->act 2 and everything else (i.e. PRESSING) to act 0 motion, always with button=1. LVGL sends LV_EVENT_PRESSING only inside indev_proc_press (lvgl/src/indev/lv_indev.c:1415) and LV_EVENT_HOVER_OVER/LEAVE only when the hovered OBJECT changes (lv_indev.c:1353, 1466-1489), so there is no per-move LVGL event lvdesk could be receiving while the button is up. The only other callers of xshim_pointer are xwin_send_button (lvdesk.c:3847-3897: Button2/3/4/5 press/release only, and returns 0 outright when fs_active, :3864) and the grab branch of mouse_poll (lvdesk.c:9346-9408), which reports motion on every position change (:9379-9383) but only to xshim_grab_top(). mouse_read_cb (lvdesk.c:9591) reports RELEASED whenever a grab is held OR fs_active, so the PRESSING path is dead in those states too. On the shim side, MotionNotify is emitted only from xshim_pointer act 0 (lvdesk/xshim.c:8984) and EnterNotify/LeaveNotify are emitted only inside xshim_pointer (xshim.c:8936-8973). Net: an ungrabbed windowed client receives MotionNotify and crossing events only while Button1 is held; an ungrabbed FULLSCREEN client receives no pointer events at all. Client side: SDL 1.2 selects PointerMotionMask on SDL_Window (sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11video.c:1058-1061) and in non-relative mode posts absolute motion from MotionNotify (SDL_x11events.c:519-541); SDL2 posts MotionNotify motion when !relative_mode or relative_mode_warp (sdl2-2.32.10/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:1367-1375); Xaw Command's default translations are "<Enter>: highlight() / <Leave>: reset()" (xlib_libXaw-1.0.16/src/Command.c:105-109), so xcalc buttons cannot highlight on hover here. The affected-app list is overstated, however. OpenTyrian is built by Buildroot with the `release` goal (buildroot/package/opentyrian/opentyrian.mk:22-28), which defines NDEBUG (opentyrian Makefile:24-28), so input_grab_enabled defaults to true (src/keyboard.c:43-47), SDL_WM_GrabInput is compiled in (keyboard.c:108-110), video.c:145 applies it at init, SDL_WM_GrabInput has no focus deferral (SDL_video.c:1870-1899) and xshim's GrabPointer succeeds unless another client already holds it (xshim.c:7169-7186). OpenTyrian therefore runs on the grab path, and it re-grabs on the first SDL_MOUSEBUTTONDOWN (keyboard.c:211-215); it only shows C6's symptom between a focus loss (keyboard.c:142-144 calls input_grab(false) on SDL_APPINPUTFOCUS loss) or Ctrl+F10 and the next click. Chocolate Doom's SDL_SetRelativeMouseMode (chocolate-doom-3.1.1/src/i_video.c:268) counts as a mouse grab in SDL2 while the window has input focus (sdl2 SDL_video.c:3003), so during play it is grabbed too. C6 also does not produce any of today's three observations: prboom and TyrQuake hold successful grabs and get motion from the grab path regardless of buttons (TyrQuake's dead mouse is not this), and Chocolate Doom's complaint is keyboard. result.corrected_mechanism: While no client holds a pointer grab, lvdesk routes the pointer only through LVGL's indev, and the client image's callback is registered for PRESSED/RELEASED/PRESS_LOST/PRESSING (lvdesk.c:5221-5231); LVGL emits PRESSING only while the button is down (lv_indev.c:1415) and has no per-move released-state event, so xshim_pointer(id,x,y,1,0) - the only source of MotionNotify (xshim.c:8984) and of EnterNotify/LeaveNotify (xshim.c:8936-8973) - runs only during a Button1 drag. Consequences: (1) an ungrabbed windowed client with PointerMotionMask sees motion and crossing events only while Button1 is held; (2) Xt/Xaw hover behaviour (Command <Enter>:highlight(), Command.c:105-109) never fires until a click; (3) an ungrabbed FULLSCREEN client gets no pointer events at all, because mouse_read_cb forces RELEASED when fs_active (lvdesk.c:9591) and xwin_send_button returns 0 when fs_active (lvdesk.c:3864). Real X delivers PointerMotion/Enter/Leave to whatever window selected them under the pointer, button state notwithstanding. Scope correction: OpenTyrian (release build, NDEBUG) grabs at init and re-grabs on the first click, so it only shows a frozen menu pointer between a focus loss or Ctrl+F10 and the next click; Chocolate Doom is grabbed while focused and playing (relative mode == grab in SDL2). The affected set is therefore Xt/Xaw clients (xcalc hover), SDL 1.2/SDL2 windows running with grab off (sdlkeys before grab_at, prboom windowed ungrabbed, OpenTyrian after focus loss), and any fullscreen client whose XGrabPointer failed or was never issued. This defect does not produce any of today's three observations (prboom OK, TyrQuake dead mouse under a successful grab, Chocolate Doom keyboard), which lie elsewhere. Fix stays as sketched: in mouse_poll's no-grab branch, hit-test xwins[] the way xwin_send_button does and call xshim_pointer(id, rx, ry, 0, 0) on each position change (dedupe like g_x/g_y), including when fs_active for the fullscreen window; leave Button1 on the LVGL path.

result.reasoning:
The two factual anchors hold: XReparentWindow is a no-op stub (xlite/stubs.c:610-615) and xshim's core switch (lvdesk/xshim.c:6131) has no case 7 (the only core mention is the opstr name table at xshim.c:2059; the case 7s at 4840/5642/8142 are RENDER/SHM/RANDR minors). It is also true that xshim_mode_window (xshim.c:9218-9260) lets the LAST res[] slot win among mapped top-levels of vm_cli that fit the mode, that both candidates fit (WMwindow is resized to the mode size before mapping, sdl-1.2.15 SDL_x11video.c:1036; FSwindow is MoveResized to >= screen size, SDL_x11modes.c:1016-1019), and that res_new takes the first free slot (xshim.c:761-777). But the hypothesis fails on the two claims that make it a bug:

1. The trigger is wrong. A first-free allocator preserves creation order between two allocations unless a slot BELOW the first one is freed in between. On a second launch, or after any client has exited, FSwindow takes the lowest free slot and WMwindow the next lowest free slot, which is necessarily higher - the order cannot flip from prior exits alone. Within the same client the only free between the two creates is the XDestroyWindow(old WMwindow) on aux-window recreation (SDL_x11video.c:380-383), and that slot is higher than the old FSwindow slot (destroyed at :339-340 just before the new FSwindow was allocated), so it cannot invert either. The only way to invert is a DIFFERENT client's client_drop (xshim.c:9140-9142, reached from the hangup checks at 9383-9389 / 9488-9491) landing inside the XInternAtom("KWM_KEEP_ON_TOP") round trip at SDL_x11video.c:369-370 (xlite's XInternAtom really blocks on a reply, xlite/xlite_req.c:50-70), i.e. another X client must disconnect during a ~1 ms window on every launch it affects. 'Every SDL 1.2 fullscreen client on a second or later launch' is not what the code does.

2. The consequence is wrong. Even with fs_win = FSwindow, the pointer does not die. X11_CreateWindow maps WMwindow and waits for it BEFORE X11_EnterFullScreen (SDL_x11video.c:1109-1115); xshim fires win_cb for every mapped top-level with no fullscreen gating (xshim.c:6620-6621) and xwin_on_window (lvdesk.c:5054-5180) has no fs_active test, so WMwindow already has an xwins entry with an img. The grab is on SDL_Window (SDL_x11wm.c:352-354), top_of(SDL_Window) = WMwindow (xshim.c:816-823, reparent being a no-op), so in mouse_poll g = WMwindow, the fallback at lvdesk.c:9364-9369 finds its img and xshim_pointer(g, rx, ry) still runs - motion and buttons arrive, merely clamped to the WMwindow's desktop-frame coordinates rather than the mode. Picture would indeed stall (xwin_on_draw at lvdesk.c:5927 presents only id == fs_win), but that is a frozen screen, not the observed 'keys work, mouse dead, picture fine' TyrQuake signature.

3. It does not touch today's observations, and says so itself: TyrQuake shows no recentering warps and no motion with a WORKING picture, which this mechanism cannot produce (a wrong fs_win freezes the display first). The propagation point about FSwindow selecting only StructureNotify (SDL_x11video.c:359, xshim.c:8828-8845) is moot because the grab is never on FSwindow.

Net: a real but very narrow latent race in fs_win selection, with an incorrect trigger and an overstated symptom; not a cause of any observed keyboard/mouse failure.

result.reasoning:
Every link in the chain checks out against the actual source, and it produces exactly the asymmetric symptom (SDL 1.2 keyboard fine, SDL2 keyboard broken on the same lvdesk/xshim/xlite).

Our side: xshim's connection setup writes min keycode 8 / max 255 (lvdesk/xshim.c:2564-2565). xlite copies those bytes verbatim into pub.min_keycode/max_keycode (xlite/xlite.c:773-774) and XDisplayKeycodes hands them back unchanged (xlite/xlite_req.c:2023-2029). The wire contract puts Return, BackSpace, Tab, Escape, Delete, Left, Up at 1..7 (xlite/xlite_wirekeys.h:17-23); lvdesk's xkey_sym returns those XLW_ values for KEY_ENTER/BACKSPACE/TAB/ESC/DELETE/LEFT/UP (lvdesk/lvdesk.c:430-439) and xshim_key sends the byte as the event detail with no remapping (lvdesk/xshim.c:9014-9043, `send_device_event(c, ..., (uint8_t)sym, ...)`). XKeycodeToKeysym is xlw_widen (xlite/xlite_key.c:100-105), XKeysymToKeycode is xlw_narrow (xlite/xlite_key.c:506-511), XkbQueryExtension returns False (xlite/xlite_key.c:129-140). No other consumer of min_keycode exists in xlite/xtlite/lvdesk (grep: only the two xlite sites).

SDL2 2.32.10 side: X11_InitKeyboard calls X11_XkbQueryExtension and only sets data->xkb on success (SDL_x11keyboard.c:159-167), so data->xkb stays NULL and X11_KeyCodeToSym falls to X11_XKeycodeToKeysym (SDL_x11keyboard.c:97-132). The fingerprint (Home, Prior, Up, Left, Delete, KP_Enter; SDL_x11keyboard.c:140-152) computes XKeysymToKeycode - min_keycode = 10-8, 12-8, 7-8, 6-8, 5-8, 15-8 = 2, 4, -1, -2, -3, 7 (SDL_x11keyboard.c:227-231); the three negatives alone give distance >= 3 for every table, so best_distance > 2 regardless of table contents (SDL_x11keyboard.c:232-249); the XF86Documents rescue narrows to 0 and 0-8 != 235 (SDL_x11keyboard.c:250-261). The else branch therefore runs `for (i = min_keycode; i <= max_keycode; ++i) data->key_layout[i] = X11_KeyCodeToSDLScancode(_this, i)` starting at 8 (SDL_x11keyboard.c:302-325 in this tree, loop at ~306). key_layout is SDL_Scancode[256] inside SDL_VideoData (SDL_x11video.h:126), which is SDL_calloc'd (SDL_x11video.c:180), so key_layout[1..7] stays SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN (0). On KeyPress/KeyRelease the handler sends SDL_SendKeyboardKey(..., videodata->key_layout[keycode]) (SDL_x11events.c:1150, 1160) and SDL_SendKeyboardKeyInternal returns 0 immediately for SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN (src/events/SDL_keyboard.c:822-826): no SDL_KEYDOWN/KEYUP is ever queued for those seven keys. Had the loop covered 1..7, the widened keysyms would have mapped, because LinuxKeycodeKeysyms contains 0xFF1B Escape, 0xFF08 BackSpace, 0xFF09 Tab, 0xFF0D Return, 0xFF52 Up, 0xFF51 Left, 0xFFFF Delete (SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:63, 76, 77, 90, 165, 167, 173) and SDL_GetScancodeFromKeySym scans that table (SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:390-435). Codes >= 8 (Right 0xFF53 at :168, Down 0xFF54 at :170, F-keys, modifiers, letters) do map, so Right/Down/letters/Ctrl/Alt/Shift work while Escape/Enter/Up/Left/Backspace/Tab/Delete are dead - a Doom that cannot open its menu, confirm anything, move forward or turn left, i.e. "does not work properly at all".

Chocolate Doom 3.1.1 keys off sym->scancode via scancode_translate_table and drops data1 == 0 (src/i_input.c:105-131, 244-259), but that never even matters here because SDL2 posts no key event at all for these keycodes.

SDL 1.2 contrast holds: X11_TranslateKeycode calls XKeycodeToKeysym(display, kc, 0) per event, Latin-1 -> xsym & 0xFF, 0xFF page -> MISC_keymap (sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:1119-1163); grep for XDisplayKeycodes/min_keycode across sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/*.c returns nothing (rc=1). So prboom, tiopex-quake and OpenTyrian (buildroot/package/opentyrian/opentyrian.mk:12 `OPENTYRIAN_DEPENDENCIES = sdl`, :25 sdl-config) are untouched; rootfs/tyr-quake is an SDL2 build (rootfs/build-tyrquake.sh:2, 22-23 `-I.../SDL2 -lSDL2`) and is affected. The SDL2 config in this tree confirms the paths taken: SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER_X11_HAS_XKBKEYCODETOKEYSYM 1 and X11 loaded dynamically as libX11.so.6 (include/SDL_config.h:397, 413).

The claim survives line by line and it is the one mechanism that distinguishes SDL2 from SDL 1.2 on identical wire traffic.

The release path (lvdesk.c:1156-1177) calls xkey_sym(ev.code) at release time with whatever `shift` is then (updated on the modifier's own event at :1114-1115), and the press path (:1194 kbd_key -> :840-849 xshim_key(grab_top, sym, 1, mods)) does the same at press time; there is no per-key cache of the press-time sym (grep for held/down_sym/pressed[]: none). xshim_key (xshim.c:9018, :9044-9045) puts `sym` unchanged into `detail` and `mods & 0x0F` into state. xlite widens 0x20-0x7E to itself (xlite_wirekeys.h:72-79: xlw_lo covers 0-31, xlw_hi 128-132), XKeycodeToKeysym ignores index (xlite_key.c:100-105), XLookupString returns the folded byte and applies only Control (:184-208), XkbLookupKeySym reports Shift as consumed (:481-496), XGetKeyboardMapping reports per_code=1 identity (xlite_req.c:2031-2049).

Only 0x24 ($) is in the extended table (:368) and it maps to KEY_DOLLAR -> SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN (scancodes_linux.h:464). Key events use key_layout[keycode] (SDL_x11events.c:1150, :1160) and SDL_SendKeyboardKeyInternal drops SCANCODE_UNKNOWN (SDL_keyboard.c:824-826). Chocolate Doom TranslateKey (i_input.c:105-131) indexes SCANCODE_TO_KEYS_ARRAY (doomkeys.h:94-118) by scancode, and its stock bindings are key_strafeleft=',' key_straferight='.' key_speed=KEY_RSHIFT (m_controls.c:34-39); prboom's are the same (m_misc.c:425-436). So with STOCK bindings the case that is hit in every game is run+strafe: Shift+',' arrives as '<' and Shift+'.' as '>' - SDLK_LESS/SDLK_GREATER (K_LESS/K_GREATER in tiopex vid_sdl.c:340/346, 60/62 in prboom) and NONUSBACKSLASH/UNKNOWN in SDL2 - none of which is the bound strafe key, and pressing Shift while a strafe key is held then leaves it stuck. Letter breakage (WASD) requires letter bindings in the card's cfg (not readable now; overlay chocolate-fullscreen.cfg has no key_* lines) or Caps Lock on. It would not by itself produce 'keyboard does not work properly at all' with arrow-key defaults, which the claim already concedes (C1 is primary); it is a real, verified secondary defect.

result.corrected_mechanism: lvdesk sends the Shift/Caps-folded Latin-1 character as the X keycode (lvdesk.c:474-481) and recomputes it independently at press and at release with the modifier state current at that instant (:1156-1177 vs :840-849), while also reporting ShiftMask/LockMask in the event state (:486-487, xshim.c:9018). xlite treats keycode==keysym with no per-index lookup (xlite_key.c:100-105) and tells XkbLookupKeySym callers Shift is already consumed (:481-496). Consequences, all verified in the client sources: (1) SDL 1.2 maps Latin-1 keysyms as `xsym & 0xFF` (SDL_x11events.c:1142) and keeps key state per SDLKey (SDL_keyboard.c:535-546); shifted or caps-locked letters become SDLKey 65-90, which are not SDLK members, so tiopex-quake drops them as K_UNKNOWN (vid_sdl.c:616) and prboom passes them through as Doom keys 65-90 (i_video.c:152) that match no lowercase binding; a Shift transition while a key is held makes the release carry a different keycode than the press, so the pressed SDLKey is never released (SDL_keyboard.c:538-541 drops the mismatched release). (2) SDL2 builds key_layout from XKeycodeToKeysym per keycode (SDL_x11keyboard.c:322-340, fingerprint branch provably unreachable because xlw_narrow gives XK_Up/Left/Delete codes 5-7 < min_keycode 8) and normalises only 0x41-0x5A (SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:402-404): shifted letters survive, but '>' '!' '@' '#' etc. are absent from its tables and become SCANCODE_UNKNOWN (dropped at SDL_keyboard.c:824), '<' becomes NONUSBACKSLASH (:148), and '$' -> KEY_DOLLAR -> UNKNOWN (scancodes_linux.h:464); a release arriving with a shifted punctuation keycode leaves SCANCODE_COMMA/PERIOD pressed. (3) With the STOCK Doom/Quake bindings (m_controls.c:34-39, m_misc.c:425-436, Quake +speed on Shift) the case actually hit is run+strafe: Shift+','/'.' arrive as '<'/'>' and are not the bound strafe key in prboom, tiopex-quake or Chocolate Doom, and a strafe key held across a Shift press sticks. Letter (WASD) breakage needs letter bindings in the card's cfg or Caps Lock on. This is a secondary contributor, not the primary 'Chocolate Doom keyboard does not work at all' cause. Fix as sketched: lvdesk sends keymap[code][0] with no caps inversion and keeps Shift/Caps in state bits; xlite applies Shift/Lock itself in XLookupString/Xutf8LookupString/XkbLookupKeySym (and stops reporting Shift consumed), honours index 1 in XKeycodeToKeysym, and reports per_code=2 from XGetKeyboardMapping.

result.corrected_mechanism: lvdesk resolves Shift and Caps into the wire keycode at the instant of each evdev event: xkey_sym() (lvdesk.c:471-482) returns keymap[code][shift?1:0] with caps inversion, and it is called with the live modifier state both on press (kbd_key, :840-849) and on release (:1156-1177). xshim forwards that byte as the X keycode (xshim.c:9042) and xlite's keysym APIs are identity on it (XKeycodeToKeysym ignores index, XGetKeyboardMapping per_code=1, XLookupString/XkbLookupKeySym treat Shift as already applied). Consequences: (1) SDL 1.2 (prboom, tiopex-quake, OpenTyrian, sdlkeys): X11_TranslateKeycode maps Latin-1 as sym = xsym & 0xFF, so Shift+w arrives as sym 87, which is not an SDLKey (gap 65-90 in SDL_keysym.h). tiopex's switch has only SDLK_a..z so it becomes K_UNKNOWN (+speed and forward cannot coexist); prboom passes 87 through as Doom key 'W' (default: rc = key->sym), which no default bind uses, and its default strafe keys ','/'.' become '<'/'>' under run. If Shift changes state while a key is held, the release carries a different code than the press; SDL_PrivateKeyboard's no-change filter drops it and SDL_KeyState[original sym] stays pressed - and also drops the next same-state press, so the key stays stuck until an unshifted release of that key. (2) SDL2 (Chocolate Doom): SDL2 falls into the 'layout unknown' branch (xlite's XKeysymToKeycode narrows the fingerprint keysyms to XLW_ low codes), so key_layout[keycode] = SDL_GetScancodeFromKeySym(keysym=keycode). Uppercase letters are normalised to lowercase so Shift+letter survives, but shifted punctuation/digit keysyms ('!' '@' '>' '<' ...) are absent from LinuxKeycodeKeysyms and the custom list, so they map to SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN, which SDL_SendKeyboardKey discards: Shift+'.' (run+strafe right) produces no key event, and '.' released while Shift is held leaves SDL_SCANCODE_PERIOD pressed. Fix is as sketched: lvdesk sends the level-0 code (keymap[code][0], no caps folding) and keeps Shift/Lock in the state mask, and xlite applies Shift/Lock itself in XLookupString/Xutf8LookupString/XkbLookupKeySym (stop reporting Shift consumed), honours index 1 in XKeycodeToKeysym/XkbKeycodeToKeysym, and reports per_code=2 in XGetKeyboardMapping; xtlite already matches level-0 keysym plus ShiftMask (xtlite.c:966-967). Not the primary Chocolate Doom failure but a genuine, code-proven secondary defect affecting every Shift-to-run game.

result.corrected_mechanism: lvdesk pre-applies Shift and Caps to the character it sends as the X keycode (lvdesk.c:474-481: keymap[code][shift] plus case inversion) AND also reports Shift/Lock in the event state (xkey_mods, :484-488; xshim.c:9018), and it computes the KeyRelease code from the modifier state current at release (:1170), not from the code sent on press. Real X sends one fixed keycode per physical key and lets the client apply the modifier mask, so both SDLs assume press and release carry the same keycode. Consequences, all verified in the client sources: (1) SDL 1.2 (prboom, tiopex-quake, OpenTyrian, sdlkeys): X11_TranslateKeycode maps a Latin-1 keysym to SDLKey = keysym & 0xFF (SDL_x11events.c:1141-1142), so Shift+w arrives as SDLKey 87 - not SDLK_w - and prboom's I_TranslateKey default (rc = key->sym) and tiopex's SDLK_a..z switch (default K_UNKNOWN) never match a 'w' binding; likewise Shift+'.' arrives as 62 (SDLK_GREATER) and misses prboom's default key_straferight '.', so strafing while running (key_speed = RSHIFT) is dead. A key pressed before and released after a Shift transition gets two different syms; SDL_PrivateKeyboard drops the release as a no-change event (SDL_keyboard.c:536-540) and SDL_KeyState[original sym] stays PRESSED - a stuck key. (2) SDL2 (Chocolate Doom, tyr-quake, sdl2keys): key_layout[] is built per X keycode from the level-0 keysym; SDL_GetScancodeFromKeySym folds 0x41-0x5A to lowercase (SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:402-404) so shifted LETTERS are fine, but shifted punctuation and digit keysyms (0x21 '!', 0x3E '>', 0x40 '@', 0x23 '#' ...) are absent from LinuxKeycodeKeysyms and the custom list, map to SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN, and SDL_SendKeyboardKeyInternal discards them (SDL_keyboard.c:824-826): Shift+digit produces no KEYDOWN, and '.' pressed then released with Shift held loses its release so SCANCODE_PERIOD sticks. xtlite is unaffected because it matches the folded keysym plus ShiftMask. Small correction to the claim: SDLK_EXCLAIM=33 does exist in SDL 1.2, so Shift+1 there is a named-but-wrong key (SDLK_EXCLAIM instead of SDLK_1 + KMOD_SHIFT) rather than an unnamed one; the game-level effect (no binding matches) is identical. Fix as sketched: lvdesk sends the level-0 character (keymap[code][0], no Caps inversion) with Shift/Lock only in state, and xlite applies Shift/Lock itself in XLookupString/Xutf8LookupString/XkbLookupKeySym (stop reporting Shift consumed), honours index 1 in XKeycodeToKeysym/XkbKeycodeToKeysym, and reports per_code=2 from XGetKeyboardMapping.

In xshim.c, xshim_pointer (:8889) is the only producer of EV_MOTION (:8984) and of Enter/Leave (:8940-8975), and its only in-server caller is the WarpPointer handler (:7273). So without a grab, a windowed client receives MotionNotify only between ButtonPress and ButtonRelease of Button1, and crossing events only at those moments. Client side: SDL 1.2 selects PointerMotionMask on SDL_Window (sdl-1.2.15 SDL_x11video.c:1058-1061) and, non-relative, posts absolute SDL_PrivateMouseMotion from MotionNotify (SDL_x11events.c:519-539); OpenTyrian in this tree is SDL 1.2 (keyboard.c:107-110 uses SDL_ShowCursor/SDL_WM_GrabInput, grab only under NDEBUG and only when enable||fullscreen) and reads menu mouse position from SDL_MOUSEMOTION (keyboard.c:147-150), so windowed/ungrabbed its mouse cursor freezes until a click. SDL_Window is a child of WMwindow (SDL_x11video.c:1051) and never leaves it, so xshim_grab_top() = top_of(SDL_Window) = WMwindow always. fs_win = WMwindow iff WMwindow's slot > FSwindow's slot. So far C4 is right that correctness depends on slot order.

2. Why the slot reversal cannot happen. create_aux_windows always (re)creates FSwindow FIRST and WMwindow SECOND: XDestroyWindow(FSwindow) :338-339, XCreateWindow(FSwindow) :352, then XGetWMHints+XDestroyWindow(WMwindow) :381-382, XCreateWindow(WMwindow) :387. With first-free-slot allocation, FSwindow takes the lowest free slot at its allocation; for WMwindow to land BELOW it a slot lower than FSwindow's must be freed between the two allocations. The only same-client frees between them are res_free_tree(WMwindow_old) (its slot is above FSwindow_old >= FSwindow_new by induction from the very first creation, and its child SDL_Window was already destroyed in X11_DestroyWindow, SDL_x11video.c:738-740, before create_aux_windows runs at :1018-1019). The claim's own code_test ("allocates the new WMwindow into the lowest free slot, which is below FSwindow if any lower slot was freed") is self-refuting: any such lower free slot is consumed by the FSwindow re-creation that precedes it. "A launch after another X client has exited" therefore does NOT change the order - the freed low slots go to FSwindow first, WMwindow next. The only residual path is another client freeing a resource in the ~2 round-trips (XInternAtom :369, XGetWMHints :381) between the two creates - a sub-10 ms cross-client race, not a repeatable "works once, not the next time" mechanism. The re-create path itself runs only when vis_change (SDL_x11video.c:958, :1019), i.e. an 8-bpp client's first SetVideoMode; it does not run again on subsequent mode sets with the same visual.

Stale-grab leg refuted. client_drop clears grab_win/grab_cli and kgrab when the holder disconnects (xshim.c:9079-9086) and also releases vm_cli (:9087-9088); xshim_grab_top() drops a grab whose window is destroyed or unmapped (:9275-9298, grab_live requires cli fd >= 0 and top mapped), and lvdesk calls it every mouse_poll pass (lvdesk.c:9347). result.corrected_mechanism: Outside an X pointer grab, lvdesk delivers pointer MOTION to an X client only through LVGL's LV_EVENT_PRESSING on the client image (lvdesk.c:3977-3997, registered :5221-5231), which LVGL emits only while the indev is in the PRESSED state and only to the object where the press began. xwin_ptr_cb turns that into xshim_pointer(id, x, y, 1, 0), so xshim emits MotionNotify (type 6, selected by PointerMotionMask = EV_MOTION bit 6, xshim.c:8767/8973) with Button1Mask set. Because EnterNotify/LeaveNotify are generated solely inside xshim_pointer (xshim.c:8944-8973), crossing is also reported only at a press. Consequences, per app in THIS tree: OpenTyrian (SDL 1.2 here: SDL_SetVideoMode video.c:106, SDL_WM_GrabInput compiled in via -DNDEBUG) reads absolute SDL_MOUSEMOTION for its menus (keyboard.c:147-149) and grabs only on the first SDL_MOUSEBUTTONDOWN (keyboard.c:211-215), dropping the grab on focus loss (:142-144): its cursor is frozen until the first click and again after any focus loss, then tracks via the grab path. Any other windowed client that expects hover motion or Enter/Leave without a button held is affected. Fix shape stands: in mouse_poll's no-grab branch, when the pointer moved and no button is down, hit-test xwins[] like xwin_send_button (skipping when fs_active) and call xshim_pointer(id, ptr_x-a.x1, ptr_y-a.y1, 0, 0) for the window under the pointer; xshim's crossing block then emits Leave/Enter itself, and xshim_flush already coalesces the motion. SDL 1.2 calls XKeycodeToKeysym per event and never consults min_keycode (sdl-1.2.15 SDL_x11events.c:1119-1142), which is why prboom and the other SDL 1.2 apps (incl. OpenTyrian, built against 'sdl'/sdl-config per opentyrian.mk:12,25) keep a working keyboard. result.reasoning:
The lvdesk half of C3 checks out, but the SDL 1.2 half does not, and without it the mechanism produces no symptom.

Our side (verified): in fullscreen lvdesk routes pointer motion/buttons only through xshim_grab_top() (lvdesk/lvdesk.c:9347-9353, delivery via xshim_pointer at :9376-9400), xwin_send_button returns 0 when fs_active (:3864-3865), and the LVGL indev is told RELEASED when fs_active (:9591-9592). xshim clears grab_win on UngrabPointer (lvdesk/xshim.c:7191-7196) and xshim_focus/send_focus deliver FocusIn/FocusOut to any window in the top-level that selected EV_FOCUS (xshim.c:9171-9205). So yes: a fullscreen SDL 1.2 client with no live grab would get keys but no pointer.

Client side (refuted): the claim is that an app which never called SDL_WM_GrabInput has input_grab == SDL_GRAB_OFF, so the 1.5 s post-FocusIn timer path X11_GrabInputNoLock(this, this->input_grab) (SDL_x11events.c:976-977) runs the mode==OFF branch and executes XUngrabPointer/XUngrabKeyboard (SDL_x11wm.c:338-341). That premise is false for a fullscreen surface. SDL_SetVideoMode saves and clears the grab (SDL_video.c:677, SDL_WM_GrabInputOff) and after the driver mode set calls SDL_WM_GrabInput(saved_grab) at SDL_video.c:764 with saved_grab == SDL_GRAB_OFF. SDL_WM_GrabInput (SDL_video.c:1892-1899) does: "If the video surface is fullscreen, we always grab" - `if (SDL_VideoSurface && (SDL_VideoSurface->flags & SDL_FULLSCREEN)) mode += SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN;` so mode becomes SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN (= 2, SDL_video.h:927). SDL_WM_GrabInputRaw (SDL_video.c:1846-1857) then, since mode != OFF and input_grab == OFF, calls video->GrabInput (X11_GrabInput -> X11_GrabInputNoLock(2), which XUngrabPointer + XGrabPointer(SDL_Window, confine SDL_Window) + XGrabKeyboard(WMwindow), SDL_x11wm.c:342-355) and stores `video->input_grab = mode` = SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN (SDL_video.c:1855-1856). The SDL_FULLSCREEN flag is set on the surface by X11_CreateWindow before this (SDL_x11video.c:1113-1114) and SDL_VideoSurface = mode at SDL_video.c:707, so the condition holds.

Consequently, when the FocusIn timer fires (SDL_x11events.c:465-479 queue, 950-983 fire), X11_EnterFullScreen returns early (SDL_x11modes.c:995-997) and X11_GrabInputNoLock(this, this->input_grab) is called with mode == SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN (2), not OFF. That takes the else branch at SDL_x11wm.c:342: XUngrabPointer (because screen is fullscreen) immediately followed by XGrabPointer(SDL_Window...) in a retry loop and XGrabKeyboard. The pointer grab is re-established in the same request stream; xshim's grab_win is cleared by case 27 and set again by the following GrabPointer. There is never a bare XUngrabPointer ~1.5 s after FocusIn, and the grab does not go dead. SDL itself documents this: SDL_x11modes.c:1125-1130 "input_grab will still have the SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN flag set ... release the grab unless the input has been explicitly grabbed" - the FULLSCREEN bit lives in input_grab precisely so that focus handling keeps the grab while fullscreen; only X11_LeaveFullScreen masks it off (input_grab & ~SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN).

The prboom explanation in C3 is likewise wrong: with input_grab already == SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN, prboom's SDL_WM_GrabInput(SDL_GRAB_ON) becomes GrabInputRaw(3), which does NOT call the driver (input_grab != OFF, SDL_video.c:1851) and merely stores 3; prboom does not "re-grab on level entry", so its working mouse cannot be attributed to that. The FocusOut path (SDL_x11events.c:483-497) does lead to X11_LeaveFullScreen + GrabInputNoLock(OFF) after 200 ms, but that is a different, already-known mechanism (lvdesk.c:3852-3865 comment) and is not the one C3 proposes; it also would drop the app out of fullscreen entirely, which is not the TyrQuake observation (fullscreen stays up, keys keep arriving, no ungrab in the trace).

Net: the SDL 1.2 implicit fullscreen grab is not dropped 1.5 s after FocusIn; lvdesk's grab-only fullscreen delivery therefore stays fed for any SDL 1.2 fullscreen app, and C3 cannot explain TyrQuake's missing motion/buttons. The fix sketch (fallback g = fs_win when no grab) is harmless but addresses a state this code path never reaches.

result.reasoning:
The claim's load-bearing step is "input_grab == SDL_GRAB_OFF when the app never called SDL_WM_GrabInput, so the 1.5 s FocusIn timer runs X11_GrabInputNoLock(OFF) and ungrabs". That is false for any fullscreen SDL 1.2 surface. SDL_SetVideoMode saves the grab state with SDL_WM_GrabInputOff() (SDL_video.c:677), sets the mode, then restores it with SDL_WM_GrabInput(saved_grab) (SDL_video.c:764). SDL_WM_GrabInput, under the comment "If the video surface is fullscreen, we always grab", strips any SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN bit and then ADDS it whenever SDL_VideoSurface->flags & SDL_FULLSCREEN (SDL_video.c:1892-1898), so saved_grab=OFF (0) becomes SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN (2, SDL_video.h:927). SDL_WM_GrabInputRaw then takes the non-OFF branch: input_grab is OFF so it calls video->GrabInput(this, 2) and stores video->input_grab = 2 (SDL_video.c:1850-1856). Hence after a fullscreen SDL_SetVideoMode, this->input_grab is SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN, never OFF, whether or not the application ever calls SDL_WM_GrabInput.

Trace the FocusIn timer with that value: SDL_x11events.c:465-479 queues switch_waiting=0x01|SDL_FULLSCREEN; at expiry X11_PumpEvents (:968-981) calls X11_EnterFullScreen (early return at SDL_x11modes.c:997-999) then, because go_fullscreen is set, X11_GrabInputNoLock(this, this->input_grab) with input_grab=2. In X11_GrabInputNoLock (SDL_x11wm.c:328-380) mode != SDL_GRAB_OFF, so it takes the else branch: XUngrabPointer then loop XGrabPointer(SDL_Window, owner_events=True, confine=SDL_Window) until GrabSuccess, then XGrabKeyboard(WMwindow). The grab is re-established in the same request stream, not dropped. xshim's UngrabPointer clears grab_win (xshim.c:7189-7196) and the immediately following GrabPointer sets it again (:7181-7187); lvdesk's mouse_poll (lvdesk.c:9346-9400) polls xshim_grab_top() per tick and sees a live grab. The claim's own code_test signature - a bare "xlite: XUngrabPointer()" ~1.5 s after "xshim: pointer grabbed by" with no following XGrabPointer - cannot be produced by this path, and the observed TyrQuake trace (grab -> 0, then nothing) does not show it either.

The "prboom survives because I_StartTic re-grabs via SDL_WM_GrabInput(ON)" corollary is also wrong. prboom's call (prboom-2.5.0/src/SDL/i_video.c:230-235) goes through SDL_WM_GrabInput, which in fullscreen maps ON->3 and OFF->2; SDL_WM_GrabInputRaw only calls the driver on a transition to or from OFF (SDL_video.c:1847-1853), and input_grab is never OFF in fullscreen, so prboom's toggles never reach X11_GrabInput at all. prboom's mouse works because the entry-time grab persists, exactly as it would for TyrQuake. The only SDL 1.2 paths that actually release the X grab in fullscreen are a FocusOut (SDL_x11events.c:483-497 -> 200 ms -> X11_LeaveFullScreen + X11_GrabInputNoLock(SDL_GRAB_OFF), SDL_x11events.c:971-979), which leaves fullscreen entirely rather than silently dropping the pointer, and the grab client/window going away (xshim.c grab_live :9275-9287). lvdesk already guards the FocusOut case: xwin_on_draw prefers the grab holder's top-level for focus (lvdesk.c:5895-5924) and win_set_focus refuses any other window while fs_active (:2794-2797); FSwindow selects only StructureNotifyMask (SDL_x11video.c:359) and SDL_Window no focus mask (:1058), so only WMwindow can receive FocusIn/FocusOut via send_focus (xshim.c:9171-9190).

What does hold: lvdesk's fullscreen pointer delivery is grab-only (lvdesk.c:9346-9400 has no fs_win fallback when xshim_grab_top() returns 0; xwin_send_button returns 0 while fs_active at :3864-3865; mouse_read_cb reports RELEASED at :9591-9592). That is an accurately described latent gap, but SDL 1.2 fullscreen clients never exercise it because they always hold a grab, so it does not explain the TyrQuake "keys but no mouse" symptom (which the claim itself concedes is masked by C2) nor any other observation listed. The proposed fix (g = fs_win fallback) would be harmless but addresses a case no SDL 1.2 fullscreen app reaches.

C3's load-bearing premise is that an SDL 1.2 fullscreen app which never calls SDL_WM_GrabInput has `this->input_grab == SDL_GRAB_OFF`, so that when the FocusIn-armed 1.5 s timer fires, `X11_GrabInputNoLock(this, this->input_grab)` (SDL_x11events.c:975-976) takes the `mode == SDL_GRAB_OFF` branch and issues XUngrabPointer/XUngrabKeyboard (SDL_x11wm.c:338-341). That premise is false in SDL 1.2.15: SDL_SetVideoMode itself leaves input_grab at SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN (=2, SDL_video.h:927), a non-OFF value, whenever the surface is fullscreen.

The chain, line by line: SDL_SetVideoMode saves the grab with `saved_grab = SDL_WM_GrabInputOff()` (SDL_video.c:677), which queries input_grab with the FULLSCREEN bit stripped (:1882-1886) - SDL_GRAB_OFF for an app that never grabbed - and forces the raw state OFF. After the driver mode set, `SDL_VideoSurface = mode` (:707) and then `SDL_WM_GrabInput(saved_grab)` (:764). SDL_WM_GrabInput(SDL_GRAB_OFF) does `if (SDL_VideoSurface->flags & SDL_FULLSCREEN) mode += SDL_GRAB_FULLSCREEN;` (:1896-1897; the flag was set by X11_SetVideoMode at SDL_x11video.c:1112-1113 before X11_EnterFullScreen), so mode becomes 2 and SDL_WM_GrabInputRaw(2) runs: mode != OFF and input_grab == OFF, so `video->GrabInput(this, 2)` is called (:1851-1852); X11_GrabInputNoLock returns its `mode` argument unchanged (SDL_x11wm.c:378; `this->screen` is non-NULL because SDL_VideoSurface is `current_video->screen`, SDL_sysvideo.h:420, assigned at :707), so `video->input_grab = 2` (:1855-1856). The comment at :1892 says it outright: "If the video surface is fullscreen, we always grab."

Consequence for the timer: when the FocusIn-queued switch fires (SDL_x11events.c:952-976), X11_EnterFullScreen returns early on currently_fullscreen (SDL_x11modes.c:997-999) and X11_GrabInputNoLock(this, 2) takes the ELSE branch (SDL_x11wm.c:342-366): XUngrabPointer on the FS window, then XGrabPointer(SDL_Window, owner=True, confine=SDL_Window) in a retry loop, then XGrabKeyboard. Net effect is a re-grab, not a release. xshim sees release-then-grab within one request burst; lvdesk's grab-only fullscreen pointer path (lvdesk.c:9346-9400) keeps a live grab top. So the proposed mechanism cannot go silent 1.5 s after FocusIn.

It also cannot be turned off by the app while fullscreen: SDL_WM_GrabInput(SDL_GRAB_OFF) in fullscreen becomes mode 2 (:1893-1897), and GrabInputRaw(2) with input_grab already 2 calls nothing and changes nothing (:1846-1858). So the claim's affected-app list is wrong too: prboom's explicit SDL_WM_GrabInput(OFF) at title/menu/paused (prboom-2.5.0/src/SDL/i_video.c:226-233) does not drop the grab either, and tiopex quake (tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/vid_sdl.c:145 calls SDL_ShowCursor(0) and never SDL_WM_GrabInput) sits in exactly the "implicit grab" class and still has input_grab = 2 after SetVideoMode. OpenTyrian in the Buildroot tree is SDL2 (opentyrian-cf5dbe.../src/keyboard.c:109 is a compat call), so it is out of scope for an SDL 1.2 mechanism anyway.

Shifted digits/punctuation ('!','>',...) arrive as their own SDLK_ values, which the games treat as different keys from '1','.'. OUR SIDE. lvdesk/lvdesk.c:379-407 keymap[KEY_CNT][2] holds {'w','W'}, {'1','!'} etc. xkey_sym (lvdesk.c:471-482) returns keymap[code][shift ? 1 : 0] and then inverts letter case under mod_caps, so the WIRE keycode is the shifted/caps-folded character. xkey_mods (lvdesk.c:486-488) additionally sets bit 0 (ShiftMask) and bit 1 (LockMask). The press path is kbd_key (lvdesk.c:840-848): sym = xkey_sym(code) -> xshim_key(top, sym, 1, xkey_mods()). The release path (lvdesk.c:1156-1174) RE-COMPUTES xkey_sym(ev.code) with the modifier state current at release time, so 'w down, Shift down, w up' is press 0x77 / release 0x57. `shift` is updated from KEY_LEFTSHIFT/RIGHTSHIFT at lvdesk.c:1107-1109 before the key itself is delivered. xshim_key (xshim.c:9013-9020) forwards sym as the event detail with st = (mods & 0x0F) | ptr_btn_state. xlite decodes the detail byte unchanged into keycode (xlite.c:186-194, "The keycode keeps the WIRE value"), and every keysym API is an identity: XKeycodeToKeysym ignores index and returns xlw_widen(kc) (xlite_key.c:100-105), XLookupString returns xlw_widen(ev->keycode) and only folds Control (xlite_key.c:184-208), XkbLookupKeySym reports ShiftMask as already consumed (xlite_key.c:481-496), XGetKeyboardMapping reports per_code=1 identity (xlite_req.c:2031-2049), min/max keycode are 8/255 (xshim.c:2564-2565).

SDL 1.2 (container sdl-1.2.15). X11_TranslateKeycode is called PER EVENT for KeyPress (SDL_x11events.c:570, :731) and KeyRelease (:770); it calls XKeycodeToKeysym(display, kc, 0) (:1124) and for Latin-1 does key = (SDLKey)(xsym & 0xFF) (:1141-1142). SDLKey has no members 65..90 ("Skip uppercase letters", include/SDL_keysym.h:75-77) so Shift+w arrives as sym 87, not SDLK_w (119). SDL_PrivateKeyboard indexes SDL_KeyState[keysym->sym] and DROPS a release whose state already matches (src/events/SDL_keyboard.c:535-546), so a release under a different keysym never clears the pressed entry - the stuck key is real. prboom's I_TranslateKey falls through to rc = key->sym (prboom-2.5.0/src/SDL/i_video.c:93, default at +59 lines) so 87 reaches the game as a key nothing is bound to; the SDL 1.2 TyrQuake (tyrquake/sdlquake-master/source/vid_sdl.c:114 uses SDL_SetVideoMode) maps only SDLK_a..z (:373-450) and defaults to K_UNKNOWN (:616-618). Shift itself IS delivered (XLW_SHIFT_L=28 -> 0xFFE1 -> MISC_keymap -> SDLK_LSHIFT, i_video.c maps SDLK_LSHIFT/RSHIFT -> KEYD_RSHIFT), and arrows are XLW codes untouched by Shift, which is exactly why prboom with default arrow bindings 'works' while Shift+letter is broken.

SDL2 (container sdl2-2.32.10). XkbQueryExtension returns False so data->xkb is NULL and X11_KeyCodeToSym uses XKeycodeToKeysym(...,0) (SDL_x11keyboard.c:124-128). The fingerprint pass cannot pick a scancode table: Escape/Return/Delete narrow to wire codes 4/1/5, below min_keycode 8, so their values are negative and distance is 4 for every table (:224-244, threshold <=2), hence key_layout is built per keycode from SDL_GetScancodeFromKeySym (:309-323). That function lowercases 0x41-0x5A (SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:402-404) so shifted LETTERS map to the same scancode as unshifted - the press/release mismatch does NOT stick letters in SDL2 (a correction to C4's wording). Shifted punctuation (0x21 '!' etc.) is in none of KeySymToSDLScancode (:29-56), LinuxKeycodeKeysyms (:61+, base keysyms only) or the extended table, so it yields SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN and SDL_SendKeyboardKeyInternal returns 0 (SDL_keyboard.c:824-826) - no KEYDOWN for Shift+digit, and a digit released while Shift is held leaves keystate[SCANCODE_n] set (release of UNKNOWN is dropped). Chocolate Doom's TranslateKey is scancode-based (chocolate-doom-3.1.1/src/i_input.c:105-134) so it is exposed to exactly that.

Caveat, as the claim itself states: this does not explain observation (a) TyrQuake's dead mouse or (b) Chocolate Doom's keyboard being broken 'at all'. Side finding while checking (b): SDL2's key_layout loop runs i = min_keycode(8)..max_keycode (SDL_x11keyboard.c:309-323), so wire codes 1-7 (XLW_RETURN, BACKSPACE, TAB, ESCAPE, DELETE, LEFT, UP; xlite_wirekeys.h:17-23) are never mapped and stay SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN; X11_HandleKeyEvent sends key_layout[keycode] (SDL_x11events.c ~1150/1160) and UNKNOWN is dropped (SDL_keyboard.c:824). That would make Return, Escape, Tab, Backspace, Left and Up dead in every SDL2 app while letters work - a much better fit for 'Chocolate Doom keyboard does not work properly at all' than C4, and fixable in xshim (report min keycode 1) or by moving those wire codes above 8.

result.corrected_mechanism: lvdesk folds Shift (and Caps) into the wire keycode: xkey_sym returns keymap[code][shift] with caps inversion (lvdesk.c:471-482), both on press (kbd_key, :840-848) and, recomputed from the modifier state current at release time, on release (:1156-1174). xlite exposes that byte unchanged as keycode AND as the index-0 keysym (xlite_key.c:100-105, :184-208, :481-496; xlite_req.c:2031-2049 per_code=1). Consequences, verified in the client sources: (1) SDL 1.2 translates every KeyPress/KeyRelease through XKeycodeToKeysym(kc,0) and maps Latin-1 as key = xsym & 0xFF (SDL_x11events.c:1124,1141-1142), so Shift+letter (or any letter with Caps on) is sym 65..90, which no SDLKey names (SDL_keysym.h:75-77) - prboom passes it through as a bogus key (i_video.c default rc=key->sym), TyrQuake 1.2 maps it to K_UNKNOWN (sdlquake-master vid_sdl.c:373-450,616-618); and because SDL_KeyState is indexed by sym and a release whose state is unchanged is dropped (SDL_keyboard.c:535-546), 'w down, Shift down, w up' (release arrives as 'W') leaves SDLK_w pressed for good. Shift itself and the XLW arrows are unaffected, which is why prboom with arrow bindings looks fine. (2) SDL2 builds key_layout per keycode from SDL_GetScancodeFromKeySym because the fingerprint pass fails (wire codes 1,4,5 for Return/Escape/Delete are below min_keycode 8; SDL_x11keyboard.c:224-244,309-323); shifted letters are lowercased there (SDL_keysym_to_scancode.c:402-404) so letters neither vanish nor stick in SDL2 - but shifted punctuation/digits ('!' '@' '#' ... '<' '>' '?' ':' '"' '{' '}' '|' '~' '_' '+') is in none of SDL2's tables, so Shift+digit produces SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN (no KEYDOWN, SDL_keyboard.c:824-826) and a digit released while Shift is held is a release of UNKNOWN, leaving keystate[SCANCODE_n] set. The X-correct fix is as sketched: send the unshifted base character as the keycode from lvdesk and carry Shift/Lock only in state, have xlite's XLookupString/Xutf8LookupString/XkbLookupKeySym apply ShiftMask/LockMask through a US shift table so text clients still receive 'A' and '!', make XKeycodeToKeysym honour index (0 base, 1 shifted) and XGetKeyboardMapping return per_code=2. An xlite-only unfold table would fix the keysym but not the press/release mismatch. Note this is a secondary defect: it does not account for TyrQuake's dead mouse or the bulk of Chocolate Doom's keyboard failure; for the latter, the separate finding that SDL2 never maps wire keycodes 1-7 (Return, Backspace, Tab, Escape, Delete, Left, Up) because its layout loop starts at min_keycode=8 (xshim.c:2564; SDL_x11keyboard.c:309-323) is the stronger candidate.

The core mechanism survives line-by-line verification, with two corrections and one explicit scoping.

CONFIRMED (SDL 1.2, sdl-1.2.15): X11_TranslateKeycode uses XKeycodeToKeysym(display, kc, 0) and maps Latin-1 as key = xsym & 0xFF (src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:1119-1142); both KeyPress branches (:559-572 non-UNICODE, :720-748 XLookupString branch; the XIM branch is unreachable because xlite XOpenIM is a stub returning 0, xlite/stubs.c:554-559) and KeyRelease (:752-778) go through it. SDLKey has no members 65..90 ("Skip uppercase letters", include/SDL_keysym.h:75-77: SDLK_AT=64 then SDLK_LEFTBRACKET=91). SDL_KeyState is indexed by sym (src/events/SDL_keyboard.c:33, :537-546) and a release whose sym is already 0 is DROPPED ("Drop events that don't change state"), so 'w' down (sym 119) / Shift down / 'w' up (arrives as 'W', sym 87) leaves SDL_KeyState[119] pressed. Worse than stated: the key-repeat timer is only cancelled when the release sym matches (:522-526), so SDL_CheckKeyRepeat (:573-594) keeps re-posting the 'w' KEYDOWN after the physical release in any app that called SDL_EnableKeyRepeat. tiopex-quake IS built from tyrquake/sdlquake-master (rootfs/build-tiopex.sh:2; scripts/board/quake-timedemo.sh:14) whose vid_sdl.c maps only SDLK_a..SDLK_z (:373-448) with default K_UNKNOWN (:616-617), so sym 87 is a dead key. prboom passes unknown syms straight through (prboom-2.5.0/src/SDL/i_video.c:152 `default: rc = key->sym`), so 'W'=87 is a different Doom key from 'w'=119. CORRECTION 1 (SDL2 over-claimed): SDL2 builds key_layout per keycode from SDL_GetScancodeFromKeySym(xlw_widen(kc), kc) (SDL_x11keyboard.c:75-83, :311-325 - the fingerprint match at :225-255 fails because XKeysymToKeycode returns xlw_narrow values 1/4/5/15 below min_keycode 8, so the "layout unknown" branch runs). The SDL2 defect is confined to the digit/punctuation rows: '!' '@' '#' etc. are in neither KeySymToSDLScancode (:31-56) nor LinuxKeycodeKeysyms/ExtendedLinuxKeycodeKeysyms (no 0x21 entry), so :436 returns SDL_GetScancodeFromTable(LINUX, 0) = SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN, SDL_SendKeyboardKey returns 0 for it (SDL_keyboard.c:824-825), and 'press 1, press Shift, release 1' (arrives as '!') leaves SDL_SCANCODE_1 pressed (SDL_x11events.c:1150/1160).

CORRECTION 2: OpenTyrian in this tree is SDL2 (opentyrian-cf5dbeb… built against sdl2-2.32.10; the task statement also says SDL2), not SDL 1.2 as listed under affected_apps.

result.reasoning:
The static facts in C5 are real but the failure mechanism built on them does not hold, and the consequence chain is wrong in two places.

(1) The trigger is arithmetically impossible as stated. res_new (lvdesk/xshim.c:761-777) is first-free, and SDL creates FSwindow then WMwindow back to back inside create_aux_windows (sdl-1.2.15 SDL_x11video.c:352 then :387). Two consecutive first-free allocations always yield slot(FSwindow) < slot(WMwindow) unless a slot BELOW FSwindow's is freed between the two XCreateWindow requests. "A previous client exiting" or "an SDL_SetVideoMode that destroys/recreates windows" frees slots BEFORE FSwindow is allocated, so FSwindow takes the lowest freed slot and WMwindow the next one - order preserved. Inside create_aux_windows the only free between the two creates is XDestroyWindow(old WMwindow) at :382, whose slot was allocated after the old FSwindow's (and the new FSwindow at :339/:352 took a slot <= the old FSwindow's), and whose child SDL_Window was already destroyed by X11_DestroyWindow (:739, SDL_GC freed :760) before create_aux_windows is re-run (:1020). The only remaining window is a different client exiting during the XInternAtom round trip at :371 (xlite_req.c:51-71 blocks in xlite_reply) while holding lower slots - a microsecond race, not the "works once, not the next time" shape claimed. The proposed code test ("res[] with a freed low slot, create FSwindow then WMwindow, call xshim_mode_window") returns WMwindow, not FSwindow.

(2) The claimed consequence "the have gate fails (no xwins img exists in fullscreen)" is false. xwins[] entries are created at map time by make_window (lvdesk.c:5119, 5180) with img created unconditionally (5200); fullscreen only stops rendering the desktop (fs_render_set(0), lvdesk.c:4164) and hides the frame (LV_OBJ_FLAG_HIDDEN, 5192). So at 9362-9366 the loop finds g with an img and have=1; motion and buttons would still be delivered to WMwindow, merely clamped to the frame rect instead of the mode rect. Even under the (impossible) slot inversion the mouse would degrade, not vanish.

(3) The claim that "an FSwindow target would hit-test FSwindow ... dropped in send_device_event" is false: lvdesk passes g = xshim_grab_top() itself as the top to xshim_pointer (lvdesk.c:9348, 9380-9400), so top_of(grab_win) == top always holds at xshim.c:8917-8926 and FSwindow is never the hit-test root in the grab path.

(4) It does not produce today's symptoms, which C5 concedes: both observations were single-launch sessions; the TyrQuake trace shows the grab succeeded (-> 0) and keys reached the WM window, which is consistent with fs_win == grab top == WMwindow, the normal path.

What survives is only the static observation: XReparentWindow is a no-op stub (xlite/stubs.c:610-615), there is no case 7 in the core switch at xshim.c:6131 (the 'case 7:' hits at 4706/4840/5642/8142 are extension switches), so SDL_Window stays a child of WMwindow and lvdesk presents/grabs on WMwindow by creation-order fallback. That is a fragility, not the cause of missing mouse/keyboard in any observed run.

result.corrected_mechanism: XReparentWindow is a silent no-op in xlite and unimplemented in xshim, so SDL_Window remains a child of WMwindow in fullscreen; lvdesk therefore presents and routes the grab to WMwindow, chosen by xshim_mode_window's creation-order 'last fitting mapped top-level of vm_cli' rule. Because res_new is first-free and SDL always creates FSwindow immediately before WMwindow (with only a non-allocating XInternAtom round trip between them), FSwindow's slot is always below WMwindow's regardless of earlier frees; the ordering is stable across relaunches and mode changes and could only invert if a different client freed lower slots during that single round trip. Even then, the grab block would still deliver motion/buttons to WMwindow (clamped to its hidden frame rect) because xwins[].img exists from map time. This is a latent fragility of the fs_win selection rule, not a cause of the observed missing mouse in TyrQuake or the Chocolate Doom keyboard failure. result.corrected_mechanism: Without a pointer grab, lvdesk routes the pointer through LVGL's indev and the client image's xwin_ptr_cb is subscribed only to PRESSED/RELEASED/PRESS_LOST/PRESSING (lvdesk.c:5221,5229-5231); LVGL emits no per-move event in the released state (lv_indev.c:1466-1490 only HOVER_OVER/LEAVE on object change), so xshim_pointer() is called for an un-grabbed windowed client only while Button1 is held (PRESSING, lvdesk.c:3997) or on a Button2/3/wheel edge (lvdesk.c:3890). Because xshim's ptr_root_x/y, its Enter/Leave crossing state and QueryPointer are all derived solely from xshim_pointer() calls (xshim.c:8889-8905,8930-8965,7064-7080), such a client sees a frozen pointer through MotionNotify, EnterNotify and XQueryPointer alike until a click. Grabbed clients (SDL 1.2 SDL_WM_GrabInput and every SDL 1.2 fullscreen; SDL2 in relative mode once its window has input focus) take the grab path (lvdesk.c:9346-9400) and get button-independent motion, which is why games work. Additionally, a FULLSCREEN client holding no grab receives no pointer input at all - mouse_read_cb reports RELEASED whenever fs_active (lvdesk.c:9591-9592), xwin_send_button returns 0 when fs_active (:3866-3867) and the grab block needs a grab - so buttons as well as motion are lost for any fullscreen client that does not grab (unreachable by SDL 1.2, reachable by SDL2 non-relative or other clients). The fix sketch (a no-grab hover branch in mouse_poll calling xshim_pointer(top, rx, ry, 0, 0) on position change, hit-testing frames like xwin_send_button, plus the same for fs_active without a grab using the fs_win/mode rectangle) is consistent with the code as read.

result.reasoning:
The factual half of C7 holds: xlite's XQueryPointer answers constants with no request (xlite/xlite_req.c:3184-3197) and XQueryKeymap memsets 32 zero bytes (xlite_req.c:3200-3207), while xshim implements a real QueryPointer reply (lvdesk/xshim.c:7064-7082). SDL2's X11_ReconcileKeyboardState does call both (container sdl2-2.32.10/src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:414,417) and runs at init (SDL_x11keyboard.c:335), at every dispatched FocusIn (SDL_x11events.c:452-458) and on KeymapNotify (SDL_x11events.c:912-919; xshim never sends type 11 - grep 'send_event_d(.*, 11,' in lvdesk/xshim.c: not found). xlite delivers FocusIn/FocusOut through decode()'s default arm with mode=detail=0 (xlite/xlite.c:245-247), which SDL2's NotifyGrab/NotifyInferior filters pass (SDL_x11events.c:1036-1050, 1067-1083). So the reconcile does run with a zeroed keymap.

The consequence claimed - "a movement key held across any of those [FocusIns] is silently dropped" because of xlite - does not follow. SDL2 drops every held key on FocusOut by itself: X11_DispatchFocusOut calls SDL_SetKeyboardFocus(NULL) (SDL_x11events.c:472-483) and SDL_SetKeyboardFocus calls SDL_ResetKeyboard whenever focus goes to NULL (sdl2-2.32.10/src/events/SDL_keyboard.c:771-774). xshim_focus dedupes by window id and sends FocusOut to the previous holder before any new FocusIn (lvdesk/xshim.c:9192-9205, send_focus 9171-9190), so every FocusIn to a game window after its first is preceded by a FocusOut, after which SDL has no key in the PRESSED state and the reconcile's `!x11KeyPressed && sdlKeyPressed` branch (SDL_x11events.c:447-449) releases nothing. On a real X server the outcome is identical: the reconcile re-presses only modifier keys (SDL_x11events.c:427-445), never a movement key. The first FocusIn (lvdesk.c:5133 at id assignment, or the !net_wm XSetInputFocus at show, SDL_x11window.c:1173-1177 -> xlite_req.c:1662-1670 -> xshim.c:7679-7681) arrives before any key can be held. The only path where xlite's zero keymap diverges from a real server is a FocusOut followed by a FocusIn inside the 200 ms deferral (PENDING_FOCUS_TIME, SDL_x11window.h:30) while last_mode_change_deadline is set (SDL_x11modes.c:740; deferred dispatch keeps only the last pending state, SDL_x11events.c:1616-1636) - i.e. a focus flap during a mode change - and lvdesk's fs_focused latch exists precisely to stop re-focusing per frame (lvdesk.c:5906-5924). That is far too narrow to be a "contributor" to Chocolate Doom's keyboard "not working properly at all".

The XQueryPointer half is inert for SDL2 too: the reconcile uses the mask only for LockMask/NumLock/ScrollLock (SDL_x11events.c:417-421), and xshim's ptr_btn_state holds button masks only (xshim.c:355, key state builds mods separately at :9018), so a real round trip would return the same zero lock bits. X11_GetGlobalMouseState (SDL_x11mouse.c:427-457) is only reached via SDL_GetGlobalMouseState, which neither Chocolate Doom nor OpenTyrian calls (grep over chocolate-doom-3.1.1/src and opentyrian-*/src: not found); xlite has no XInput2 (xlite_req.c:1956 XQueryExtension, no XISelectEvents anywhere in xlite/*.c). SDL 1.2's X11_UpdateMouse (sdl-1.2.15/src/video/x11/SDL_x11video.c:1275-1295) runs once from SDL_SetVideoMode (SDL_video.c:761-762) and with 0,0 posts a single absolute motion to 0,0 and sets APPMOUSEFOCUS - a one-shot at mode set that cannot produce TyrQuake's persistent "view never turns" (b), nor prboom's working mouse (a), nor Chocolate Doom's keyboard (c). C7 itself concedes it explains none of the observations; the evidence shows it would not even produce the spurious-release the board test predicts, because SDL_ResetKeyboard at FocusOut fires first on any server.

The mechanism survives a line-by-line read of our side, but the affected-app list is partly wrong and it explains neither of today's two observations (the proposal concedes this).

Our side, verified: the client image registers xwin_ptr_cb only for LV_EVENT_PRESSED/RELEASED/PRESS_LOST/PRESSING (lvdesk/lvdesk.c:5221-5231); xwin_ptr_cb maps PRESSED->act 1, RELEASED/PRESS_LOST->act 2, anything else (i.e. PRESSING)->act 0 and always passes button=1 (lvdesk.c:3990-3997), so the only un-grabbed motion (act 0 -> EV_MOTION, xshim.c:8982) is generated while Button1 is held. xwin_send_button (lvdesk.c:3847-3897) sends only button acts for 2/3/4/5. The grab block in mouse_poll (lvdesk.c:9346-9400) is the sole place that calls xshim_pointer(g, rx, ry, 0, 0) on a bare position change (lvdesk.c:9380), and it runs only when xshim_grab_top() != 0. mouse_read_cb (lvdesk.c:9573-9593) only feeds LVGL's indev. LVGL cannot substitute: in the released state it emits LV_EVENT_HOVER_OVER/HOVER_LEAVE only when the object under the pointer CHANGES (lvgl/src/indev/lv_indev.c:1466-1490), never per move, and lvdesk registers neither anyway. xshim's Enter/Leave crossing events are also generated only inside xshim_pointer (xshim.c:8930-8975), so they too need a press or a grab. Net: an un-grabbed windowed client never sees MotionNotify (or Enter/Leave) unless Button1 is down. Every client here selects PointerMotionMask (SDL 1.2 SDL_x11video.c:1061; SDL2 SDL_x11window.c:681-686) and forwards un-grabbed motion as absolute (SDL 1.2 SDL_x11events.c:532-538; SDL2 SDL_x11events.c:1367-1377).

Grabbed clients are unaffected as claimed: SDL2 relative mode always results in XGrabPointer because SDL_UpdateWindowGrab sets mouse_grabbed when relative_mode is on (SDL_video.c:3002-3007, grab at SDL_x11window.c:1700-1706); here XI2 is never initialised because xshim answers every QueryExtension "not present" (xshim.c:6068, 6132), so SDL2 falls back to relative_mode_warp (SDL_mouse.c:1146-1152) - still grabbed.
