result.corrected_mechanism: No client in this stack ever asks the SERVER whether a pointer exists, and nothing in the server or desktop can 'declare' one absent. Core X has no such query; SDL2 probes only XInputExtension via XQueryExtension, which xshim answers absent (xshim.c:6132-6191), so SDL_x11xinput2.c:132-135 returns, X11_SetRelativeMouseMode fails (SDL_x11mouse.c:381-384) and SDL_SetRelativeMouseMode falls back to warp emulation (SDL_mouse.c:1148-1152), which xshim's WarpPointer-synthesised MotionNotify at the exact warp destination satisfies (xshim.c:7221-7278, 8889ff; SDL_mouse.c:558-577). SDL 1.2 DOES issue pointer requests - XQueryPointer (SDL_x11video.c:1284 from SDL_SetVideoMode via SDL_video.c:761-762; SDL_x11events.c:1329) and XGetPointerControl/XChangePointerControl (SDL_x11mouse.c:258, 273) - but xlite answers all of them locally without a round trip: XQueryPointer returns True with (0,0)/mask 0 (xlite_req.c:3184-3197), so X11_UpdateMouse always grants SDL_APPMOUSEFOCUS (needed in full_focus at SDL_x11mouse.c:229, 247-250 before relative mode is entered) and posts one absolute motion to (0,0); XGetPointerControl returns 2/1/4 and XChangePointerControl is a no-op (2421-2437). These 'declarations' are always permissive: they can only enable mouse-look, never remove motion. On the desktop side, is_mouse = REL_X && BTN_LEFT && !KEY_A (lvdesk.c:8919-8935) and keyboard = KEY_A (734-736) decide only which evdev nodes are read; REL deltas from every mouse fd are summed into the one pointer (9206-9211), so a mis-classified 8bitdo if0 adds motion, never subtracts it. 'input starved for N ms' is the time between successive kbd_poll calls (929-956), and kbd_poll runs only when a keyboard fd is readable or a rescan is due (10362, 10382, 10387; input_rescan_due 326-331), so N is the time since the last key event or hotplug - it cannot distinguish 'no key pressed' from 'the loop stalled' and is evidence of neither. 'INPUT LOST - evdev overflow on mouse fd' is a genuine SYN_DROPPED (9190-9204): the kernel client buffer is max(hint*8,64) rounded up to a power of two (evdev.c:12-13, 457-464), so lvdesk left that fd unread for at least ~64 events (~170 ms at 125 Hz); the pre-drop accumulators are zeroed, the post-drop remainder of that packet is still summed (9152-9279 has no discard-until-SYN_REPORT state), and ptr_pressed is forced to 0 without an EVIOCGKEY re-sync (none in lvdesk.c), which the grab path turns into one ButtonRelease (9383-9387). That is a transient stall and a possible one-off lost click or released fire button, not a persistent loss of the pointer. The user's 'is it how the mouse is declared?' hypothesis is therefore closed; the TyrQuake and Chocolate Doom symptoms need a different mechanism.

result.how_to_verify_on_board:
Deploy lvdesk.bin the supported way (lvdesk/build.sh -> overlay/usr/bin/lvdesk, per docs/worklog-2026-09-19.md:1299; restart the desktop) when the board is free. Then:
1. Windowed, ungrabbed motion (the fix itself): run rootfs/sdlkeys.bin WITHOUT reaching its grab_at (or before it), with XLITE_TRACE_INPUT unset (it does not print motion anyway), and inject `uinject move` with the pointer over the sdlkeys window and NO button held. Before: sdlkeys prints motion only while Button1 is down. After: it prints SDL_MOUSEMOTION with changing absolute x/y per move. Set a root cursor first and honour UINJECT_SETTLE (memory: uinject aims true only once per desktop unless UINJECT_SETTLE beats the 2 s rescan).
2. Xt hover: xcalc via xtlite - move over a button without clicking; XSHIM_TRACE=1 on lvdesk should now show `xshim: ptr act=0 -> win ...` lines and EnterNotify (type 7) per crossing while no button is down. (xtlite's highlight action is a no-op, so no visible change is expected in xcalc; the trace is the proof.)
3. OpenTyrian windowed: alt-away / Ctrl+F10 to drop its grab, then move the mouse - the menu cursor must follow without a click.
4. Regression: prboom fullscreen and TyrQuake fullscreen (grab path, unchanged) still recentre/turn as before; click on desktop chrome, drag a title bar, right-click desktop menu, click-into-xcalc-and-type all still work (Button1 windowed path is untouched). Watch lvdesk.log for any new per-move cost: xshim's motion fold means at most one MotionNotify write per loop pass per client.
result.risks:
1. LeaveNotify on exit to the bare desktop is still not generated: xshim's `inside` tracker (xshim.c ~8944) only emits Leave when a DIFFERENT window next receives a pointer event, and xshim has no API for "pointer is over root". So an Xaw button hovered then left to the desktop would stay highlighted (if a real Xt did highlighting). Out of C6's fix sketch; a follow-up would add e.g. xshim_pointer_leave() and call it when xwin_under_pointer returns -1.
2. Hit-test order is xwins[] order, not z-order (inherited from xwin_send_button, unchanged); with overlapping client windows the motion can go to the wrong one, as clicks already could. Not new.
3. Cost: one xshim_pointer() (res_find + hit_test + 32-byte staged event, folded by send_event_d) per position change per loop pass while hovering a client. No socket write until xshim_flush; expected negligible, but not measured - the board could not be touched.
4. Fullscreen-without-grab Button1 delivery is new behaviour beyond the sketch; it only fires when fs_active, fs_win resolved and xshim_grab_top()==0. Grabbed games (prboom, TyrQuake, SDL2 relative mode) never enter it. A fullscreen client whose grab failed now gets clicks, which real X would also give it.
5. This does not fix the three 2026-09-23 observations (TyrQuake dead mouse under a successful grab, Chocolate Doom keyboard - the latter is addressed by the separate xshim.c min-keycode change already in the working tree, which this lvdesk.bin includes).
6. Not deployed, not committed, board untouched; sibling working-tree edits (xshim.c, lvdesk.syms regenerated by the build) left as found.

result.summary: Made XLITE_TRACE_INPUT a complete instrument instead of a sampled one. (a) xlite/xlite_req.c XWarpPointer (~line 2410): dropped the `n++ % 50 == 0` sampler so every warp prints as "xlite: XWarpPointer #n -> win x,y"; comment records why (XDefineCursor/XGrabPointer print every call, so the sampled warp log looked complete; SDL 1.2 recentres only within 8 px of the edge per SDL_x11events.c:331-368, so 1-49 recentring warps printed identically to none, which is what the 2026-09-23 "TyrQuake never recentres" reading came from). (b) xlite/xlite.c: new static trace_input() above decode(); decode() now calls it for KeyPress/KeyRelease/ButtonPress/ButtonRelease/MotionNotify when XLITE_TRACE_INPUT is set. Keys print exactly as before ("xlite: key press kc=.. win=.."); pointer events print "xlite: motion|button press|button release #n win=0x.. x,y root rx,ry [b=N] state=0x.." - by COUNT, not sampled: the first TRACE_PTR_FULL=256 in full, then one per TRACE_PTR_EVERY=256 carrying the running number so the gap is visible. The comment records the symptom (trace could not separate "server never sent MotionNotify" from "client discarded it") with the SDL file:line. (c) XLookupKeysym returning the raw wire code was ALREADY fixed in the working tree before this task: xlite/xlite_key.c:241-245 routes through xlite_kc2ks() (xlite_key.c:154-157) which calls xlw_widen and applies the US two-level table; the task's cited lines 177-182 are HEAD's version. No change made there. No lvdesk/xshim change needed (this cause is xlite-only tooling hygiene). Nothing deployed, nothing run on the board, nothing committed.

With the env var set, motion tracing writes one stderr line per event for the first 256 pointer events (and every 256th after), each a synchronous write to a 1 Mbps console if stderr is the console - redirect stderr to a file on the card when measuring latency, or the instrument perturbs it (same class of cost as the dev_info-per-frame lesson). The unwidened-keycode fix (c) was already in the working tree and is being verified together with the uncommitted XKeycodeToKeysym two-level table change; this task did not re-review that change.
